Web Preview Text EN: Five installations that displace “the human” from any fixed ontological ground—framing it as a condition in constant becoming, rewritten across technological systems, perceptual structures and socio-material forces. Is humanity still a stable category or already something else?
Description EN:
Negotiated Realities brings together five interwoven installations that seek to displace “the human” from any fixed ontological position, as a provisional field continuously rewritten across technological systems, perceptual structures and socio-material infrastructures. Here, technology is not an external tool but a pervasive condition—invisibly redistributing how we perceive, behave and assign value.
The Neo-Urban Reef translates urban infrastructure into a mutable “data stratum”, entangling biological and technological logics within a generative system. Neural Negotiating treats the brain as a body that leaves material traces—brainwave activity rendered through light and woven fiber optics. Cupid Proxy stages intimate communication as a transactional service, exposing what is surrendered each time AI is permitted to speak in our place. C/Si exposes the tension between human augmentation and depletion. The Bias of Creation stages aesthetic judgment as a contested zone in human–machine co-creation.
Together, these works form a non-linear ecology in which visitors are embedded as dynamic variables—their actions captured, computed and fed back, generating shifting perceptual regimes and subtle distortions of reality.
Resonating with NEGOTIATING HUMANITY, the exhibition asks whether “humanity” remains a stable category, or has already become a continuously negotiated relational condition—emerging through the co-constitution of bodies, systems and environments.
Web Preview Text DE: Diese fünf Installationen hinterfragen “das Menschliche” als feste Kategorie und verstehen es stattdessen als einen Prozess des ständigen Werdens – geprägt von technologischen Systemen, Wahrnehmungsstrukturen und sozio-materiellen Beziehungen. Ist das Menschsein noch eine stabile Kategorie?
Description DE:
Negotiated Realities vereint fünf miteinander verwobene Installationen, die “das Menschliche” aus jeder festen ontologischen Position lösen und es als vorläufiges Feld begreifen, das fortlaufend durch technologische Systeme, Wahrnehmungsstrukturen und sozio-materielle Infrastrukturen neu geschrieben wird. Technologie erscheint dabei nicht als externes Werkzeug, sondern als allgegenwärtige Bedingung, die unmerklich darüber mitbestimmt, wie wir wahrnehmen, handeln und Werte zuschreiben.
The Neo-Urban Reef übersetzt städtische Infrastrukturen in eine veränderliche “Datenschicht” und verflechtet biologische und technologische Logiken innerhalb eines generativen Systems. Neural Negotiating versteht das Gehirn als einen Körper, der materielle Spuren hinterlässt – neuronale Aktivität wird hier in Licht und gewebte Glasfaserstrukturen übersetzt. Cupid Proxy inszeniert intime Kommunikation als transaktionalen Dienst und legt offen, was jedes Mal aufgegeben wird, wenn KI-Systemen erlaubt wird, für uns zu sprechen. C/Si verhandelt Spannung zwischen menschlicher Augmentation und Erschöpfung. The Bias of Creation inszeniert ästhetisches Urteilsvermögen als umkämpftes Feld in der Mensch-Maschine-Ko-Kreation.
Gemeinsam bilden diese Arbeiten eine nichtlineare Ökologie, in die Besucher*innen als dynamische Variablen eingebettet sind – ihre Handlungen werden erfasst, berechnet und rückgekoppelt und erzeugen so sich wandelnde Wahrnehmungsregime sowie subtile Verzerrungen der Realität.
In Anlehnung an NEGOTIATING HUMANITY fragt die Ausstellung, ob “Menschlichkeit” noch eine stabile Kategorie ist – oder längst zu einem fortwährend ausgehandelten relationalen Zustand geworden ist, der sich in der Ko-Konstitution von Körpern, Systemen und Umwelten entfaltet.

Web Preview Text EN: The Neo-Urban Reef is a permeable spatial lattice installation that conceptualizes the urban structure as a fluid, modular and digitally responsive “living system”. It investigates digital technology as a primary medium of negotiation between our biological heritage and evolving social “genes”.
Description EN: The Neo-Urban Reef is a permeable lattice structure conceptualizing the city as a fluid “living system”. Embedded screens surface data from Chinese urban life—consumer behavior, drone logistics, public spaces—treating each dataset as a social “gene” in mutation. Acting as a synthetic data reef, the installation envisions a near future where algorithmic code and human agency are inextricably intertwined, reshaping cognition behavior, and relation within the hybrid city.

Description EN:
As a species that has shaped the Earth, humans have transformed their environment like no other species before. With every new technology, our influence—and our responsibility for the future we are shaping—potentially grows.

The tour Homo Futuris explores questions such as: How is technology changing what it means to be human? How does it shape the way we live together? What visions of the future guide us? And what role do WE play in all of this?

To mark the 30th anniversary of the Ars Electronica Center, we’re looking both back and forward: The focus is on the new exhibitions opening as part of the Ars Electronica Festival. Together, we’ll explore visions of the future, current developments, and the big questions of an era in transition.

Web Preview Text EN: The Ars Electronica Center’s media façade is more than just a brightly lit surface. With a few tricks, it becomes a democratic tool—visible, public and customizable.
Description EN:
The Ars Electronica Center’s media façade is more than just a brightly lit surface. With a few tricks, it becomes a democratic tool—visible, public and customizable.

In this workshop, you will “hack” our digital canvas and turn your ideas into colorful pixels using microcontrollers and code. Instead of spray cans, you will use the façade’s LEDs to project your messages into the urban space. Algorithms become color, the glass becomes a canvas—and suddenly your thoughts shine: temporary, collaborative and impactful. The resulting creations can be viewed on the facade between 21:00–21:30.

Web Preview Text EN: This year’s collaboration with the Ars Electronica Festival is stronger than ever, with 30+ international universities coming together in the center of Linz in a bid to express and inspire. Inside the art university’s buildings, 80+ artworks by students and emerging artists await the public, spanning a diverse array of themes.
Description EN:
This year’s collaboration with the Ars Electronica Festival is stronger than ever, with 30+ international universities coming together in the center of Linz in a bid to express and inspire. At the very center of it all comes a public structure with many faces, a welcoming architecture that hosts art and people, a safe space for all to speak up and listen to the voices of the few and many. In this public intervention, watch out for activist collaborations, with performing partners such as Attac Austria, FIFTITU%, and Ars Electronica’s Flood the Zone with Courage. Inside the art university’s buildings, 80+ artworks by students and emerging artists await the public, spanning a diverse array of themes. This year´s festival theme suggests a future is coming, but at the University of Arts Linz and the Kunstuni Campus, we boldly ask: At what cost?

Isaac Asimov’s 1956 science fiction piece, The Last Question, is underlined by this precise question: What does the future hold for us? Can humans exist forever? And at what cost? His story explores humanity’s reliance on a galactic supercomputer, similar to that of an AI assistant today, to escape entropy: the inevitable end and the future of the universe. For trillions of years, humans have asked how to stop it, and the machine gives the same repeated response: “INSUFFICIENT DATA FOR MEANINGFUL ANSWER.” This standoff continues until the end of the dying universe, when the last of the advanced humans merge consciousness with the computer. The omni-being is then left alone in the void, existing purely to calculate the answer humanity always sought—at the cost of humanity itself. As the people in Asimov’s story, in times of need, we turn to technology, seeking solutions. Currently, people are outsourcing their creativity to Generative AI, hands-on learning has been replaced by instant gratification and exploring moral dilemmas has been reduced to simple automated outputs. Will AI find out the answers for our future? Or should we listen to the voices of the current? Instead of relying on machines for answers, the students, partners of the Kunstuni and the public take to Linz's Main Square to raise their voices in an active demonstration of community and artistic expression.
Algorithmic models may promise a uniform future, but the physical reality of our present is defined by disputes over world politics, power, history and culture. True progress will not materialize through the tidy promises of AI or the grim scenarios of science fiction. In contrast to Asimov’s story, where humanity achieves immortality by converging itself into a powerful machine, the artists and activists at Kunstuni remember that the future is built on human messiness, friction and diversity. This year’s exhibition serves as a counterpoint to tech-solutionism; it speaks to the future potential that lies not in cutting-edge solutions but in the collaborations of cultural voices. Supporting this amalgam of voices and ideas, a public structure in the Main Square accommodates that very solidarity. Bringing together dozens of nationalities, feminist perspectives via FIFTITU%, anti-war stances and resistance with Attac Austria, Ars Electronica invites the public to step away from neat algorithms and to “Flood the Zone with Courage”. Acting upon a cultural problem is messy, but diversity is what makes us beautiful. True beauty and answers are found in our collective willingness to speak, listen and act together in the present and locally, with our neighbors.
Constant change, as small and insignificant as it may seem, like tiny particles that vibrate, together become a conglomerate of bouldering movement. While the world presses on toward what the future may bring, it still undergoes disputes rooted in century-old fights over land and sea, resources and consumption, nature and pollution, diversity and division. Disputes so ugly that we would rather look away, pretend they are too far from us, pretend that time will take care of them, pretend that they are someone else’s responsibility. Yet, much like the ocean’s garbage patches that have formed their own synthetic ecosystems, these societal issues not only persist but constantly evolve. We must not see them as relics of the past, but as part of us: driving forces for the future, material we carry with us and defining factors of our culture. Once forgotten, they return again and again, like plastic waste thrown away, only to reappear as microplastics. Just as material is recycled, we must continually revisit these unresolved cultural disputes. True activism operates like constant recycling: a necessary, messy patchwork of collaboration where every individual voice counts. These friction-filled matters are the very material we must carry with us to actively shape our future.

This active reclamation of our present is incorporated in the very design language of the Kunstuni Campus exhibition. A raw, democratic landscape built not on algorithmic perfection, but on a beautiful, complicated mess. True collaboration is rarely easy; it requires us to navigate the friction of differing perspectives to construct a shared space. This year’s Ars Electronica Festival theme reminds us of our agency in the present. FUTURE BEGINS written in the present tense, suggests the future begins now, and not a destination we passively wait for. It is the continuous, conscious act of change itself. As Asimov's tale ends (and restarts), “Step by step, it must be done.”
Web Preview Text DE: Die diesjährige Zusammenarbeit mit dem Ars Electronica Festival ist intensiver denn je: Mehr als 30 internationale Hochschulen kommen im Zentrum von Linz zusammen, um drängenden Themen Ausdruck zu verleihen und neue Perspektiven zu eröffnen.
Description DE:
Die diesjährige Zusammenarbeit mit dem Ars Electronica Festival ist intensiver denn je: Mehr als 30 internationale Hochschulen kommen im Zentrum von Linz zusammen, um drängenden Themen Ausdruck zu verleihen und neue Perspektiven zu eröffnen. Im Mittelpunkt steht eine öffentliche Struktur mit vielen Gesichtern; eine einladende Architektur, die Kunst und Menschen beherbergt; ein sicherer Raum, in dem alle ihre Stimme erheben und den Stimmen der Wenigen wie der Vielen zuhören können. Die öffentliche Intervention fungiert als Plattform für aktivistische Kooperationen mit Partnern wie Attac Austria, FIFTITU% und dem Ars-Electronica-Projekt Flood the Zone with Courage. In den Gebäuden der Kunstuniversität erwarten die Besucher*innen mehr als 80 Werke von Studierenden und aufstrebenden Künstler*innen, die ein breites Spektrum an Themen behandeln. Das diesjährige Festivalthema deutet darauf hin, dass die Zukunft unmittelbar bevorsteht, doch an der Kunstuniversität Linz und auf dem Kunstuni Campus wird bewusst die Frage gestellt: Zu welchem Preis?

Diese Frage steht auch im Zentrum von Isaac Asimovs Science-Fiction-Erzählung The Last Question aus dem Jahr 1956: Was hält die Zukunft für uns bereit? Kann die Menschheit ewig bestehen? Und was nehmen wir dafür in Kauf? Die Geschichte schildert die Abhängigkeit der Menschheit von einem galaktischen Supercomputer – vergleichbar mit heutigen KI-Assistenten –, um der Entropie und damit dem unvermeidlichen Ende des Universums zu entkommen. Über Billionen von Jahren hinweg fragt die Menschheit, wie dieser Prozess aufgehalten werden kann, und die Maschine gibt immer wieder dieselbe Antwort: “DATEN UNZUREICHEND FÜR SINNVOLLE ANTWORT.” Diese Pattsituation dauert bis zum Ende des sterbenden Universums an, als die letzten hochentwickelten Menschen ihr Bewusstsein mit dem Computer verschmelzen. Die Superintelligenz bleibt schließlich allein im Nichts zurück und existiert nur noch, um die Antwort zu berechnen, nach der die Menschheit immer gesucht hat – um den Preis der Menschheit selbst. Wie die Menschen in Asimovs Geschichte wenden auch wir uns in Zeiten der Unsicherheit an die Technologie und suchen nach Lösungen. Gegenwärtig lagern viele Menschen ihre Kreativität an generative KI aus, praktisches Lernen wird durch sofortige Bedürfnisbefriedigung ersetzt, und die Auseinandersetzung mit moralischen Dilemmata wird auf automatisierte Outputs reduziert. Wird die KI die Antworten für unsere Zukunft finden? Oder sollten wir auf die Stimmen der Gegenwart hören? Anstatt sich bei der Suche nach Antworten auf Maschinen zu verlassen, begeben sich die Studierenden, Partnerorganisationen der Kunstuni und die Öffentlichkeit auf den Linzer Hauptplatz, um ihre Stimmen zu erheben – als aktive Demonstration von Gemeinschaft und künstlerischem Ausdruck.

Algorithmische Modelle mögen eine einheitliche Zukunft versprechen, doch die physische Realität unserer Gegenwart ist geprägt von Auseinandersetzungen um Weltpolitik, Macht, Geschichte und Kultur. Wahrer Fortschritt wird sich weder durch die gleichförmigen Versprechen der KI noch durch die düsteren Szenarien der Science-Fiction verwirklichen. Im Gegensatz zu Asimovs Geschichte, in der die Menschheit Unsterblichkeit durch die Verschmelzung mit einer Maschine erreicht, erinnern die Künstler*innen und Aktivist*innen der Kunstuniversität daran, dass die Zukunft auf menschlicher Unordnung, Reibung und Vielfalt aufbaut. Die diesjährige Ausstellung versteht sich als Gegenentwurf zum Techno-Solutionismus. Sie verweist auf ein Zukunftspotenzial, das nicht in immer neuen Lösungsansätzen liegt, sondern in der Zusammenarbeit kultureller Stimmen. Die öffentliche Installation auf dem Hauptplatz unterstützt dieses Konglomerat aus Stimmen und Ideen und verkörpert genau diese Solidarität. Ars Electronica bringt Dutzende von Nationalitäten, feministische Perspektiven durch FIFTITU%, Antikriegshaltungen und Widerstand mit Attac Austria zusammen und lädt die Öffentlichkeit ein, sich von den scheinbar sauberen Algorithmen zu lösen und stattdessen das Feld mit Mut zu fluten – “Flood the Zone with Courage”. Kulturelle Probleme aktiv anzugehen ist oft chaotisch, doch gerade die Vielfalt macht uns aus. Wahre Schönheit und tragfähige Antworten entstehen durch unsere kollektive Bereitschaft, in der Gegenwart und in unserer unmittelbaren Umgebung mit unseren Nachbar*innen zu sprechen, zuzuhören und zu handeln.

Ständiger Wandel, so klein und unbedeutend er zunächst erscheinen mag, gleicht winzigen Teilchen, die durch ihre Bewegung schließlich eine mächtige Dynamik erzeugen. Während die Welt auf das zusteuert, was die Zukunft bringen mag, ist sie weiterhin von Konflikten geprägt, die oft auf jahrhundertealten Auseinandersetzungen um Land und Meer, Ressourcen und Konsum, Natur und Umweltverschmutzung sowie Vielfalt und Spaltung beruhen. Konflikte, die so unangenehm sind, dass wir lieber wegschauen, sie für zu weit entfernt halten oder glauben, die Zeit werde sie lösen und so tun, als seien sie die Verantwortung anderer. Doch ähnlich wie die Müllstrudel in den Ozeanen, die längst eigene synthetische Ökosysteme gebildet haben, bestehen diese gesellschaftlichen Probleme nicht nur fort, sondern entwickeln sich ständig weiter. Wir dürfen sie nicht als Relikte der Vergangenheit betrachten, sondern als Teil von uns: als treibende Kräfte der Zukunft, als Material, das wir mit uns tragen, und als prägende Faktoren unserer Kultur. Werden sie verdrängt, kehren sie immer wieder zurück – wie Plastikmüll, der als Mikroplastik wieder auftaucht. So wie Materialien recycelt werden, müssen auch ungelöste gesellschaftliche Konflikte immer wieder neu betrachtet werden. Wahrer Aktivismus funktioniert wie ein fortlaufender Recyclingprozess: ein notwendiges, chaotisches Geflecht der Zusammenarbeit, in dem jede einzelne Stimme zählt. Gerade diese von Reibung geprägten Themen sind das Material, mit dem wir unsere Zukunft aktiv gestalten müssen.

Diese aktive Rückeroberung unserer Gegenwart spiegelt sich auch in der Designsprache der Ausstellung auf dem Kunstuni Campus. Eine rohe, demokratische Landschaft, die nicht auf algorithmischer Perfektion, sondern auf einem schönen und komplexen Durcheinander aufgebaut ist. Wahre Zusammenarbeit ist selten einfach; sie erfordert, dass wir die Reibungen unterschiedlicher Perspektiven meistern und einen geteilten Raum schaffen. Das diesjährige Thema des Ars Electronica Festival erinnert uns an unsere Handlungsfähigkeit in der Gegenwart. FUTURE BEGINS, bewusst im Präsens formuliert, macht deutlich, dass die Zukunft jetzt beginnt und kein fernes Ziel darstellt, auf das wir lediglich passiv warten. Zukunft ist der fortlaufende, bewusste Akt der Veränderung selbst. Und wie Asimovs Geschichte endet – und zugleich neu beginnt – gilt auch hier: “Es muss Schritt für Schritt getan werden.”

Web Preview Text EN: Classical craft education is one of the oldest disciplines at the University of Arts. Since 2016, the Design: Technology. Textile course has not only combined content from the former subjects of Technical Crafts and Textile Crafts, but has also expanded these to include current digital production techniques.
Description EN:
Classical craft education is one of the oldest disciplines at the University of Arts. Since 2016, the Design: Technology. Textile course has not only combined content from the former subjects of Technical Crafts and Textile Crafts, but has also expanded these to include current digital production techniques.

This new field of study focuses on the perception of living environments and the question of materials, processes and/or objects that influence and determine our surroundings as well as our own creative, knowledgeable actions and active participation in shaping the environment. Material culture is explored in its manifestations, functions and meanings in an interdisciplinary, action-oriented manner and through active engagement—inventing, constructing and artistically designing.

Web Preview Text EN: The Fine Arts program at the University of Arts Linz equips students with a diverse set of skills to work as freelance artists on both national and international levels.
Description EN: The Fine Arts program at the University of Arts Linz equips students with a diverse set of skills to work as freelance artists on both national and international levels. It fosters conceptual skills by helping students recognize when and where artistic action is needed. Practical expertise is developed through focused work in Painting & Graphic Art, Sculpture—Transmedial Space and Experimental Design. Theoretical competence is cultivated through engagement with academic theory as a source of inspiration, a tool for research and critical reflection and a means of developing strong argumentation skills. In addition, the program emphasizes organizational and professional techniques, including entrepreneurial thinking and communication skills essential for self-organization and sustainable artistic practice.

Description EN: The Industrial Design department focuses on developing innovative, serial products and systems at the intersection of people, technology and society. As both creative specialists and interdisciplinary generalists, our designers shape the future by driving strategic, user-oriented value. With a strong emphasis on digitalization, networking and technology integration, we prepare you to lead next-generation product innovations.

Web Preview Text EN: This year’s exhibition arises from a moment marked by acceleration, fragmented attention, the constant production of information and the endless triggering of emotional responses.
Description EN:
This year’s exhibition arises from a moment marked by acceleration, fragmented attention, the constant production of information and the endless triggering of emotional responses. In a time increasingly shaped by mediated realities and distant forms of conflict, we are compelled to ask: who constructs the narratives through which we perceive the world, and what forms can still create shared meaning? While information expands through endless accumulation, stories and rituals establish moments of temporary closure, rendering time inhabitable and creating structures of attention, repetition, and resonance through which new imaginaries and unexpected forms of coexistence unfold.

Interface Cultures students do not simply present works, but their own personal systems and situations that operate as new forms of code and ritual. Through new materialities that move within and beyond the screen, they activate new spaces of encounter, friction and collective imagination. Their projects have become environments for trial and error, for productive misuse, for getting into trouble together, but also for practising care and play. Rather than presenting finished statements, Codes [ ] Rituals should be understood as a celebration of process itself—a temporary suspension of productivity before the projects begin their life beyond the exhibition space.

Web Preview Text EN: Postdigital Lutherie reconnects the various aspects of acoustic, electronic and digital design of musical instruments within tangible sonic artifacts designed for musical expression.
Description EN: The design of musical instruments looks back on a long cultural and artistic tradition throughout the millennia. With the development of electronic music inthe last century, a radical paradigmatic shift has occurred, which has accelerated in recent decades through further advances in digitalization of music and the accompanying virtualization of instruments. Postdigital Lutherie intends to reflect these developments by reconnecting the various aspects of acoustic, electronic and digital design of musical instruments by means of tangible sonic artifacts designed for musical expression. This opens new design perspectives and artistic possibilities for established cultural techniques and musical practices, all set within in the context of ongoing digitalization.

Web Preview Text EN: The spectrum of use in the Master’s program ranges from an innovative-experimental approach to the appropriation of traditional ceramic techniques in order to realize artistic projects that reference a specific tradition.
Description EN: In recent years, ceramics has become a much-discussed material in the visual arts. Just a few years ago, the roots of ceramics in design, arts and crafts and the field of hobby pottery were viewed critically, denying it the opportunity to establish itself as a material of fine art. Today, the attitude has almost reversed. Precisely because ceramics has such a rich tradition and has an impact on so many areas of life, it has become a sought-after material for internationally renowned artists. The spectrum of use in the Master’s program ranges from an innovative-experimental approach to the appropriation of traditional ceramic techniques in order to realize artistic projects that reference  a specific tradition.

Web Preview Text EN: The program Textile Art and Design explores a wide range of textile techniques, material science and project-based artistic processes, fostering experimental approaches in the development of a personal design language.
Description EN: The program Textile Art and Design explores a wide range of textile techniques, material science and project-based artistic processes, fostering experimental approaches in the development of a personal design language. The integration of textile methods, craftsmanship, surface and spatial design, along with the conceptualization of design projects, support the formation of a strong, creative and artistic practice.

Web Preview Text EN: The Time-Based and Interactive Media program offers students a professional approach to the theory, techniques and design of digital media, combining two complementary focus areas: time-based media and interactive arts.
Description EN: The Time-Based and Interactive Media program offers students a professional approach to the theory, techniques and design of digital media, combining two complementary focus areas: time-based media and interactive arts.

Web Preview Text EN: The Time-based Media program positions itself within an interdisciplinary exploration of various approaches to working with time-based media—including video (both practice and theory), film (theory), sound, media installations and productions, interactive systems, digital media design and innovative programming.
Description EN:
The Time-based Media program positions itself within an interdisciplinary exploration of various approaches to working with time-based media—including video (both practice and theory), film (theory), sound, media installations and productions, interactive systems, digital media design and innovative programming.
Students develop their own artistic, scholarly and transdisciplinary projects. Experimental, performative, spatial, cultural studies and art-historical perspectives are integrated into both project development and theoretical training in time-based media, media practice and media production.

Web Preview Text EN: The Department of Visual Communication understands images not as illustrations of already-formed ideas, but as an independent mode of knowledge—asking what images actually show, what they draw from and what they make visible or conceal.
Description EN: The Department of Visual Communication understands images not as illustrations of already-formed ideas, but as an independent mode of knowledge. Students move between craft practice, experimental design and conceptual research—working where design meets science, music, activism and the public. From this position, research emerges that interrogates the conditions of seeing itself—what images show, what they draw from, what they make visible or conceal. The works shown this year are an expression of that.

Web Preview Text EN: Neural Negotiating explores how fleeting neural responses to taste can become a material presence. Visitors encounter a taste stimulus while wearing an OpenBCI EEG cap, allowing real-time brain activity to animate a multi-layer fiber-optic embroidered sculpture.
Description EN: Neural Negotiating explores how fleeting neural responses to taste can become a material presence. Visitors encounter a taste stimulus while wearing an OpenBCI EEG cap, allowing real-time brain activity to animate a multi-layer fiber-optic embroidered sculpture. Color, brightness, rhythm and depth emerge from EEG signals, forming a luminous neural cloud. Rather than visualizing brain data, the work materializes a temporary trace of perception—an experience that normally remains invisible.

Web Preview Text EN: The Crafting Futures Lab presents an exhibition-in-progress where making becomes collective research. Starting with material—its grain, resistance, memory—we follow the stories embedded in fibers, dust, tools and hands.
Description EN: The Crafting Futures Lab presents an exhibition-in-progress where collective making becomes a method of research. We follow material and the stories embedded in its fibers, dust and tools. Through workshops, conversational settings, rituals and responsive matter, we explore, collect and exchange. We weave notes, fragments and failures back into the exhibition as an archive growing day by day. Join us in crafting knowledge across disciplines and generations: collaborative, messy and maybe unexpected.

Description EN: A reprogrammed robotic cat, a projected body and Arduino-controlled displays create a distributed system of perception and response. The installation examines posthuman embodiment, hauntological memory and human–machine coexistence through a fragile choreography of projection, technical interfaces and affective automation.

Web Preview Text EN: Stone Butch Blues fuses techno beats with readings of excerpts from Leslie Feinberg’s eponymous novel, which powerfully explores the lived experiences of transgender individuals.
Description EN: Stone Butch Blues fuses techno beats with readings of excerpts from Leslie Feinberg’s eponymous novel, which powerfully explores the lived experiences of transgender individuals. It touches on themes of transphobia, resistance and the longing for a world beyond oppression. The work opens a space for escapism—a dreamlike vision of freedom, acceptance and belonging. It evokes the fragile hope and courage of those who dream of a world in which they can finally breathe, live and be truly free.

Web Preview Text EN: mental teratoma aims at embodying the elusive feeling of loneliness. It feels like a second skin that wraps tightly, a grip one wants to break free from, but cannot.
Description EN: mental teratoma aims at embodying the elusive feeling of loneliness. It feels like a second skin that wraps tightly, a grip one wants to break free from, but cannot. At the same time it only exists on the inside, steadily but silently growing bigger until it becomes indistinguishable from oneself. Social interactions rarely make it disappear, they often even intensify it. This breeds the paradox of wanting to escape loneliness by getting rid of social neediness altogether.

Web Preview Text EN: The Command of Origin is an experimental film centered on a particle universe that appears to generate its own order. Through particle movement, individuality, collectivity and larger systems gradually emerge.
Description EN: The Command of Origin is an experimental film centered on a particle universe that appears to generate its own order. Through particle movement, individuality, collectivity and larger systems gradually emerge. Yet this autonomy is shaped by heart rate data translated into visual parameters. A persistent cursor interrupts the illusion of a closed narrative, revealing the invisible structures governing the system and the reciprocal relationship between the individual and control system.

Web Preview Text EN: Can painting still create presence within systems built around speed, personalization and constant visual flow? This installation creates an interactive, fluid space by bringing painting into an environment shaped and affected by interactive user behavior.
Description EN: Can painting still create presence within systems built around speed, personalization and constant visual flow? What changes when a medium traditionally experienced in physical space enters the logic of screens and digital interfaces? This installation creates an interactive, fluid space by bringing painting into an environment shaped and affected by interactive user behavior.

Web Preview Text EN: Retinal Noise is a single channel audiovisual work exploring unstable perception through intermittent photographic flashes, darkness and electronic sound.
Description EN: Retinal Noise is a single channel audiovisual work exploring unstable perception through intermittent photographic flashes, darkness and electronic sound. The work stages the body as a fragmented and uncertain presence, oscillating between visibility and disappearance. Through sensory interruption and perceptual tension, the installation examines the limits of recognition, embodiment and spatial orientation.

Subtitle EN: Collection of Traces: [Photographic Casting 001 (La Friche, 13003 Marseille)]
Web Preview Text EN: Through repeated engagement with a single form, a practice emerges that is both media-analytical and existential. Traces—overlooked, seemingly meaningless—are imbued with time, history and reality.
Description EN: Through repeated engagement with a single form, a practice emerges that is both media-analytical and existential. Traces—overlooked, seemingly meaningless—are imbued with time, history and reality. Photography not as a representation, but as an imprint. A serial display shows the path: from trace to form, from cast to image. Through the repetition and variation of the same small trace, an appreciative attitude develops toward the environment, time and everyday life.

Web Preview Text EN: A 360° image slips off the screen and becomes a space to enter. The work is based on a long-exposure recording of the folk dance Ausseer Steirischer, in which movements appear as traces of light.
Description EN: A 360° image slips off the screen and becomes a space to enter. The work is based on a long-exposure recording of the folk dance Ausseer Steirischer, in which movements appear as traces of light. Instead of music, the sound focuses on the rhythm of the dancers’ steps. The work shows how cultural practices are not only recorded through technology, but also transformed: simplified, broken apart and reassembled in new ways.

Web Preview Text EN: This project is an ecocritical exploration of the rapid evolution of technology, questioning the role of photography today in the Anthropocene era, where AI is rapidly expanding.
Description EN: This project is an ecocritical exploration of the rapid evolution of technology, questioning the role of photography today in the Anthropocene era, where AI is rapidly expanding. Three frames compose this conceptual, futuristic tree. I draw inspiration from the patterns carved into bark by bark beetles, insects harmful to trees. Their designs resemble our electronic sheet networks.  To dig these images imitates the extractivism inherent in the creation of technological objects and data centers.

Name EN: Glitch & Leak: Overflowing Bodies in Public Space
Name DE: Glitch & Leak: Überfließende Körper im öffentlichen Raum
Artists: FIFTITU% Vernetzungsstelle für Frauen* in Kunst und Kultur in OÖ (AT)
Web Preview Text EN: Glitch & Leak is an invitation to open up a space together: a space of disruption, permeability, collective imagination and transformation. It uses disruption and leakage to collectively imagine how public space could be transformed.
Description EN:
Glitch & Leak is an invitation to open up a space together: a space of disruption, permeability, collective imagination and transformation. The glitch is not an error in the system, but a strategy of resistance—a way of interrupting established patterns and creating openings for other possibilities.
These patterns are also embedded in public space. Public space is never neutral. It is shaped by social, political and economic power relations, which determine who can access it, how it can be used and whose presence is welcomed or excluded. Glitch & Leak uses disruption and leakage as ways to make these structures visible, to unsettle them and to collectively imagine how public space could be transformed.
Web Preview Text DE: Glitch & Leak ist eine Einladung, gemeinsam einen Raum zu öffnen: einen Raum der Störung, der Durchlässigkeit, der kollektiven Imagination und der Transformation.
Description DE:
Glitch & Leak ist eine Einladung, gemeinsam einen Raum zu öffnen: einen Raum der Störung, der Durchlässigkeit, der kollektiven Imagination und der Transformation. Der Glitch ist kein Fehler im System, sondern eine Strategie des Widerstands – er unterbricht etablierte Muster und schafft Öffnungen für anderes.
Diese Muster sind auch dem öffentlichen Raum eingeschrieben. Öffentlicher Raum ist nie neutral. Er wird von gesellschaftlichen, politischen und ökonomischen Machtverhältnissen geformt, die bestimmen, wer Zugang hat, wie er genutzt werden kann und wessen Anwesenheit willkommen ist und wessen ausgeschlossen wird. Glitch & Leak arbeitet mit Störung und Durchsickern, um diese Strukturen sichtbar zu machen, sie zu irritieren und gemeinsam zu entwerfen, wie öffentlicher Raum verändert werden könnte.

Subtitle EN: What happens when courage is not just discussed, but tested live?
Web Preview Text EN: DorfTV – Radical Broadcast transforms the Kunstuni Campus into an experimental television zone somewhere between loss of control, improvisation and grandeur.
Description EN:
DorfTV – Radical Broadcast transforms the Kunstuni Campus into an experimental television zone somewhere between loss of control, improvisation and grandeur. Under this motto, a show emerges that dares to evolve while it is happening: wild live broadcasts, risky decisions, technical experiments and interactions with visitors and artists who are either courageous—or simply careless.
A specially appointed jury evaluates everything in real time: Who is acting bravely? Who is completely overestimating themselves? And at what point does courage turn into chaos?
The control room itself becomes part of the experiment. New technical setups, spontaneous image changes, unpredictable situations and the conscious abandonment of safe routines turn the production itself into a test of courage. DorfTV – Radical Broadcast is not a perfect television show. It is an attempt to stay loud despite uncertainty, to make risks visible and to collectively discover what happens when people dare.

Web Preview Text EN: Sound Campus – Listening Underground, explores the movement beneath the surface. It considers the ongoing, divergent processes which are felt but not always seen. To submerge opens up new modes of attention and multi-sensory listening that change our relation with the surrounding.
Description EN:
This year’s edition of Sound Campus proposes a music program inspired in intersectional spaces created by sound. Taking the notion of “underground” as a shared continuum, it invites artists and audience to a collective listening experience.
Sound Campus – Listening Underground explores the movement beneath the surface. It considers the ongoing, divergent processes which are felt but not always seen. To submerge opens up new modes of attention and multi-sensory listening that change our relation with our surroundings.
The conditions for immersion allow space for vulnerability, equal self-expression and freeform.
Regarding spacetime as a stream of gradual transitions provides an image where the individual parts are not dis-articulated from each other, but coexist in mutual affection. 
Sound Campus is a sound festival within Ars Electronica and Kunstuniversität Linz. Since 2020, it has been a format hosted by the Kunstuniversität Linz, providing an opportunity for students and performers to exchange and share their work with a wider audience. With a focus on its community, the program is committed to supporting diverse voices in experimental and electronic music.
Web Preview Text DE: Sound Campus – Listening Underground erkundet Bewegungen unter der Oberfläche. Im Fokus stehen fortlaufende, divergierende Prozesse, die spürbar, aber nicht immer sichtbar sind. Das Eintauchen eröffnet neue Formen der Aufmerksamkeit und des multisensorischen Hörens, die unser Verhältnis zur Umgebung verändern.
Description DE:
Die diesjährige Ausgabe von Sound Campus präsentiert ein Musikprogramm, das von den intersektionalen Räumen inspiriert ist, die durch Klang entstehen. Ausgehend von der Vorstellung des “Underground” als gemeinsamem Kontinuum lädt sie Künstler*innen und Publikum zu einer kollektiven Hörerfahrung ein.
Sound Campus – Listening Underground erkundet Bewegungen unter der Oberfläche. Im Fokus stehen fortlaufende, divergierende Prozesse, die spürbar, aber nicht immer sichtbar sind. Das Eintauchen eröffnet neue Formen der Aufmerksamkeit und des multisensorischen Hörens, die unser Verhältnis zur Umgebung verändern. 
Die Bedingungen des Eintauchens schaffen Raum für Verletzlichkeit, gleichberechtigten Selbstausdruck und Freiform. 
Raumzeit als einen Strom allmählicher Übergänge zu begreifen, eröffnet eine Perspektive, in der die einzelnen Teile nicht voneinander losgelöst sind, sondern koexistieren und wechselseitig aufeinander einwirken.
Sound Campus ist ein Soundfestival, das während des Ars Electronica Festivals stattfindet. Seit 2020 wird das Format von der Kunstuniversität Linz veranstaltet und bietet Studierenden und Performer*innen die Möglichkeit, sich auszutauschen und ihre Arbeiten einem breiteren Publikum zu präsentieren. Mit einem besonderen Fokus auf seine Community setzt sich das Programm dafür ein, vielfältige Stimmen in experimenteller und elektronischer Musik zu fördern.

Web Preview Text EN: With the Democracy Zone, Attac creates a space where civil society and social movements come together to challenge the dominant economic system. The interplay of art and activism comes to life through Flood the Zone with Courage: public space is reclaimed and transformed as a site of resistance, revealing democratic alternatives.
Description EN:
With the Democracy Zone, Attac creates a space where civil society and social movements come together to challenge the dominant economic system. At its core is the unchecked power of large corporations that profit from crises and wars while social and ecological justice are pushed aside. The interplay of art and activism comes to life through Flood the Zone with Courage: public space is reclaimed and transformed as a site of resistance, revealing democratic alternatives.

For five days, Attac, together with artists, activists and experts, will animate the city’s Main Square. Through a diverse and interactive program of workshops and performances, the Democracy Zone demonstrates that the democratization of society is not an abstract idea but a collective practice—especially at a time when authoritarian forces are gaining ground.

The Democracy Zone is both a call to action and a space for learning. Whether through performative games taking on Elon Musk & Co., feminist drumming against oppression, banner-making or participatory workshops exposing the profiteers of war and crisis, it creates opportunities to exchange ideas, deepen understanding and build resistance. In dialogue with artists Attac explores the emancipatory potential of universal basic income and raises the question of who should own and control AI infrastructure.

Open to everyone, the Democracy Zone welcomes ideas, uncertainties and diverse perspectives. Together, participants reflect on the kind of world they want to live in.

Each workshop opens with OXID, a sound miniature by artist and activist Aaron Maria Steiner.

Das Zusammenspiel von Kunst und Aktivismus wird mit Flood the Zone with Courage greifbar: Der öffentliche Raum wird angeeignet um demokratische Alternativen sichtbar zu machen.
Description DE:
Mit der Demokratiezone schafft Attac eine Schnittstelle zwischen Zivilgesellschaft und sozialer Bewegung, die das herrschende Wirtschaftssystem hinterfragt. Im Fokus steht die unkontrollierte Macht großer Konzerne, die von Krisen und Kriegen profitieren, während soziale und ökologische Gerechtigkeit auf der Strecke bleiben. Das Zusammenspiel von Kunst und Aktivismus wird mit Flood the Zone with Courage greifbar: Der öffentliche Raum wird angeeignet und gestaltet, um Widerstand zu leisten und demokratische Alternativen sichtbar zu machen.

Fünf Tage lang bespielt Attac mit Künstler*innen, Aktivist*innen und Expert*innen den Hauptplatz. Ein breites, interaktives Workshop- und Performanceprogramm zeigt: Die Demokratisierung gesellschaftlicher Verhältnisse ist kein abstraktes Konzept, sondern lässt sich gemeinsam gestalten – gerade in Zeiten, in denen autoritäre Kräfte an Macht gewinnen.

Die Demokratiezone ist Aufruf und Lernraum zugleich. Ob im performativen Spiel gegen Elon Musk & Co., beim feministischen Trommeln gegen Unterdrückung, beim Bannermalen oder in partizipativen Workshops, die Kriegs- und Krisenprofiteure sichtbar machen: Es entstehen Räume zum Austauschen, Verstehen und Widerstehen. Im Austausch mit Künstler*innen geht es um die emanzipativen Chancen eines Grundeinkommens und um die Frage, wem die KI-Infrastruktur eigentlich gehört.

Offen für alle – Ideen, Unsicherheiten und verschiedene Meinungen sind willkommen: Gemeinsam überlegen die Teilnehmenden, in welcher Welt sie leben möchten.

Den Beginn der Workshops markiert jeweils die Klangminiatur OXID des Künstlers und Aktivisten Aaron Maria Steiner.

Description EN:
Leonardo LASER is an international program that brings together artists, scientists, academics and the public to share their work and inspire one another through presentations, performances and discussions.

Our recurring LASER series, Lab Songs, explores evolving cultures of experimentation. Scientific and artistic breakthroughs arise not only from discoveries, but from transformations in practices, methodologies and systems of care. As a result, laboratories are increasingly reimagined as spaces where aesthetic, technological, ecological and theoretical forms of knowledge come into proximity.

For this year’s Sobremesas, we gather around the dining table as a site of encounter. Much like the laboratory, it is a place where experiences are shared, differences remain present and knowledge is collectively digested. Join us in celebrating the conversations, relationships and acts of care through which new understandings emerge and unexpected encounters unfold.

Description EN: When does a recipe become your own? Kochlust is a haptic companion exploring culinary authorship. It bridges digital speech recognition with analog archiving. Users can narrate their cooking achievements into the voice-controlled device, which instantly materializes the words into a physical recipe. By showcasing personal cooking success, the project aims to boost confidence in one's own cooking skills, transforming volatile digital content into a tangible collection of one's own recipes.

Description EN: This project focuses on the perception and memory of matter, using media-archaeological techniques that release captured information as sound waves from scratches. Description EN: Phobos is an interactive installation that mimics inner dialogues, raising questions that challenge certainties and invite reflection. Named after the Greek personification of fear, Phobos stems from the roots of contemporary fears, uncertainties and anxieties born of conflict and war. It is built as a reflective conversational layer on top of an inverted version of the knowledge-generating combinatorial system "Ars magna generalis ultima", created by Ramon Llull in the 13th century.

Description EN: You are invited to leave the singular human perspective behind. You are stepping into a shared reality where the edges of your own body seem to dissolve. The installation does not tell you what to see or how to feel. Instead, it offers a threshold. It is a place where the gap between species and machine is finally bridged, if only for a short time. The goal is for you to carry the memory of that hybrid state with you.

Description EN: in/affection is a performance and interactive sound installation that translates the bioelectrical activity of living molds into sound. Different species are cultivated under varying conditions and connected to a self-developed synthesizer. Fluctuations in electrical resistance are transformed in real time into evolving sonic structures. The audience interacts physically by touching cables, thereby becoming participants in a shared sonic ecosystem. How does coexistence sound when non-human life is given a voice?

Description EN: Spectral Roots is an interactive installation linking 19th-century and contemporary extraction. A projected tree morphs into cables and mineral crystals, referencing Palaquium gutta, a nearly extinct tree first extracted under colonial rule to insulate the earliest submarine telegraph cables and now used for the rare minerals powering today’s devices. Wireless signals from devices in the surrounding space pass through the piece, reshaping transitions and revealing that the invisible is anchored to matter extracted from the earth.

Description EN: BioCore is a kinetic sculpture that bridges the living and the machine. This soft, robotic sculpture features an artificial core wrapped in living vegetation, blending nature with technology. Instead of relying on cold data, it is brought to life by the visitor’s body heat, thereby accelerating its biological decay. By highlighting the fragility of both biological and artificial existence, it serves as a reflection on the temporal nature of life and the short-lived cycle of our technology.

Description EN: Vocal Duets is shaped around contemporary conflicts between languages and countries, conflicts that take the form of war. While language is generally assumed to be a means of closeness, intimacy and communication, these duets use the irony of the situation to revive the lost intimacy and peace between the neighboring alphabets of Russian-Ukrainian, Hebrew-Farsi and Hebrew-Arabic.

Description EN: Composition continues the Cycle of Emotions series (G.MAP Gwangju, South Korea, 2026). Here, as opposed to just information, emotion data becomes an abstract painting, and one user’s color becomes part of the next viewer’s composition.

Subtitle EN: How financial systems profit from war
Web Preview Text EN: At Least I’m Making Money is an interactive installation about how money, power and the arms industry uphold modern war.
Description EN: At Least I'm Making Money is an interactive installation about how money, power and the arms industry uphold modern war. War is usually framed as a conflict between nations, such as the US vs Iran, Russia vs Ukraine or Israel vs Palestine, but this can hide other dimensions. For instance, war is also a financial event. These layers are often so abstract that we forget how they sustain modern war and geopolitical conflict. As systems collapse, the cost is counted in numbers, never in terms of the people paying for it.

Web Preview Text EN: Into the air is a technological and sound installation by m22. Infrasound and seismic waves generated by military explosions disrupt avian magnetoreception, causing birds to abandon their habitat.
Description EN:
Birds leave the places where the war is sounding.

Infrasound and seismic waves generated by weapon detonations and explosions disrupt avian spatial orientation, magnetoreception, alter nesting patterns, migration routes and trigger hyperresponsive stress reactions that mirror PTSD-like symptoms observed in combat veterans. These same waves could provide acoustic evidence of ongoing war: in 2023, the researchers from NORSAR developed a methodology to identify air strikes in Ukraine in near-real time, using infrasound and seismic data.

m22 (Vlada Oleinik & Nail Gainulla) connects these two forces within a single technological installation: three antenna structures, reminiscent of the objects birds use to perch on, linked by cables that translate the data from a monitoring station in Northern Ukraine into audible and visible vibrations. A small LCD screen on the switch box displays the exact time, date and location of each registered strike.

Description EN: A participatory kinetic sculpture driven by global conflict data. As violence escalates, structural support is continuously withdrawn, causing the sculpture to collapse. Only the physical intervention of passing strangers can restore and sustain it. The work proposes shared maintenance over automated mediation, suggesting that a common world is sustained through the continuous collective care of strangers.

Web Preview Text EN: By the Time We Looked is an archival installation and live audiovisual performance developed through research into the Standard Model, the Higgs boson and reconstruction methodologies at CERN.
Description EN: By the Time We Looked is an archival installation and live audiovisual performance developed through research into the Standard Model, the Higgs boson and reconstruction methodologies at CERN. This piece approaches reconstruction as a condition through which we access reality. In particle physics, collisions are never directly observed but are reconstructed from traces and delayed signals, providing access to both the event and the underlying structures that describe microscopic interactions.

Description EN: Who Speaks for Me explores how algorithms claim authority over human emotion. Using live heartbeat data, the installation generates machine-assigned emotional labels that reshape a participant’s digital facial double in real time. Description EN: Residual Time: Smoke is the first time-based media work from Trace-driven Computational Painting. Through frame sampling and motion translation, drifting smoke becomes marks, stains, shadows and layers, compressing a vanishing movement into a computational painting surface.

While the rotating image shows a hypnotizing landscape, viewers have to pedal in order to catch a glimpse of ground.

The project investigates how touch and sound shape memory, movement and relationships, creating new ways of sensing and remembering.

Web Preview Text EN: HEAR SAY (HÖREN SAGEN) asks a fundamental question: What does a machine make of what it hears—and who determines what it makes?
Description EN: HEAR SAY (HÖREN SAGEN) asks a fundamental question: What does a machine make of what it hears—and who determines what it makes? It operates within a framework shaped by humans: training data, parameters, assumptions and interests. We only see the output as an image. The project follows a core principle of Co.Lab Beta Now: treating aesthetic experience as a tool for inquiry. What emerges when we watch a machine interpret our language—and hold its reading in our hands?
Credits long: Co.Lab Beta Now investigates what happens when something fleeting—a word, a gesture, a sentence—is translated into material form, and what role the translating tool plays in that process. A person speaks and receives an image. A machine listens and renders what it hears visually: rhythm, tone, emotional texture, modes of thought. The result is printed and taken home.

Artists: Anna Steward (DE), Sebastian Gfellner (AT), Hannes Buchwieser (DE)
Web Preview Text EN: A 45-minute open-format performance. A performer outside. A scientist inside. What opens up the space between them? Signs, gestures and materials drift across the field.
Description EN:
A 45-minute open-format performance. A performer outside. A scientist inside. What opens up the space between them? Signs, gestures and materials drift across the field. Separated by the BioLab, an enclosed laboratory space connected through tubes and tools, they carry out a ritualized workflow: microbial probes are prepared, biopolymers produced and microbial explorers placed into cryogenic hibernation. 

At the center, a concealed arkship—a vessel for microbial astronauts—is gradually revealed and readied for launch. Set up to reach the unknown and initiate a “molecular handshake” with microbial extraterrestrial siblings. Framed by science fiction and rooted in astrobiology, the BioQuantum Record asks: What if we sent life itself instead of a message into space? You can enter or exit the frame at any time. The performance stages astrobiology not as a distant discipline, but as a material, performative and narrative practice—a porous space between art and science, self and other, the Earth and the unknown. 

This special edition is presented at the Ars Electronica Festival 2026. Earlier stages: https://ars.electronica.art/center/en/arcreactor/ research residency at the Ars Electronica Center’s BioLab and https://ars.electronica.art/center/en/events/long-night-of-research-2026/ workshop during the Long Night of Research 2026.
Web Preview Text DE: Eine 45-minütige Performance im offenen Format. Eine Performerin draußen. Ein Wissenschaftler drinnen. Was entsteht im Raum zwischen ihnen? Zeichen, Gesten und Materialien zirkulieren zwischen den beiden.
Description DE:
Eine 45-minütige Performance im offenen Format. Eine Performerin draußen. Ein Wissenschaftler drinnen. Was entsteht im Raum zwischen ihnen? Zeichen, Gesten und Materialien zirkulieren zwischen den beiden. Getrennt durch das BioLab, einem abgeschlossenen Laborraum, doch verbunden durch Schläuche und Werkzeuge, führen sie einen ritualisierten Arbeitsablauf durch: mikrobielle Proben werden vorbereitet, Biopolymere hergestellt und mikrobielle Entdecker in kryogenen Schlaf versetzt.   

Im Zentrum wird nach und nach ein verhülltes Arkship – ein Gefäß für mikrobielle Astronauten – enthüllt und für den Start vorbereitet: Eine Mission ins Unbekannte, um einen “molekularen Handschlag“ mit mikrobiellen extraterrestrischen Geschwistern zu initiieren. Zwischen Science-Fiction und Astrobiologie stellt BioQuantum Record die Frage: Was wäre, wenn wir statt einer Botschaft das Leben selbst ins All schicken würden? Das Publikum kann jederzeit kommen und gehen. Die Performance inszeniert Astrobiologie nicht als abstrakte Disziplin, sondern als materielle, performative und narrative Praxis – einen porösen Raum zwischen Kunst und Wissenschaft, Selbst und Anderem, der Erde und dem Unbekannten.   

Diese Special Edition wird auf dem Ars Electronica Festival 2026 präsentiert. Frühere Stationen: Research Residency https://ars.electronica.art/center/de/arcreactor/ im BioLab des Ars Electronica Centers und Workshop https://ars.electronica.art/center/de/events/lange-nacht-forschung-2026/ während der Langen Nacht der Forschung 2026.

Web Preview Text EN: House of Negotiated Selves is an interactive installation where an AI mirrors visitors, then warps their reflection. What begins as presence becomes substitution, exploring how human agency slips through the negotiation between the embodied self and its artificial echo.
Description EN:
House of Negotiated Selves explores the line between human autonomy and machine representation. With AI becoming increasingly prevalent in mediating and shaping our interactions, creation and decision-making, an ongoing negotiation is taking place.

In response to the 2026 theme of NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS, House of Negotiated Selves frames this negotiation as an embodied experience. Through the metaphor of the fun-house's distorted mirrors, the reflections of ourselves appear similar but ultimately deceive us. The installation asks when our reflection becomes substitution, and when the machine begins to speak for us.

Visitors step into a world where their presence is sensed and interpreted. Initially, the system seems to be a mirror of their true selves and presence. Gradually, the reflection starts to wander, predicting, distorting and misrepresenting the visitor. What begins as recognition becomes ambiguity and displacement. Rather than fixing a single form of distortion, the work allows it to emerge, exposing the visitor to the unsettling experience of representation that no longer belongs to them.

House of Negotiated Selves explores AI-mediated representation and the erosion of human agency. Placed at the intersection of interaction design, critical AI studies and sensory art, this project translates an abstract discussion into a tangible experience, one that is not about what AI is but rather how it starts representing us, whether we agree to it or not.
Web Preview Text DE: House of Negotiated Selves ist eine interaktive Installation, in der eine KI die Besucher*innen zunächst spiegelt und ihr Abbild anschließend verändert. Die Arbeit untersucht, wie sich menschliche Agency in der Aushandlung zwischen dem verkörperten Selbst und seinem künstlichen Echo verschiebt.
Description DE:
House of Negotiated Selves untersucht die Grenze zwischen menschlicher Autonomie und maschineller Repräsentation. Da KI zunehmend unsere Interaktionen, kreativen Prozesse und Entscheidungen vermittelt und mitgestaltet, findet fortwährend ein Aushandlungsprozess statt.

Als Reaktion auf das diesjährige Thema NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS  macht House of Negotiated Selves diese Verhandlung körperliche erfahrbar. Mithilfe der Metapher verzerrter Spiegel eines Spiegelkabinetts erscheinen unsere Abbilder vertraut, führen uns jedoch letztlich in die Irre. Die Installation stellt die Frage, wann unser Spiegelbild zum Ersatz wird und wann die Maschine beginnt, für uns zu sprechen.

Die Besucher*innen betreten eine Welt, in der ihre Anwesenheit erfasst und interpretiert wird. Zunächst scheint das System ihr wahres Selbst und ihre Präsenz widerzuspiegeln. Allmählich beginnt die Reflexion jedoch, sich zu verselbstständigen: Sie sagt voraus, verzerrt und stellt die Besucher*innen falsch dar. Was als Moment des Wiedererkennens beginnt, wird zu Ambivalenz und Verdrängung. Die Arbeit legt keine bestimmte Form der Verzerrung fest, sondern lässt sie situativ entstehen und konfrontiert die Besucher*innen mit der irritierenden Erfahrung einer Repräsentation, die ihnen nicht mehr gehört.

House of Negotiated Selves untersucht KI-vermittelte Repräsentation und die Erosion menschlicher Agency. An der Schnittstelle von Interaktionsdesign, kritischer KI-Forschung und sensorischer Kunst angesiedelt, übersetzt das Projekt eine abstrakte Diskussion in eine greifbare Erfahrung. Im Mittelpunkt steht dabei nicht die Frage, was KI ist, sondern vielmehr wie sie beginnt, uns zu repräsentieren – unabhängig davon, ob wir dem zustimmen oder nicht.

Web Preview Text EN: Sound Bananas is an interactive installation that invites visitors to generate and shape sound through balance and movement—making the body itself the instrument.
Description EN:
Sound Bananas is an interactive installation that invites visitors to generate and shape sound through balance and movement—making the body itself the instrument. Sound Bananas consists of rocking, banana-shaped objects with integrated electronics. By moving, sitting on or rocking them, visitors generate musical sounds together—turning listening into a playful, collective and cross-modal experience. 
 
The project raises questions about participation and accessibility. Through intuitive, sensory-driven interfaces, it invites diverse audiences to engage—positioning sound not as a fixed output, but as a dynamic, co-created process shaped through shared bodily experience. The project explores listening as a physical, full-body practice involving balance, coordination and spatial awareness. It investigates how sound perception emerges through the interaction of body, movement and technology. The installation reveals how reality is shaped through embodied experience and technological mediation, opening up a reflection on how perception forms our relationship with the world.
Web Preview Text DE: Sound Bananas ist eine interaktive Installation, die Besucher*innen dazu einlädt, Klänge durch Gleichgewicht und Bewegung zu erzeugen und zu gestalten – wobei der eigene Körper selbst zum Instrument wird.
Description DE:
Sound Bananas besteht aus schaukelnden, bananenförmigen Objekten mit integrierter Elektronik. Indem die Besucher*innen sie bewegen, sich darauf setzen oder darauf wippen, erzeugen sie gemeinsam musikalische Klänge – Hören wird so zu einer spielerischen, kollektiven Erfahrung, die mehrere Sinnesmodalitäten verbindet.

Die interaktive Installation wurde am ligeti center in Hamburg entwickelt und verortet sich in aktuellen Diskursen zu Embodied Cognition, Mensch-Maschine-Interaktion und inklusivem Design. Das Projekt stellt Fragen nach Teilhabe und Zugänglichkeit. Über intuitive, sensorisch gesteuerte Schnittstellen lädt es ein vielfältiges Publikum zum Mitmachen ein und begreift Klang nicht als feststehendes Ergebnis, sondern als dynamischen, gemeinschaftlich hervorgebrachten Prozess, der durch geteilte körperliche Erfahrung entsteht.

Das Projekt untersucht Hören als körperliche Praxis, die den ganzen Körper einbezieht und Gleichgewicht, Koordination und räumliche Wahrnehmung umfasst. Es erforscht, wie Klangwahrnehmung im Zusammenspiel von Körper, Bewegung und Technologie entsteht – und wie solche Formen der Auseinandersetzung unser Verständnis menschlicher Agency in technologisch vermittelten Umgebungen verändern.

Web Preview Text EN: Quantum Compass is an interactive installation presenting the first typography based on quantum physics, capable of representing opposing concepts simultaneously. It uses quantum physics as a metaphor to invite reflection on post-truth and how we construct meaning.
Description EN:
Quantum Compass is an interactive installation presenting the first font based on the principles of quantum physics, designed to represent simultaneously multiple interpretations of public debate. Like particles passing through a double slit, the letters coexist in multiple states at once, behaving as waves that generate interference patterns until observation collapses them into a single stable form.
Set in the context of post-truth, the work uses quantum physics as a metaphor for polarized or contradictory interpretations, inviting reflection on the role we play in public discourse. It opens a space where contradiction can be experienced, as a trigger for reflection on meaning, technology and debate.

The Quantum Font is activated through hand gestures that trigger the quantum state of seemingly opposing concept pairs. Through movement, the audience navigates this ambiguity and brings the words toward their familiar, stable form, turning the participant’s body into an active part of the meaning-making process.
The installation incorporates infographics on the double-slit experiment and wave-particle duality, a photorealistic documentary on the material foundations of quantum computing and an interactive quantum computer for exploring its components.
Web Preview Text DE: Die interaktive Installation Quantum Compass präsentiert die erste auf Quantenphysik basierende Typografie, die in der Lage ist, gegensätzliche Konzepte gleichzeitig darzustellen. Sie nutzt die Quantenphysik als Metapher, um über Post-Wahrheit und die Konstruktion von Bedeutung nachzudenken.
Description DE:
Quantum Compass ist eine interaktive Installation, die die erste auf den Prinzipien der Quantenphysik basierende Schrift präsentiert. Die Typografie kann mehrere Interpretationen öffentlicher Debatten gleichzeitig darstellen. Wie Teilchen, die einen Doppelspalt passieren, existieren die Buchstaben gleichzeitig in mehreren Zuständen. Sie verhalten sich wie Wellen, die Interferenzmuster erzeugen, bevor sie durch Beobachtung eine eindeutige Form annehmen.
Im Kontext der Post-Wahrheit nutzt die Arbeit die Quantenphysik als Metapher für polarisierte oder widersprüchliche Interpretationen und lädt dazu ein, über die Rolle nachzudenken, die wir selbst im öffentlichen Diskurs einnehmen. Sie eröffnet einen Raum, in dem Widersprüche erfahrbar werden – als Anstoß zum Nachdenken über Bedeutung, Technologie und Debatte.

Die Quantum Font wird durch Handgesten aktiviert, die den Quantenzustand scheinbar gegensätzlicher Begriffspaare auslösen. Durch Bewegung navigieren die Besucher*innen durch diese Mehrdeutigkeit und führen die Wörter schrittweise in ihre vertraute, stabile Form über. So wird der Körper der Teilnehmer*innen selbst zu einem aktiven Bestandteil des Prozesses der Bedeutungsbildung.
Die Installation umfasst Infografiken zum Doppelspaltexperiment und zur Welle-Teilchen-Dualität, eine fotorealistische Dokumentation über die materiellen Grundlagen des Quantencomputings sowie einen interaktiven Quantencomputer, mit dem dessen Komponenten erkundet werden können.

Web Preview Text EN: Inspired by Waiting for Godot, Watching in Vain is an interactive telephone installation exploring the absurdity of endless waiting. Visitors lift the receiver seeking connection, but hear only short poems and unanswerable questions—a quiet paradox of hope without arrival.
Description EN: The project investigates the absurdity of endless waiting. Inside a semi-enclosed space, audiences encounter an interactive telephone installation. Lifting the receiver, they hear not a voice, but randomized short poems and unanswerable questions. The work offers a cultural critique of modern society’s state of constant suspension, where individuals are trapped in cycles of expectation, endlessly waiting for digital responses or futures that never arrive.

Web Preview Text EN: Assembled Faces is a 3D mapping installation exploring identity and surveillance. A camera captures viewers’ faces, using AI to mutate their features. The resulting algorithmic double is projected onto a wall of 3D-printed faces, critiquing how AI biases silently recode human identity.
Description EN: The project investigates the face as both an interface of identity and a target of surveillance. Audiences encounter a material wall of anonymously 3D-printed faces. A camera captures the viewers’ own faces, processing them through AI diffusion models to mutate their features. This algorithmic double is then projected onto the 3D wall. The installation offers a socio-political critique of modern surveillance and reveals how AI models, driven by biased training data, silently recode human subjects.

Description EN: The project investigates the dynamic preservation of cultural heritage. Audiences experience an interactive installation where their physical movements unfold layers of evolving digital imagery. Reimagining the ceremonial ephemerality of traditional paper craft, the visuals respond directly to the viewers’ gestures. Culturally, the work draws from Hong Kong’s Cheung Chau Bun Festival, allowing collective memory to be refolded and transforming static folklore into a living digital organism.

It follows a girl mourning her grandmother while accompanied by an AI designed to “repair” her grief, questioning if human loss retains meaning when emotions become computable.
Description EN: The project investigates whether human loss retains meaning when emotions become computable. Audiences will watch a 20-minute AIGC-generated short film depicting a teenage girl and an AI companion as they navigate their way through a period of mourning. Culturally rooted in Guangdong’s 49-day mourning rituals, the work critiques a socio-scientific future where AI systems manage emotional regulation, exploring how technology reconstructs and amplifies the inherent instability of human memory and grief.

Web Preview Text EN: Flood the Zone with Courage is conceived as an infrastructure for democratic negotiation in the heart of the city—a place for dissent and productive ambiguity, where the capacity to engage with conflict is not an abstract imperative but a daily practice. Throughout the festival, a packed program unfolds: performances, open workshops, Engagement Zones and participatory interventions in urban space.
Description EN:
In 2025, global military spending reached a record high of 2.9 trillion US dollars, rising for the eleventh consecutive year (SIPRI Military Expenditure Database 2026). At the same time, hard-won progress in equality, climate action and social infrastructure is coming under increasing pressure. War and militarization also serve as political excuses for sidelining urgent social questions. This is exactly where Flood the Zone with Courage begins: on Linz’s Main Square, where new forms of protest emerging from artistic practice meet research and civic engagement, and where it becomes apparent that our world knows not one truth but many, all claiming validity at the same time.
Developed collaboratively by the University of Arts Linz, Attac Austria, the Circus of Knowledge of Johannes Kepler University Linz and Ars Electronica, this project is conceived as a continuous, multi-voiced practice of democratic negotiation. It is not only a protest against something, but a commitment for something. Here, protest is understood not as disruption but as design. The aim is not consensus, but the capacity to engage with conflict—to move from debate to negotiation, from asking “Who is right?” to asking “How can contradictory yet legitimate concerns coexist?”.

Who profits from war and militarization, and who bears the costs? The assumption that security must primarily be achieved through military means, while social issues can be postponed until later, is not a political necessity—it is a political choice. Declaring equality, climate justice, social infrastructure or the rights of marginalized groups to be secondary in times of war is opting for a very narrow definition of security that obscures whose protection is prioritized, and whose vulnerability is accepted as the price. At a time when peace research is increasingly being pushed to the margins of public discourse, this format takes a clear position: it is precisely in times of escalating conflict that social justice, ecological responsibility and democratic participation must become even more central. War and militarization must not become an excuse for neglecting the urgent social issues of how we want to live together.

Throughout the festival, a packed program unfolds: performances, open workshops, Engagement Zones and participatory interventions in urban space. Its spatial core is the constantly evolving container architecture by Paul Eis, embodying the idea that a world in perpetual reconstruction holds no ready-made answers. The interventions favor co-creation over observation and invite active participation: through dancing together, voting rituals, choreographed actions and encounters across linguistic, class and cultural boundaries. Some interventions are conspicuous and loud, others so subtly woven into the fabric of the festival that visitors may already be participating without realizing it. Flood the Zone with Courage is conceived as an infrastructure for democratic negotiation in the heart of the city—a place for dissent and productive ambiguity, where the capacity to engage with conflict is not an abstract imperative but a daily practice.
Web Preview Text DE: Flood the Zone with Courage versteht sich als Infrastruktur des demokratischen Verhandelns mitten in der Stadt, als Ort des Dissens und der produktiven Uneindeutigkeit, an dem Konfliktfähigkeit nicht nur gefordert, sondern täglich neu erprobt wird. Während des Festivals entsteht ein dichtes Programm aus performativen Aktionen, offenen Workshops, Engagement Zones und partizipativen Interventionen im Stadtraum.
Description DE:
2025 haben die globalen Militärausgaben ein Rekordhoch von 2,9 Billionen US-Dollar erreicht, zum elften Mal in Folge (vgl.  SIPRI Military Expenditure Database 2026). Gleichzeitig geraten mühsam erarbeitete Fortschritte in der Gleichstellung, im Klimaschutz und in der sozialen Infrastruktur zunehmend unter Druck. Krieg und Aufrüstung funktionieren auch als politische Ausrede, gesellschaftliche Fragen zu verdrängen. Genau dort setzt Flood the Zone with Courage an: am Hauptplatz von Linz, wo neue Formen des Protests, hervorgegangen aus künstlerischen Prozessen, auf Forschung und zivilgesellschaftliches Engagement treffen und wo sichtbar wird, dass unsere Welt nicht eine Wahrheit kennt, sondern viele, die gleichzeitig Gültigkeit beanspruchen.  

Gemeinsam realisiert von der Kunstuniversität Linz, Attac Österreich, dem Zirkus des Wissens der Johannes Kepler Universität Linz und Ars Electronica, versteht sich das Projekt als kontinuierliche, vielstimmige Praxis demokratischer Aushandlung, die sich nicht nur gegen etwas richtet, sondern für etwas einsteht. Protest wird hier nicht als Störung verstanden, sondern als Gestaltung. Nicht Konsens ist das Ziel, sondern Konfliktfähigkeit, der Wechsel vom Debattenmodus in den Verhandlungsmodus, von der Frage “Wer hat recht?” zur Frage “Wie können widersprüchliche, legitime Anliegen nebeneinander bestehen?”.  Wer profitiert von Krieg und Aufrüstung, und wer trägt die Kosten? Die Logik, wonach Sicherheit militärische Priorität erfordert und gesellschaftliche Fragen auf spätere Zeiten vertagt, ist keine politische Notwendigkeit, sondern eine Entscheidung. Wer in Kriegszeiten Gleichstellung, Klimagerechtigkeit, soziale Infrastruktur und die Rechte marginalisierter Gruppen als nachrangig erklärt, entscheidet über eine sehr enge Definition von Sicherheit, die strukturell verschleiert, wessen Schutz gemeint ist und wessen Verwundbarkeit dabei in Kauf genommen wird. In einer Zeit, in der Friedensforschung zunehmend aus dem öffentlichen Diskurs gedrängt wird, setzt dieses Format dem eine klare Haltung entgegen: Gerade in Zeiten eskalierender Konflikte müssen soziale Gerechtigkeit, ökologische Verantwortung und demokratische Teilhabe umso entschiedener ins Zentrum rücken. Krieg und Aufrüstung dürfen keine Ausrede werden, um gesellschaftliche Fragen zu verdrängen.
 
Während des Festivals entsteht ein dichtes Programm aus performativen Aktionen, offenen Workshops, Engagement Zones und partizipativen Interventionen im Stadtraum. Den räumlichen Kern bildet die sich ständig verändernde Containerarchitektur von Paul Eis am Linzer Hauptplatz, die sichtbar macht, dass eine Welt, die immer wieder neu gebaut werden muss, keine fertigen Antworten kennt. Die Interventionen setzen auf Mitgestaltung statt Beobachtung und laden zur aktiven Teilnahme ein: durch gemeinsames Tanzen, Abstimmungsrituale, choreografische Aktionen und Begegnungen über Sprach-, Klassen- und Kulturgrenzen hinweg. Manche sind sichtbar und laut, andere so subtil in das Festivalgeschehen eingewoben, dass Besucher*innen bereits Teil von ihnen sind, ohne es zu wissen. Flood the Zone with Courage versteht sich als Infrastruktur des demokratischen Verhandelns mitten in der Stadt, als Ort des Dissens und der produktiven Uneindeutigkeit, an dem Konfliktfähigkeit nicht nur gefordert, sondern täglich neu erprobt wird.
