Name EN: Impact Initiative: Transforming Medicine Through AI and Arts
Subtitle EN: Ludwig Boltzmann Gesellschaft—Open Innovation in Science Center
Web Preview Text EN: The Impact Initiative: Transforming Medicine Through AI and Arts by the Ludwig Boltzmann Gesellschaft brings together science, art, technology and societal actors to develop new and open approaches to healthcare.
Description EN:
The way we think about health is less straightforward than it seems. It is shaped by scientific knowledge, cultural values, lived experience and ongoing societal negotiations—and it evolves with every new technological development.
With the emergence of Artificial Intelligence, the question is no longer what becomes medically possible, but also how AI is changing our understanding of health itself. Between bodies and data, professional judgment and algorithmic recommendation, care and efficiency, lived experience and standardized knowledge, fundamental questions arise: What forms of knowledge should shape healthcare in the future? Whose voices are heard—and whose are not? What constitutes good care? And ultimately, what kind of future for healthcare do we want to create in light of the possibilities enabled by AI?

The Impact Initiative: Transforming Medicine Through AI and Arts approaches these questions as a call to collaborate and co-create. It brings together science, art, technology and societal actors to develop new and open approaches to healthcare. Central to the initiative is the creation of spaces in which the transformation of healthcare can be explored, questioned and shaped collectively. Within this framework, art is not understood as a vehicle for illustrating scientific knowledge. Rather, it becomes a way of generating knowledge—revealing assumptions, raising new questions and enabling experiences that often remain inaccessible within scientific or technological paradigms alone.

The initiative was conceived by the Open Innovation in Science Center of the Ludwig Boltzmann Gesellschaft (LBG OIS Center) and has been carried out over the past two years in collaboration with the Linz Institute for Transformative Change (LIFT_C) at Johannes Kepler University Linz and Ars Electronica. It is funded by the Fonds Zukunft Österreich (FZÖ). The objective is to develop new forms of interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary collaboration between science, technology and the arts, fostering innovative approaches to the future challenges of healthcare.

At the heart of the initiative lies the conviction that innovation does not emerge from technological progress alone. It emerges where different forms of knowledge, experience and practice intersect. Each partner of the initiative contributes a distinct perspective: the Ludwig Boltzmann Institutes (LBI DHP, LBI NetMed, LBI SOAP) connect the initiative with leading fields of health research; the curatorial team of Ars Electronica provides access to artistic expertise and international creative networks; and LIFT_C at Johannes Kepler University Linz contributes research infrastructure, scientific expertise and engagement with students and researchers. The LBG Open Innovation in Science Center brings these different forms of knowledge together, designing the exploratory spaces and processes in which diverse perspectives do not merely meet, but begin to work together.

The initiative began with a series of Open Innovation in Science-based co-creation processes, in which researchers, artists, medical professionals and technology experts jointly developed challenges at the intersection of AI and healthcare. These challenges were further explored during a multi-day hackathon held in the lead-up to the Ars Electronica Festival 2025. Students from Artificial Intelligence, Medicine and Design collaborated with researchers and artists to materialize ideas, test assumptions through practice and develop initial prototypes. The resulting concepts were discussed as part of the Ars Electronica Festival with Knowledge and Innovation Communities (KICs) EIT Health and EIT Culture & Creativity and presented at JKUniverse.

The first experiments gave rise to new project collaborations that continued well beyond the hackathon. Through iterative development, new collaborations, and targeted support in project development and funding, they evolved into the works presented at the Ars Electronica Festival 2026. Two exhibition projects and a participatory workshop explore different questions at the intersection of AI, health and society. An interactive engagement point provides an entry into the initiative itself, inviting visitors to contribute their own perspectives to a collectively created graphic novel. Together, these different formats create spaces for encounter, participation and reflection, in which established understandings of health and technology can be reconsidered.

How Artificial Intelligence will shape healthcare—and what understandings and responsibilities will emerge through it—is therefore not merely a question of technology, but one of societal design and impact. The projects brought together within the Impact Initiative do not seek to provide conclusive answers. Instead, they invite us to reframe the questions, bring different perspectives into dialogue and collectively imagine how health and medicine might be shaped in the future.
Web Preview Text DE: Die Impact Initiative: Transforming Medicine Through AI and Arts bringt Wissenschaft, Kunst, Technologie und gesellschaftliche Akteur*innen zusammen, um neue, offene Zugänge zur Gesundheitsversorgung zu entwickeln.
Description DE:
Die Art und Weise, wie wir über Gesundheit nachdenken, ist weit weniger selbstverständlich, als es auf den ersten Blick scheint. Unser Verständnis von Gesundheit wird von wissenschaftlichem Wissen, kulturellen Werten, persönlichen Erfahrungen und gesellschaftlichen Aushandlungsprozessen geprägt – und verändert sich mit jeder neuen technologischen Entwicklung.
Mit dem Aufkommen Künstlicher Intelligenz stellt sich deshalb nicht mehr nur die Frage, was medizinisch möglich wird, sondern auch, wie KI unser Verständnis von Gesundheit selbst verändert. Zwischen Körpern und Daten, professioneller Urteilskraft und algorithmischen Empfehlungen, Fürsorge und Effizienz, gelebter Erfahrung und standardisiertem Wissen entstehen grundlegende Fragen: Welche Formen von Wissen sollen die Gesundheitsversorgung der Zukunft prägen? Wessen Stimmen werden gehört – und welche nicht? Was bedeutet gute Versorgung? Und letztlich: Welche Zukunft der Medizin wollen wir angesichts der Möglichkeiten, die Künstliche Intelligenz eröffnet, gemeinsam gestalten?

Die Impact Initiative: Transforming Medicine Through AI and Arts versteht diese Fragen als Einladung zur Zusammenarbeit und gemeinsamen Gestaltung. Sie bringt Wissenschaft, Kunst, Technologie und gesellschaftliche Akteur*innen zusammen, um neue, offene Zugänge zur Gesundheitsversorgung zu entwickeln. Im Zentrum der Initiative steht die Schaffung von Räumen, in denen die Transformation des Gesundheitswesens gemeinsam erforscht, hinterfragt und gestaltet werden kann. Kunst wird dabei nicht als Mittel verstanden, wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse zu veranschaulichen. Vielmehr wird sie selbst zu einer Form der Wissensproduktion: Sie macht Annahmen sichtbar, eröffnet neue Fragestellungen und ermöglicht Erfahrungen, die innerhalb rein wissenschaftlicher oder technologischer Paradigmen oft unzugänglich bleiben.

Konzipiert wurde die Initiative vom Open Innovation in Science Center der Ludwig Boltzmann Gesellschaft (LBG OIS Center) und in den vergangenen zwei Jahren gemeinsam mit dem Linz Institute for Transformative Change (LIFT_C) an der Johannes Kepler Universität Linz sowie Ars Electronica umgesetzt. Gefördert wird sie vom Fonds Zukunft Österreich (FZÖ). Ziel ist es, neue Formen inter- und transdisziplinärer Zusammenarbeit zwischen Wissenschaft, Technologie und Kunst zu entwickeln und damit innovative Zugänge zu den Herausforderungen der Gesundheitsversorgung von morgen zu schaffen.

Im Zentrum der Initiative steht die Überzeugung, dass Innovation nicht allein aus technologischem Fortschritt entsteht. Sie entsteht dort, wo unterschiedliche Formen von Wissen, Erfahrung und Praxis aufeinandertreffen. Jede Partnerinstitution der Initiative bringt dabei eine eigene Perspektive ein: Die Ludwig Boltzmann Institute (LBI DHP, LBI NetMed, LBI SOAP) verbinden die Initiative mit führenden Bereichen der Gesundheitsforschung, das kuratorische Team der Ars Electronica eröffnet den Zugang zu künstlerischer Expertise und internationalen Netzwerken, und LIFT_C an der Johannes Kepler Universität Linz trägt wissenschaftliche Infrastruktur, Forschungskompetenz sowie die Einbindung von Studierenden und Forschenden bei. Das LGB Open Innovation in Science Center schafft die Rahmenbedingungen für diese Zusammenarbeit und gestaltet jene Räume und Prozesse, in denen unterschiedliche Perspektiven nicht nur aufeinandertreffen, sondern produktiv miteinander arbeiten.

Den Ausgangspunkt bildete eine Reihe von Open-Innovation-in-Science-basierten Co-Creation-Prozessen, in denen Forschende, Künstler*innen, Mediziner*innen und Technologieexpert*innen gemeinsam Fragestellungen an der Schnittstelle von Künstlicher Intelligenz und Gesundheitsversorgung entwickelten. Diese wurden im Rahmen eines mehrtägigen Hackathons im Vorfeld des Ars Electronica Festival 2025 weiterbearbeitet. Studierende der Künstlichen Intelligenz, Medizin und des Designs arbeiteten gemeinsam mit Forschenden und Künstler*innen daran, Ideen zu materialisieren, Annahmen praktisch zu überprüfen und erste Prototypen zu entwickeln. Die entstandenen Konzepte wurden beim Ars Electronica Festival gemeinsam mit den Knowledge and Innovation Communities (KICs) EIT Health und EIT Culture & Creativity diskutiert und anschließend im JKUniverse präsentiert.

Die ersten Experimente führten zu neuen Projektkooperationen, die weit über den Hackathon hinaus fortbestanden. Durch iterative Weiterentwicklung, neue Kooperationen sowie gezielte Unterstützung in Projektentwicklung und Finanzierung entstanden daraus die Arbeiten, die beim Ars Electronica Festival 2026 präsentiert werden. Zwei Ausstellungsprojekte und ein partizipativer Workshop untersuchen unterschiedliche Fragestellungen an der Schnittstelle von KI, Gesundheit und Gesellschaft. Eine interaktive Anlaufstelle bietet einen Einstieg in die Initiative selbst und lädt Besucher*innen ein, ihre eigenen Perspektiven zu einer gemeinsam entstehenden Graphic Novel beizutragen. Gemeinsam schaffen diese unterschiedlichen Formate Räume der Begegnung, Teilhabe und Reflexion, in denen etablierte Vorstellungen von Gesundheit und Technologie neu gedacht werden können.

Wie Künstliche Intelligenz die Gesundheitsversorgung verändern wird – und welche Vorstellungen von Gesundheit, Verantwortung und Fürsorge daraus hervorgehen –, ist daher nicht allein eine technologische, sondern vor allem eine gesellschaftliche Gestaltungsfrage. Die in der Impact Initiative versammelten Projekte verstehen sich nicht als abschließende Antworten. Sie laden vielmehr dazu ein, Fragen neu zu formulieren, unterschiedliche Perspektiven miteinander ins Gespräch zu bringen und gemeinsam darüber nachzudenken, wie Gesundheit und Medizin der Zukunft gestaltet werden können.

Web Preview Text EN: Step into an illusory challenge where art meets real-time immersive technology. You’ll be plunged into darkness, surrounded by puzzles and an Artificial Intelligence won’t let you escape unless you prove your humanity...!
Description EN: The project explores the boundary between physical presence and spatial memory: How do individuals leave their mark within a tracked, collective ecosystem? The audience enters a pitch-black shapeless labyrinth, where UV lights and interactive projections show the world of illusions. Looking for their own way among apparent walls, hidden rooms and traces left by previous visitors, everyone will find the solution in their own way. Behind the scenes, a distributed network of sensors, AIs, projectors and real-time movement trackers, challenges the visitor armed only with a marker to draw. In an era of pervasive surveillance and isolated digital echo chambers, collaborative play is the key to beat this tracking technology. 13 transforms the isolating nature of being monitored into a vibrant, socio-cultural act of human expression, allowing thousands of authors (the public) to construct a boundless work of art, together.
Web Preview Text DE: Tauche ein in eine illusorische Herausforderung, bei der Kunst auf immersive Echtzeit-Technologie trifft. Dich erwarten völlige Dunkelheit, Rätsel und eine Künstliche Intelligenz, die dich nicht entkommen lässt, solange du nicht deine Menschlichkeit unter Beweis stellst...!
Description DE: Das Projekt untersucht die Grenze zwischen physischer Präsenz und räumlichem Gedächtnis: Wie hinterlassen Individuen ihre Spuren in einem überwachten, kollektiven Ökosystem? Besucher*innen betreten ein stockdunkles, formloses Labyrinth, in dem UV-Licht und interaktive Projektionen eine Welt der Illusionen entfalten. Auf der Suche nach ihrem eigenen Weg zwischen scheinbaren Wänden, versteckten Räumen und Spuren früherer Besucher*innen findet jede Person auf ihre ganz eigene Weise die Lösung. Hinter den Kulissen fordert ein verteiltes Netzwerk aus Sensoren, KI-Systemen, Projektoren und Echtzeit-Bewegungstrackern die Besucher*innen heraus, die lediglich mit einem Marker zum Zeichnen ausgestattet sind. In einer Zeit allgegenwärtiger Überwachung und isolierter digitaler Echokammern ist Kollaboration der Schlüssel, um diese Tracking-Technologie zu überwinden. 13 verwandelt den isolierenden Charakter der Überwachung in einen lebendigen, soziokulturellen Akt menschlichen Ausdrucks und ermöglicht es Tausenden von Urheber*innen (dem Publikum), gemeinsam ein grenzenloses Kunstwerk zu schaffen.

Subtitle EN: Make, Stir, Connect: Bubble Tea as an Immersive Cultural Interface
Web Preview Text EN: Bubble Tea turns the space into a giant cup of Taiwan’s iconic drink. Audiences become tapioca pearls, stirring, colliding and connecting through playful movements to brew an ever-changing bubble tea of culture and interaction.
Description EN: The event turns the space into a giant cup of bubble tea, where audiences become tapioca pearls inside a shifting virtual drink. Through movement, disturbance and connection, they collectively brew a constantly changing milk tea. With interactive projection, sensing and real-time animation, Bubble Tea reimagines Taiwan’s iconic drink culture as a playful system of cultural collision, social exchange and shared transformation.
Web Preview Text DE: Bubble Tea verwandelt den Raum in einen überdimensionalen Becher des ikonischen taiwanesischen Getränks. Die Besucher werden zu Tapiokaperlen, die sich spielerisch bewegen, miteinander in Berührung kommen und Verbindungen schaffen. So entsteht ein sich ständig wandelnder Bubble Tea aus Kultur, Begegnung und Interaktion.
Description DE:
Die Veranstaltung verwandelt den Raum in einen überdimensionalen Becher Bubble Tea, in dem die Besucher zu Tapiokaperlen in einem sich ständig verändernden virtuellen Getränk werden.
Durch Bewegung, Störung und Begegnung entsteht ein kollektiver Prozess, in dem fortwährend neuer Milchtee “gebraut“ wird. Mithilfe interaktiver Projektion, Sensorik und Echtzeit-Animation interpretiert Bubble Tea die ikonische Getränkekultur Taiwans als spielerisches System kultureller Kollision, sozialer Interaktion und gemeinsamer Transformation.
Credits short: With the support of Time-based and Interactive Media Art, University of Arts Linz and the Department of New Media Art at Taipei National University of the Arts.

The artist also thanks the roommates and close friends who shared tea, offering care and encouragement so she could continue completing the work, and the friends and family in Taiwan who listened to her most imaginative ideas from afar. She is grateful to the Department of New Media Art at Taipei National University of the Arts, including its faculty and administrative staff, whose support made the exchange and this project possible. Name EN: Sonic Saturday: Audible Futures, Silent Decisions
Web Preview Text EN: Sonic Saturday hosted by Anton Bruckner University features spatial sound concerts, live performances, and audiovisual and sound installations. This year’s edition explores how the future takes form within sonic practices.
Description EN:
Since 2016, Anton Bruckner University (ABU) has been hosting the Sonic Saturday as part of the Ars Electronica Festival. The event features spatial sound concerts, live performances, and audiovisual and sound installations. We aim to bring together artists, researchers and an audience interested in electroacoustic music, sonic art, spatial audio and multimedia practices to allow for an informal, in-person exchange of ideas.

Inspired by the festival theme Negotiating Humanity – Future Begins, we consider how the future takes form within sonic practices. 

The future is often imagined as something ahead of us. Yet if it is already embedded in the present, it unfolds through decisions: what is being developed, adopted, or ignored. In digital sound practices, we constantly choose what to render audible, what to simulate, what to enhance and what to leave behind. Spatial audio technologies promise ever more convincing environments and increasingly persuasive illusions. But to what end? 

Listening becomes a site where realities are constructed, filtered and negotiated. Some signals are amplified; others disappear through omission or design. What emerges is not only a sonic space, but a position within it. As artists and listeners, we operate within systems that increasingly automate these decisions. The question is no longer only what we can create, but what we choose to sustain. Will our digital music environments become a testing ground for possible futures, controlled simulations, or just additional layers of aesthetic insulation?

Web Preview Text EN: An evolving panoramic dusk sky is filled with auspicious signs drawn from East Asian tradition, which are generated endlessly and overwritten by one another until the sky buckles under their excess. Once rare omens seldomly read in the heavens, the work questions whether a blessing reproduced infinitely can still hold meaning.
Description EN: This is the world premiere of the newest artwork from Sputniko!, commissioned by Julius Baer Bank in collaboration with Ars Electronica. In this installation, an evolving panoramic dusk sky overflows with signs and symbols of good fortune drawn from East Asian tradition, inviting us to question the dissolving boundary between authenticity and fabrication in an age of AI-generated worlds.
Web Preview Text DE: Ein sich wandelnder Abendhimmel als Panorama füllt sich mit glückverheißenden Zeichen aus der ostasiatischen Tradition, die endlos erzeugt und gegenseitig überschrieben werden, bis der Himmel unter ihrer Überfülle einknickt. Einst waren es seltene Omen, die nur gelegentlich am Himmel gelesen wurden – nun stellt das Werk die Frage, ob ein unendlich oft reproduzierter Segen überhaupt noch Bedeutung haben kann.
Description DE: Dies ist die Weltpremiere des neuesten Kunstwerks von Sputniko!, das von der Julius Bär Bank in Zusammenarbeit mit Ars Electronica in Auftrag gegeben wurde. In dieser Installation wird ein Panorama eines sich stetig wandelnden Abendhimmels mit simulierten Glückszeichen der ostasiatischen Tradition überflutet und lädt dazu ein, die zunehmend verschwimmende Grenze zwischen Authentizität und Fiktion in einer Zeit KI-generierter Welten zu hinterfragen.

Subtitle DE: Negotiating Humanity Platform
Web Preview Text EN: How is our understanding of being human changing? Through artistic prototypes, interactive installations, and evolving artworks, Hello Worlds! invites visitors to experience, question and help shape possible futures together. Who will we become? What does it mean to be human?
Description EN:
Artificial Intelligence is increasingly becoming a counterpart in our world. It no longer exists on screens alone, but in robots, vehicles and intelligent systems. It speaks with us, moves through our environments and acts within them. Many abilities once considered uniquely human can now be simulated—or even performed—by AI. We develop and shape these technologies, while they shape us in return. They transform how we perceive, communicate, move, imagine the future and understand ourselves.
Through artistic prototypes, interactive installations and shared experiences, Hello Worlds! invites visitors to explore these questions together. The exhibition is the public outcome of the Future Humanity Project, an experimental research collaboration between Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota Motor Corporation’s Advanced R&D and Engineering Company. Visitors are invited to contribute their own perspectives, helping to shape the project's ongoing research.

Find more information about the exhibition on the websites of the https://ars.electronica.art/center/en/hello-worlds/ and the https://ars.electronica.art/futurelab/en/hello-worlds/.
Web Preview Text DE: Wie verändert sich unser Verständnis vom Menschsein? Mit künstlerischen Prototypen, interaktiven Installationen und sich weiterentwickelnden Kunstwerken lädt Hello Worlds! dazu ein, mögliche Zukünfte gemeinsam zu verhandeln. Wer werden wir in Zukunft sein? Was bedeutet es, Mensch zu sein?
Description DE:
Künstliche Intelligenz wird zunehmend zu einem Gegenüber: nicht nur auf Bildschirmen, sondern in Robotern, Fahrzeugen und intelligenten Systemen. Sie spricht mit uns, bewegt sich durch die Welt und handelt in ihr. Vieles von dem, was lange als einzigartig menschlich galt, kann KI heute simulieren – oder selbst leisten. Wir entwickeln und formen diese Technologien – und zugleich prägen sie uns. Sie verändern, wie wir wahrnehmen, sprechen, uns bewegen, die Zukunft denken und uns selbst verstehen.
Mit künstlerischen Prototypen, interaktiven Installationen und Kunstwerken lädt Hello Worlds! dazu ein, diese Fragen gemeinsam zu erkunden. Die Ausstellung ist das öffentliche Ergebnis eines Pilotprojekts des Ars Electronica Futurelab und der Toyota Motor Corporation Advanced R&D and Engineering Company.  Besucher*innen sind eingeladen, ihre Perspektiven einzubringen und so zur laufenden Forschung beizutragen.

Mehr Informationen zur Ausstellung auf den Websites des https://ars.electronica.art/center/de/hello-worlds/ und des https://ars.electronica.art/futurelab/de/hello-worlds/.

Web Preview Text EN: UN-ORGANIC is the eighth edition of an interdisciplinary artistic project developed since 2019 by the Random Check Media Ensemble (RCME). The project comprises four audiovisual compositions, performative actions and an interactive multimedia installation.
Description EN:
UN-ORGANIC is the eighth edition of an interdisciplinary artistic project developed since 2019 by the Random Check Media Ensemble (RCME)—a collective of artists affiliated with the Eugeniusz Geppert Academy of Art and Design and the Karol Lipinski Academy of Music in Wrocław along with invited guest collaborators. The project comprises four audiovisual compositions, performative actions and an interactive multimedia installation.  
The central theme of the Random Check 8 project is UN-ORGANIC. Their interest lies in what is inverted in relation to the organic (i.e., the living, human, natural, biological, etc.) and at the same time impossible without it.  
 
UN-ORGANIC is an exceptionally flexible category in process, continuously reflecting our relationship to nature and technology, to the nature—culture dichotomy in the 21st century, to the spontaneous hybridization of the worlds of humans and non-humans (including machines and AI) and to the prosthetization of human capacities for thinking and communication through increasingly “human” silicon-based solutions. 
 
Media art and new technologies teach us to unlearn the classical image of a world divided into dead and living matter, the inorganic and the organic. UN-RGANIC reverses the traditional logic of history: fixed points of reference dissolve into loops between humans and machines, nature and technology. 
 
New media return to nature—not as origin, but as an artificial and virtual image, shaped by art and culture from the very beginning around human needs. In this return, classical conceptions of nature and humanity begin to fade. The twilight of classical conceptions of nature and humanity is approaching. Will UN-ORGANIC*save us from disappearance?

Name EN: The Syntax of Nature and Other Approximate Truths
Web Preview Text EN: The Syntax of Nature and Other Approximate Truths questions the status of truths commonly regarded as natural and universal, exploring a space in which the notions of origin and originality begin to dissolve.
Description EN: The Syntax of Nature and Other Approximate Truths questions the status of truths commonly regarded as natural and universal. In a world increasingly shaped by algorithms and computational models, the boundary between discovering and constructing reality becomes ever more blurred. The work oscillates between the organic and the synthetic, the human and the generated, exploring a space in which the notions of origin and originality begin to dissolve. At the same time, it acts as a provocation—an impulse to break free from systems of rules in defense of intuition, instinct and epiphany.

Web Preview Text EN: The eponymous composition UN-ORGANIC unfolds as an unstable ecology of drifting filaments, luminous spores, vaporous tissues and half-formed organisms.
Description EN: The eponymous composition UN-ORGANIC unfolds as an unstable ecology of drifting filaments, luminous spores, vaporous tissues and half-formed organisms. Matter hovers between dead and alive: it breathes without permission, leaks, sends signals through membranes and withdraws into shadow. Familiar divisions between organic and inorganic, natural and artificial collapse into a speculative zone of latent life, nonhuman agencies and perception caught in the undergrowth of machines.

Web Preview Text EN: NEKRO//MAKINA is an audiovisual ritual in which death is no longer treated as an ending, but as a state that remains active. Suspended between ritual and machine, it inhabits a post-terminal condition where endings have already occurred, yet the apparatus continues to operate.
Description EN: NEKRO//MAKINA is an audiovisual ritual in which death is no longer treated as an ending, but as a state that remains active. Sound and image are bound together within a system that persists beyond collapse, continuously shifting between control and rupture, density and erosion. A fixed audiovisual core provides structure and duration, while live electronic interventions introduce instability, friction and excess. Suspended between ritual and machine, NEKRO//MAKINA inhabits a post-terminal condition where endings have already occurred, yet the apparatus continues to operate.

Web Preview Text EN: /////////// is a live audiovisual ritual of transformation and suspension. It emerges from noisy textures and unstable resonances and inhabits a space between continuity and dissolution.
Drawing upon the four compositions that form Random Check 8, the multimedia installation unfolds as a dynamic field of sound, image and bodily presence.
Description EN: Drawing upon the four compositions that form Random Check 8, the multimedia installation unfolds as a dynamic field of sound, image and bodily presence. Through choreographic actions and the energy generated by performers and audience alike, it continuously reconfigures the relationships between organic and synthetic forms, inviting participants into a process of transformation, reciprocity and emergence.

Description EN:
This audiovisual performance with live music, dance, moving image and immersive audio explores the limits between body, image and sound. 
Created by the collective Lluvia de Palos after more than a decade of research, this project proposes a sensory experience that brings together music, movement and image from a non-hegemonic perspective inspired by Mesoamerican thought. 
A scenic laboratory where the body thinks, remembers and acts: dance as a political gesture and a form of knowledge. The piece invites a return to the body as a territory of memory, trance and communion, understanding creation as a “saying-through-doing”, where thought becomes embodied through a poetics of ritual, in which Death appears as a transformative force—not as an end, but as transition, decomposition and rebirth. 
Here, the body does not represent; it transforms, fragments and multiplies. An experience where art, territory and memory intertwine through sound and movement.

Artists: Sandra Muciño (MX), Lilith Samer (AT), Mobina Vatandoost (IR), Boris Shershenkov (RU), Ricardo Pastor (ES), Saumil Bhandari (IN), Andreas Grünauer (AT), Bernhard Breuer (AT)
Web Preview Text EN: The Post-Digital Instruments Concert features a performance for bassoon and electronics by Sandra Muciño and a collaboratively developed composition on instruments with a post-digital reference by the Post-Digital Ensemble.
Description EN:
Program: 

Sandra Muciño (MX) 
Vultus
Performance for bassoon and electronics  

Behind this mask sounds the voice of Sandra Muciño’s grandmother; a censored and fragmented voice, like that of so many women. Through sound synthesis and real-time control, Muciño transforms this memory into an electronic landscape that engages in dialogue with the bassoon. Reinterpreting these garments of oppression appears as an act of resistance and Muciño’s own emancipation. 
If the trace is memory, this work seeks to ensure that the voices of the women who came before her continue to resonate through her steps and the means of her present.

Web Preview Text EN: MEDIUM SONORUM presents a selection of recent multichannel works. Performed through the impressive Sonic Lab’s 20.4 loudspeaker system, the concert explores contemporary approaches to spatial composition in relation to the theme Audible Futures, Silent Decisions.
Description EN:
MEDIUM SONORUM presents a selection of recent multichannel works chosen from the international call for contributions. Performed through the impressive Sonic Lab’s 20.4 loudspeaker system, the concert explores contemporary approaches to spatial composition in relation to the theme Audible Futures, Silent Decisions. 
 
Program: 
  
Xizan Liu (CN) 
Devour 
 
Devour (2024 / 15:00 min), inspired by the book Monster of God: The Man-Eating Predator in the Jungles of History and the Mind, is an octophonic piece that aims
 to evoke a dark and intense atmosphere, allowing listeners to freely imagine and interpret it as they wish. The composition features hybrid materials, including field recordings from Aulus Les Bains and synthesizer sounds from Hordijk Modular System, Make Noise Strega and Soma Laboratory Lyra-8. Diverse microphones were used for the field recordings—lavalier mics, contact mics, hydrophones and electromagnetic mics. 
 
Marta Zigante (IT) 
Nastro Finestre 
 
Nastro Finestre (2026 / 9:18 min) (trad. tape Windows) is a piece that explores the timbral characteristics of a cassette layer and the details of magnetic tape noise, movement and deterioration. 
The work aims to open and close “windows” in which listening is filtered through the physical properties of the medium, creating a dialogue between the concrete and the artificial. The main technique used in the piece is the sound processing of samples through an Irradio RE-730 cassette player, highlighting the details—and sometimes the malfunctions—of its mechanical operation.
Another technique employed is repeated tape recording and re-digitization, in order to emphasize the deterioration of both the sound spectrum and the tape itself when subjected to stress. The spatialization is intentionally radical: the main cassette player is positioned directly in front of the listener, while each of the eight loudspeakers also functions as a cassette player. The more ambient moments of the piece are instead diffused in a homogeneous and open manner, emphasizing the transition “from inside to outside the tape”. 
 
Wei-Yin Lo (TW) 
Sonic Flux: Spatial Resonance of Micro-Textures and Macro-Tensions 
 
Sonic Flux: Spatial Resonance of Micro-Textures and Macro-Tensions (2026 / 8:22 min) responds to the theme Audible Futures, Silent Decisions through an electroacoustic exploration of environmental collapse and spiritual redemption. 
The macro-structure initiates with the opening of the “Karmic Gate”. The composer personally journeyed to Yangmingshan and Zhuzihu for field recordings, capturing the underlying anxiety of the landscape shifting under human karma. This organic soundscape continuously alternates with synthetic audio, blurring the boundaries between physical reality and digital illusion. Integrating a spiritual resonance of Bhutan’s pure land, the piece seeks to capture moments of frozen time and universal fulfillment. Spoken texts, recorded by the composer, gradually strip away syntax and semantic coherence, dissolving into abstract phonetic matter that merges with the sonic architecture. As the piece progresses, layers of deconstructed piano overlap with vocal fragments to create an illusory psychoacoustic haze, symbolizing external chaotic interference. 
The central movement escalates into a catastrophic Anthropocene collapse—a protest from nature driven by simulated tectonic ruptures and violent dynamic hydro-acoustic tensions. In the aftermath, a digitally simulated chanting ritual is introduced via advanced synthesis, acting as a cosmic sanctuary mourning a destabilized planet. The composition finally resolves into a minimalist post-catastrophe landscape. As external interference fades, the piece returns to primal purity, digitally frozen into an eternal sonic horizon. When all turbulence settles within this frozen frequency, the acoustic silence transforms into a profound contemplative sanctuary for human reflection on our silent decisions. It evokes the essence of “form is emptiness, emptiness is form”, returning the soul to a deep sense of peaceful stability.
This work is dedicated to the spiritual peace of all sentient beings. 
 
Jonty Harrison (GB) 
Kammermusik 
– dedicated to Folkmar Hein 
 
Kammermusik (2022 / 11:47 min). A space (or concatenation of spaces) whose qualities we examine, explore and experience in sound… Different areas (sections) of this “chamber” betray their physical sources, but also resonate with references to terms used in electroacoustic music and signal processing—in order: threshold, noise floor, brick wall, windowing and headroom. The final section combines materials from the first four in a kind of “free association”, after windowing ends with two further “windows” which offer aural glimpses of “beyond”—outside, to external spaces, but also within, to the internal space of the imagination. 
Kammermusik was commissioned through the Thomas Seelig Fixed Media Award given by DEGEM. It was premiered on September 24th, 2022 in the Jahreskonzert der DEGEM und Verleihung des Thomas-Seelig-Fixed-Media-Preises as part of the KONTAKTE ’22 festival at the Akademie der Künste in Berlin (Germany). 
 
Zazie Productions [Zazie Kanwar-Torge (US)] 
Slippage Beyond the Hyperlink 
 
Slippage Beyond The Hyperlink (2026 / 2:15 min) is an immersive electroacoustic sound work assembled from degraded field recordings, manipulated found objects, synthetic ASMR textures, granular synthesis, corrupted signal chains and unstable digital artifacts. Drawing from acousmatic composition, analog decay, internet subcultures and binaural 3D spatial design, the piece unfolds as a collapsing auditory ecosystem in which glitches cease to function as interruptions and instead behave as adaptive mutations inside an increasingly automated technological landscape. 
Fragments of tactile noise, fractured ambience, compressed media residue, phantom notifications and hyperreal stereo illusions drift through the composition like remnants of failed future communication systems. Familiar sonic materials are repeatedly stretched, degraded, spatialized and recursively transformed until they begin to resemble emotional artifacts rather than recordings. 
Rather than presenting technology as sleek, frictionless or utopian, the work dwells inside malfunction, drift, compression scars, sensory overload, algorithmic repetition and unintended sonic consequences. Here, technological error becomes aesthetic language. Digital residue becomes cultural memory. Artificial intimacy becomes indistinguishable from ambient infrastructure. 
 
Chuowen Liang (CN) 
Dysregulation 
 
Dysregulation (2026 / 8:20 min) is an 8-channel spatial composition responding to the systemic crisis of burnout. In our relentless pursuit of automated progress, modern society operates on an unspoken consensus: that human exhaustion is an acceptable, even necessary, fuel for growth. Rather than viewing the days ahead as an abstract destination, this piece examines the realities we are actively constructing right now. It confronts the neglected psychological friction that our productivity-obsessed culture constantly marginalizes, questioning a system that demands endless output at the expense of our vital creative essence. 
To bring this invisible mental health crisis into a visceral, shared auditory space, the composition centers on a vocabulary of non-speech vocals. Stripped of language, these sounds project the sheer physical strain of a body pushed beyond its 
limits. The piece opens abruptly with high-tension, disturbing breaths, 
enveloping the listener in an environment of severe overstimulation. Gradually, the overwhelming structural order destabilizes. The anxious momentum sinks into a hollow, low-energy state, mirroring the paralyzing peak of burnout where the human engine completely stalls. By spatializing these vulnerable, exhausted textures, the work forces the discarded realities of mental health directly into the open. 
Following this devastating period of transition and silence, the immersive 8-channel space begins to shift. The composition slowly reintroduces tonality and defined pitches, mapping the delicate, complex process of recovery. Moving from bodily tension through collapse and finally into melodic restoration, Dysregulation transforms an isolating internal struggle into a collective physical experience. It challenges audiences to envision a tomorrow where sustainable human well-being is prioritized, rather than quietly sacrificed for perpetual motion.

Subtitle DE: Das Versprechen von Zugehörigkeit
Web Preview Text EN: RADICAL GAMING is a game experience and live performance about online belonging and radicalization. Players follow a person seeking acceptance online, where harmless play slowly turns into conformity, manipulation and exclusion. The work exposes how digital communities can transform recognition into control.
Description EN: RADICAL GAMING is a game experience and live performance in which players and audiences are gradually drawn into an online community that offers recognition and belonging. Structured as a three-part video game experience, players are pulled into a virtual world that feels at first rewarding but hides a deeper, darker reality underneath. Players step into the role of a young person who, ignored by their peers in real life, finds refuge online. What begins as harmless play gradually reveals the social mechanics behind many digital spaces: peer pressure, group conformity, status seeking and the desire to be seen. By the final level, the roles are reversed. Those once seeking acceptance are now asked to ridicule and harm others. Combining urban dance, freestyle performance, MCing and interactive media, RADICAL GAMING turns research into a game and the game into a mirror, exposing how communities built on belonging can become environments of control and radicalization.
Web Preview Text DE: RADICAL GAMING verbindet Videospiel und Performance zum Thema Online-Zugehörigkeit und Radikalisierung. Spieler*innen und Publikum begleiten eine junge Person auf ihrer Suche nach Akzeptanz im Internet. RADICAL GAMING zeigt auf, wie digitale Gemeinschaften Anerkennung in Kontrolle verwandeln können.
Description DE: RADICAL GAMING ist Videospiel und Live-Performance zugleich. Spieler*innen und Publikum werden nach und nach in eine Online-Community hineingezogen, die Anerkennung und Zugehörigkeit verspricht. Als dreiteiliges Spielerlebnis aufgebaut, führt das Projekt immer tiefer in eine virtuelle Welt, die zunächst einladend wirkt, unter deren Oberfläche sich jedoch eine dunklere Realität verbirgt. Die Spieler*innen schlüpfen in die Rolle einer jungen Person, die im realen Leben ignoriert wird und online Zuflucht findet. Was als harmloses Spiel beginnt, enthüllt nach und nach die sozialen Mechanismen vieler digitaler Räume: Gruppenzwang, Konformität, Statusstreben und der Wunsch, gesehen zu werden. Im letzten Level kehren sich die Rollen um. Aus dem Wunsch nach Akzeptanz wird Ausgrenzung. Durch die Verbindung von Urban Dance Freestyle-Performance, MCing und interaktiven Medien wird Forschung zum Spiel und das Spiel zum Spiegel, der zeigt, wie Online-Communities zu Räumen von Kontrolle und Radikalisierung werden können.

Web Preview Text EN: CAM Trails and tot–M2 turn technological limitations into design opportunities. CAM Trails builds atmosphere through the slow, ghosting visuals of an e-ink display, while tot–M2 explores tactile play and an asynchronous multiplayer. Both rethink how hardware shapes gameplay and storytelling.
Description EN: Both exhibits CAM Trails and tot–M2 explore how technological constraints can become a core part of game design. While CAM Trails uses the slow refresh and visual artifacts of an e-ink display to create tension and shape its narrative, tot–M2 reimagines handheld gaming through tactile interaction and an asynchronous multiplayer. Together, the projects demonstrate how hardware and interface design can influence storytelling, play and new forms of social connection.

Web Preview Text EN: In Rethinking Digital Imagery, student works explore alternative ways of displaying and communicating content through unconventional media, materials and technologies. Using interactive installations, they examine communication, memory, identity and perception while challenging conventional screens and digital media.
Description EN: A collection of student projects titled Rethinking Digital Imagery explores the display and transmission of information through unconventional media materials, and technological principles. Through interactive installations, the works examine relationships between humans and technology, addressing communication, memory, identity and perception. Together, they challenge conventional screens and digital media, seeking new ways to record, share and experience information.

Artists: LIT Open Innovation Center at JKU Linz (AT), Creative Region (AT), University of South Bohemia in České Budějovice (CZ), Art in the City (CZ)
Web Preview Text EN: The exhibition Creativity Matters, part of the Interreg AT-CZ project KreATivita&InovaCZe, features projects from the creative industries (CCI) in Upper Austria and South Bohemia. The exhibit focuses on the projects’ impact and how CCI sparks innovation across economy, society and the region.
Description EN:
The exhibition Creativity Matters, part of the Interreg AT-CZ project KreATivita&InovaCZe, showcases projects from the creative industries in Upper Austria and South Bohemia whose impact reaches well beyond their own field: Creativity opens up rural regions to new players, generates innovative production methods and makes research tangible. Communication translates regional character into brand identity. Architecture makes housing more affordable and climate-friendly. Design makes medical diagnostics more gender-equitable.
In short: These projects introduce creative methods such as co-creation and prototyping to various industries, strengthen regional identity, and connect generations, disciplines and countries.
Here, impact means more than just numbers. It’s about lasting change—in people, places, industries. Together, the projects show how the creative industries as a cross-cutting sector spark innovation across the economy, society and the region.
Web Preview Text DE: Die Ausstellung Creativity Matters ist Teil des Interreg AT-CZ-Projekts KreATivita&InovaCZe und präsentiert Projekte der Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft aus Oberösterreich und Südböhmen. Sie zeigt, wie dieser Sektor Innovationen in Wirtschaft, Gesellschaft und der regionalen Entwicklung vorantreibt.
Description DE:
Die Ausstellung Creativity Matters ist Teil des Interreg AT-CZ-Projekts KreATivita&InovaCZe und präsentiert Projekte der Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft aus Oberösterreich und Südböhmen, deren Wirkung weit über ihren eigenen Bereich hinausreicht: Kreativität eröffnet ländlichen Regionen neue Perspektiven, schafft innovative Produktionsmethoden und macht Forschung erlebbar. Kommunikation übersetzt regionale Identität in starke Marken. Architektur entwickelt bezahlbaren und klimafreundlichen Wohnraum. Design trägt zu einer geschlechtergerechteren medizinischen Diagnostik bei.
Kurz gesagt: Die vorgestellten Projekte bringen kreative Methoden wie Co-Creation und Prototyping in unterschiedlichste Branchen ein, stärken die regionale Identität und schaffen Verbindungen zwischen Generationen, Disziplinen und Ländern. “Impact” bedeutet hier mehr als messbare Kennzahlen. Die Wirkung zeigt sich in nachhaltigen Veränderungen – für Menschen, Orte und Branchen. Gemeinsam machen die Projekte sichtbar, wie die Kultur- und Kreativwirtschaft sektorübergreifende Innovationen in Wirtschaft, Gesellschaft und der regionalen Entwicklung anstößt.

Web Preview Text EN: Sola Tarantula is a kinetic installation that invites visitors to play and interact. When the work suddenly comes to a standstill, a moment of dependence arises: asking for or offering help becomes necessary. In this way, the work explores how care, cooperation and positive change come about.
Description EN:
Sola Tarantula is a kinetic installation that invites visitors to play and interact. It is made from two mobility scooters, various steel and 3D-printed parts and appears to move of its own accord. When the work unexpectedly comes to a standstill, a new situation arises: the participants must act independently or ask others for help. In this way, Sola Tarantula reflects life itself. Things do not always go as planned, and we often need one another to move forward. The installation explores how care, cooperation and positive change come about; it is a kinetic work about relying on one another, which invites the public to participate in a playful experience of movement and interaction. 

Within the context of the exhibition, Sola Tarantula explores how social realities are created through relationships, mutual support, collective action and care. It asks what forms of community can emerge when we understand interdependence not as a weakness, but as a foundation of human coexistence.
Web Preview Text DE: Sola Tarantula ist eine kinetische Installation, die Besucher*innen zu einer spielerischen Erfahrung von Bewegung und Interaktion einlädt. Die Arbeit untersucht, wie soziale Wirklichkeit durch Beziehungen, gegenseitige Unterstützung und gemeinsames Handeln mit Fürsorge entsteht.
Description DE:
Sola Tarantula ist eine kinetische Installation, die Besucher*innen zu einer spielerischen Erfahrung von Bewegung und Interaktion einlädt. Die aus zwei Elektromobilen, Stahl und 3D-gedruckten Elementen bestehende Skulptur scheint sich eigenständig fortzubewegen. Wenn die Arbeit unerwartet zum Stillstand kommt, entsteht eine neue Situation: Die Beteiligten müssen selbst handeln oder die Unterstützung anderer suchen. In diesem Moment der Abhängigkeit macht die Arbeit sichtbar, dass Fortbewegung und Veränderung nicht immer individuell möglich sind, sondern auf gegenseitiger Unterstützung beruhen. Sie reflektiert damit grundlegende soziale Erfahrungen: dass wir aufeinander angewiesen sind, Hilfe benötigen und gemeinsam Wege finden müssen, um weiterzukommen. 

Im Kontext der Ausstellung untersucht Sola Tarantula, wie soziale Wirklichkeit durch Beziehungen, gegenseitige Unterstützung und gemeinsames Handeln mit Fürsorge entsteht. Sie fragt danach, welche Formen von Gemeinschaft wir hervorbringen können, wenn wir Abhängigkeit nicht als Schwäche, sondern als Grundlage menschlichen Zusammenlebens verstehen.

Name EN: I Tell the Moon My Secret and the Moon Tells Me Yours
Web Preview Text EN: An interactive artwork invites visitors to submit secrets that are translated into robotic movements and long-exposure photographs. Using the Moon as the sole light source, the work transforms secrets into cryptic visual traces shaped by computational systems and the uncontrollable environment.
Description EN: This interactive artwork explores digital communication shaped by forces beyond human control. Visitors whisper secrets that are translated into robotic movements and long-exposure photographs with the Moon as the sole light source. The project combines robotics, photography and the environment to transform secrets into cryptic visual traces, reflecting on human relationships with technology, nature and uncertainty. The Moon is an active participant rather than a passive object of observation.
Credits long: Artwork by Zoe Qi-Jing Li | Supervisor: Clea von Chamier-Waite | Computational Media and Arts Thrust, Information Hub, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Guangzhou, China

Subtitle EN: Cross-Modal Translation of Implicit Micro-Actions in Chinese Calligraphy
Web Preview Text EN: BruSHŪ is a sensor-embedded calligraphy brush that captures subtle gestures, orientation changes and motion during writing. These signals are translated into sound and generative visuals, creating a real-time feedback loop in which every audiovisual output emerges directly from live brush movement.
Description EN: BruSHŪ is a sensor-embedded calligraphy brush and real-time cross-modal feedback system. It captures implicit micro-actions during brushwork—contact boundaries, orientation shifts, motion energy—and translates them into synchronized sound and generative visual output. The system operates as a closed sensing-to-feedback loop with no pre-recorded content; all output is generated in real time from live brush movement.
Credits long: Artwork by Tian-Cheng Liu, Nicolò Merendino | Supervisor: Kang Zhang | Computational Media and Arts Thrust, Information Hub, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Guangzhou, China

Web Preview Text EN: Blending art and science, this interactive installation uses real-time eye-tracking to connect human perception with cosmic and geological processes. Viewers’ gaze shapes a simulation of 64,000 astronomical bodies and projected quarry landscapes, making invisible planetary forces tangible.
Description EN: Blending art and science, this installation uses a hybrid media approach, using real-time eye-tracking to connect human perception with cosmic and geological phenomena. A wearable eye tracker maps viewers’ gaze onto a simulation of 64,000 astronomical bodies shaped by dark matter and dark energy, while also shaping projected geological textures derived from an abandoned quarry in China. Integrating astronomy, computation and geology, the work renders invisible planetary forces tangible.
Credits long: Artwork by Jue Wang | Supervisor: Clea von Chamier-Waite | Computational Media and Arts Thrust, Information Hub, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Guangzhou, China

Web Preview Text EN: This multi-channel audiovisual installation explores generative AI as a process of transforming possibility into perception. Combining live-action footage with AI-generated imagery creates an immersive space that blurs the boundaries between the real, the imagined and the algorithmically possible.
Description EN: KARMA is a multi-channel audiovisual installation exploring generative AI through the artist’s concept of sensory projection, in which generation is understood as the collapse of countless high-dimensional possibilities into perceptible forms by human intent. Combining real footage with AI-generated imagery, the work unfolds as a shifting field of imagined realities, inviting viewers into an embodied, spatialized encounter with algorithmic perception and the boundaries between the real and the possible.

Web Preview Text EN: This interactive textile installation explores trauma as an embodied experience beyond language. Using resistant materials and responsive woven forms, the work invites touch and participation, allowing personal and collective traumas to emerge, evolve and transform through bodily engagement.
Description EN: Touch Our Scar is a tactile, interactive artwork examining trauma as an embodied, non-linguistic experience through “painful weaving”, in which hostile materials are woven into textile forms. Nine individual trauma textiles prompt touch, while two collective textile works detect and respond to contact, evolving in real time as trauma manifests, is processed, and is transformed between body, material and time.

Name EN: SPILLING THE TEA? – A Soft Material Experience
Name DE: SPILLING THE TEA? – A Soft Material Experience
Web Preview Text EN: SPILLING THE TEA? – A Soft Material Experience is a ceremonial tea salon with a robotic touch. Visitors are invited to wear knitted exoskeletal gloves to pour themselves a cup of tea, while exploring the relationship between the human body, soft textile technology and perceived control and trust.
Description EN:
SPILLING THE TEA? – A Soft Material Experience illustrates how wearable robotics made from textiles may change the way people perceive their own bodies, abilities and agency. With this project, we translate the relationship between material properties, robotic systems and social interactional context into an embodied experience.
Visitors are invited to enter a cozy yet unusual tea salon entirely shaped by soft, handcrafted textiles. At the tea table, knitted exoskeletal gloves with pneumatic actuators can be worn to grasp and interact with requisites of a tea set. The exoglove guides hand movements in everyday tasks and can be controlled by the wearer themselves, but potentially also other entities.
The installation connects psychological research on exoskeletons with textile-based wearable robotics. It relates to wider questions about smart clothing, assistive technologies, trust, control, vulnerability, and how close, soft and active technology should come to the human body.
Web Preview Text DE: SPILLING THE TEA? – A Soft Material Experience ist eine Teezeremonie mit einem Hauch Robotik. Besucher*innen sind eingeladen, sich mit gestrickten Hand-Exoskeletten eine Tasse Tee einzuschenken und die Beziehung zwischen Körper, tragbarer textiler Technologie und erlebter Kontrolle zu erkunden.
Description DE:
SPILLING THE TEA? – A Soft Material Experience zeigt, wie tragbare textile Robotik die Wahrnehmung des eigenen Körpers und seiner Fähigkeiten verändern kann. Das Projekt macht die Beziehung zwischen Material, moderner Robotik und sozialer Interaktion körperlich erfahrbar.
Besucher*innen sind eingeladen, einen gemütlichen und zugleich ungewöhnlichen Teesalon zu betreten, der vollständig aus weichen Textilien gestaltet ist. Am Teetisch können sie gestrickte Exoskelett-Handschuhe mit pneumatischen Aktuatoren anziehen, um Gegenstände eines Teeservices zu greifen und mit ihnen zu interagieren. Der Exo-Handschuh unterstützt die Handbewegungen und kann von den Träger*innen selbst, potenziell aber auch von anderen Akteur*innen gesteuert werden.
Die Installation behandelt übergeordnete Fragen zu intelligenter Kleidung, assistiven Systemen, Vertrauen und Kontrolle. Sie wirft die Frage auf, wie nah diese textile und aktive Form von Technologie dem menschlichen Körper kommen sollte.

Description EN: Becoming Space is a sculpture and video installation exploring human-animal transformation through Ovid’s Metamorphoses. Drawing on Deleuze and Guattari’s concept of “becoming-animal”, the artist presents transformation as an intensification of identity and capacity, always collective, always entangled with forces beyond the individual. AI generation and 3D printing participate actively in this process, distributing agency across algorithms, text, machines and matter, creating a non-human approach to becoming.

Web Preview Text EN: Chaos is an interactive, multiplayer experience that explores music and form. Players use their own movements to change the frequency and amplitude of certain visual waves, and when these waves intersect with those of other players, they create unique melodies.
Description EN: This project explores the connections between music and form. When the game starts, the player will see waves that can be manipulated through their own movement. Moving along the X-axis changes the wave’s amplitude, while moving along the Y-axis changes its frequency. When the player’s waves come into contact with those of other players, they intersect and music begins to play.
Web Preview Text DE: Ein interaktives Multiplayer-Erlebnis, das Musik und Form erforscht. Die Spieler*innen nutzen ihre Bewegungen, um Frequenz und Amplitude visueller Wellen zu verändern. Wenn sich ihre Wellen überschneiden, entstehen einzigartige Melodien.
Description DE: Das Projekt erforscht die Verbindung von Musik und Form. Sobald das Spiel beginnt, sehen die Besucher*innen Wellen, die durch ihre eigenen Bewegungen manipuliert werden können: Eine Bewegung entlang der X-Achse verändert die Amplitude der Welle, während eine Bewegung entlang der Y-Achse ihre Frequenz verändert. Wenn die eigenen Wellen jene anderer Spieler*innen berühren, überschneiden sie sich, und Musik beginnt zu spielen.

Web Preview Text EN: While the festival theme NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS proposes that humanity is not a fixed condition, but an ongoing process of negotiation, Negotiating Beyond Humanity expands this horizon by turning towards the more-than-human beings.
Description EN:
While the festival theme NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS proposes that humanity is not a fixed condition, but an ongoing process of negotiation, Negotiating Beyond Humanity expands this horizon by turning towards the more-than-human beings. Grounded in the transdisciplinary exchanges that have unfolded through three years of the Studiotopia residency program, the exhibition contributes to a broader inquiry into the possibilities opened by sustained dialogue between artistic and scientific perspectives on planetary coexistence. 

To move beyond the human perspective is to recognize the many forms of life, living systems and material processes that continually shape our shared reality, and the relationships through which we are entangled with them. From soil organisms, microbes and fungi to insects, rivers and forests, these are encountered not as passive objects or resources, but as active participants whose agencies, temporalities and modes of communication exceed familiar human frameworks.

Much of life unfolds beyond what is immediately perceptible. The microbial worlds beneath our feet and within our bodies sustain complex exchanges that continually shape living systems while remaining largely invisible. By drawing attention to these hidden ecologies, the works expand sensory experience and encourage forms of knowing grounded not only in observation, but in listening, touch, immersion and reciprocity, too.

From these processes barely noticeable to the human eye, the exhibition then turns towards more readily perceptible forms of life by exploring how different beings sense, inhabit and negotiate their environments. Rather than claiming to represent non-human experience, the works create situated encounters that invite visitors to recognize the limits of human perception while remaining open to other sensory worlds. Smell, color, vibration and ecological interaction become points of contact through which relationships emerge without reducing differences.

Finally, our attention shifts to ecological crises, tracing how drought, extraction, deforestation and planetary transformation unfold across intertwined environmental, technological, legal and political processes. Here, the exhibition questions whose voices, knowledges and forms of participation shape responses to these challenges. It foregrounds negotiations that unfold across species, infrastructures and territories, recognizing that ecological futures cannot be understood through human perspectives alone.

By moving from imperceptible microbial exchanges to planetary ecological transformations, Negotiating Beyond Humanity reveals negotiation as a practice that reaches beyond human perspectives alone. It leaves us with an open invitation to consider how the Symbiocene might begin not as an ideal future, but through the relationships and negotiations we cultivate in the present.

This exhibition features projects developed in the framework of Studiotopia, co-funded by the Creative Europe Programme of the European Union, as well as presents the projects in the framework of Seeds of Connection – Soil Literacy & Innovation through Digital Arts and the STARTS Prize, funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme.

Web Preview Text DE: Während das Festivalthema NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS das Menschsein nicht als unveränderlichen Zustand, sondern als fortwährenden Aushandlungsprozess versteht, erweitert Negotiating Beyond Humanity diesen Horizont und wendet sich den mehr-als-menschlichen Wesen zu.
Description DE:
Während das Festivalthema NEGOTIATING HUMANITY – FUTURE BEGINS das Menschsein nicht als unveränderlichen Zustand, sondern als fortwährenden Aushandlungsprozess versteht, erweitert Negotiating Beyond Humanity diesen Horizont und wendet sich den mehr-als-menschlichen Wesen zu. Die Ausstellung baut auf den transdisziplinären Begegnungen auf, die im Laufe der drei Jahre des Studiotopia-Residency-Programms entstanden sind. Sie leistet damit einen Beitrag zu einer umfassenderen Auseinandersetzung mit den Möglichkeiten, die sich eröffnen, wenn künstlerische und wissenschaftliche Perspektiven auf das planetare Zusammenleben in einen kontinuierlichen Dialog treten.

Über das Menschliche hinauszudenken bedeutet, die Vielzahl von Lebensformen, lebendigen Systemen und materiellen Prozessen, die unsere gemeinsame Wirklichkeit kontinuierlich mitgestalten, sowie die Beziehungen, durch die wir mit ihnen verflochten sind, anzuerkennen. Von Bodenorganismen, Mikroben und Pilzen bis hin zu Insekten, Flüssen und Wäldern – ihnen wird nicht als passive Objekte oder bloße Ressourcen begegnet, sondern als aktive Teilnehmende, deren Agency, Zeitlichkeiten und Kommunikationsformen die vertrauten menschlichen Denkrahmen überschreiten.

Ein Großteil des Lebens entfaltet sich jenseits des unmittelbar Wahrnehmbaren. Die mikrobiellen Welten unter unseren Füßen und in unseren Körpern bilden komplexe Netzwerke, die lebendige Systeme fortlaufend prägen, ohne unmittelbar sichtbar zu sein. Indem die Arbeiten die Aufmerksamkeit auf diese verborgenen Ökologien lenken, erweitern sie unsere sinnliche Erfahrung und ermutigen zu Formen des Wissens, die nicht allein auf Beobachtung, sondern auch auf Zuhören, Berührung, Immersion und Reziprozität beruhen.

Von diesen für das menschliche Auge kaum wahrnehmbaren Prozessen wendet sich die Ausstellung schließlich weniger verborgenen Lebensformen zu. Die Arbeiten erkunden, wie unterschiedliche Wesen ihre Umwelt wahrnehmen, bewohnen und mit ihr in Beziehung treten. Statt zu behaupten, nicht-menschliche Erfahrung repräsentieren zu können, schaffen sie situierte Begegnungen, die die Grenzen menschlicher Wahrnehmung sichtbar machen und sie zugleich für andere sensorische Welten öffnen. Gerüche, Farben, Schwingungen und ökologische Wechselwirkungen werden zu Berührungspunkten, durch die Beziehungen entstehen, ohne Unterschiede einzuebnen.

Schließlich richtet sich der Fokus auf ökologische Krisen und zeichnet nach, wie Dürre, Rohstoffgewinnung, Entwaldung und planetare Transformation sich über miteinander verwobene ökologische, technologische, rechtliche und politische Prozesse hinweg zeigen. Die Ausstellung hinterfragt, wessen Stimmen, welches Wissen und welche Formen der Teilhabe unser Handeln angesichts dieser Herausforderungen prägen. Sie stellt Verhandlungen in den Vordergrund, die sich über Arten, Infrastrukturen und Territorien hinweg entfalten, und verdeutlicht, dass ökologische Zukünfte nicht allein aus menschlicher Perspektive verstanden werden können.
 
Indem Negotiating Beyond Humanity den Bogen von unsichtbaren mikrobiellen Austauschprozessen bis hin zu planetaren ökologischen Transformationen spannt, versteht die Ausstellung das Verhandeln als eine Praxis, die über rein menschliche Perspektiven hinausreicht. Sie lädt dazu ein, das Symbiozän nicht als ideale Zukunft zu begreifen, sondern als etwas, das in den Beziehungen und Verhandlungen beginnt, die wir bereits heute gestalten.

Die Ausstellung zeigt im Rahmen von Studiotopia entwickelte Projekte, kofinanziert durch das Creative Europe Programme der Europäischen Union, sowie Arbeiten im Rahmen von Seeds of Connection – Soil Literacy & Innovation through Digital Arts und des STARTS Prize, gefördert durch das Forschungs- und Innovationsprogramm Horizon Europe der Europäischen Union.

Web Preview Text EN: Take control of a gigantic flock of birds and experience the mechanism behind the fascinating natural phenomenon of a murmuration. Either be a part of these synchronized movements and create fluid, constantly morphing shapes or disturb these movements as a bird of prey!
Description EN: A murmuration is a stunning natural phenomenon where thousands of birds form complex, organism-like shapes in the sky. This project explores how relatively simple rules create such collective behavior. Visitors can interact with the flock: the first person becomes the attractor, guiding the flock, while others act as birds of prey, disrupting the swarm and causing ripples. Such emergent behaviors highlight both the vital connectivity but also the fragility of the ecosystems all around us.
Web Preview Text DE: Übernimm die Kontrolle über einen riesigen Vogelschwarm und erlebe den Mechanismus hinter dem faszinierenden Naturphänomen der Murmuration. Werde Teil dieser synchronisierten Bewegungen und erschaffe fließende, sich ständig verändernde Formen – oder störe diese Abläufe als Raubvogel!
Description DE: Die Murmuration ist ein beeindruckendes Naturphänomen, bei dem tausende Vögel komplexe, an Organismen erinnernde Formen am Himmel bilden. Dieses Projekt untersucht, wie relativ einfache Regeln ein solches kollektives Verhalten erzeugen können. Besucher*innen können mit dem Schwarm interagieren: Die erste Person wird zum Attraktor und lenkt den Schwarm, während andere als Raubvögel agieren, die den Schwarm stören und Wellenbewegungen auslösen. Solche emergenten Verhaltensweisen machen sowohl die lebenswichtige Vernetzung als auch die Fragilität unserer Ökosysteme sichtbar.

Description EN:
The exhibition showcases the 23 winning projects in the u19—create your world category of the Prix Ars Electronica 2026.

Since 1998, this competition has invited young creatives and critical thinkers to share their ideas and projects for the world of tomorrow—across the fields of art, technology and society. Participants are free to choose their medium, resulting in a wide range of analog and digital submissions. All works are created by creatives up to 19 years of age, boldly expressing personal perspectives and presenting inspiring visions for the future. 

A jury of five experts from diverse disciplines reviews all entries based on their creativity and expressiveness, selecting the 23 winning projects. Additional participants are also invited to develop commissions and workshops for create your world. This year’s winning projects will be presented at the https://ars.electronica.art/negotiatinghumanity/en/view/AwardCeremonyu19createyourworld-38438ddb450c80bf90daebfed8347fba/ on September 12th at 14:00 in Lecture Hall 1, MED Campus. The young artists will receive their certificates and offer a brief insight into the ideas behind their work.

Blending art archives, storytelling and media art, the project invites visitors to explore and experience cultural heritage in new ways.
Description EN: This event explores how Klemens Brosch’s unfinished late work Red Dinosaurs can be reinterpreted and recontextualized through new technologies. Visitors encounter a gigapixel reproduction of the painting, an abstract animation and an interactive installation based on the artwork. The project investigates how art archives can become living spaces for dialogue, bringing historical works back into public discourse and creating new connections between cultural heritage and contemporary society.

Web Preview Text EN: The Writing Lab offers a space for writing in all its forms. Here, you will find a quiet place to put your thoughts on paper freely and without distraction.
Description EN:
The Writing Lab offers a quiet space where you can put your thoughts on paper, freely and without pressure.

Want to try writing your first short story? 
Have an idea for a novel but keep putting off the first page? 
Turn your festival experiences into a poem? 
Write a letter to your younger—or older—self?
Experiment with a screenplay or a play? 
Or don’t have an idea yet? No problem. Browse the writing prompts available on site and see where they take you.

Pick up a pen and paper—or sit down at a typewriter—and simply start writing.

The Writing Lab celebrates the often less visible art of writing in all its forms, creating the space it deserves.

Every day from 15:00 to 17:00, everyone with an interest in writing is invited to join the Writing Lab to talk about their texts, exchange ideas and give each other feedback—on Wednesday by Antonia Schneider, on Thursday by Maria Hinterkörner (drehbuchFORUM Vienna), on Friday by Felicitas Tholey, on Saturday by Sofia Engler (TEXTE Festival) and on Sunday by Abelina Holzer.
There are no expectations: You do not need to bring a finished or polished piece. You are welcome to simply listen or share feedback.
Web Preview Text DE: Mit der Schreibwerkstatt möchten wir der Kunstform des Schreibens in all ihren Facetten Raum bieten. Hier findest du einen ruhigen Ort, um deine Gedanken frei zu Papier zu bringen.
Description DE:
Die Schreibwerkstatt bietet dir einen ruhigen Raum, um all deine Gedanken frei zu Papier zu bringen.

Du willst dich an deiner ersten Kurzgeschichte versuchen?
Du hast eine Idee für einen Roman, drückst dich aber vor dem Beginn?
Du möchtest die Erlebnisse deines Festivaltages in ein Gedicht verpacken?
Du möchtest einen Brief an dein älteres oder jüngeres Ich schreiben?
Du wolltest dich schon immer mal an einem Drehbuch oder Theaterstück versuchen?
Du hast noch keine konkrete Idee? Kein Problem – lass dich einfach von einer der Schreibideen vor Ort inspirieren!

Schnapp dir Stift und Papier oder setz dich an die Schreibmaschine und schreib einfach drauflos.

Mit der Schreibwerkstatt möchten wir der – oft weniger sichtbaren – Kunstform des Schreibens in all ihren Facetten den Raum verleihen, der ihr gebührt.

Täglich von 15:00 bis 17:00 sind alle Schreibinteressierten eingeladen, sich in der Schreibwerkstatt einzufinden, über ihre Texte zu sprechen und sich gegenseitig Feedback zu geben – angeleitet am Mittwoch von Antonia Schneider, am Donnerstag von Maria Hinterkörner (drehbuchFORUM Wien), am Freitag von Felicitas Tholey, am Samstag von Sofia Engler (TEXTE Festival) und am Sonntag von Abelina Holzer.
Bei der Textwerkstatt gibt es keinerlei Erwartungshaltung: Du musst keinen fertigen oder perfekten Text mitbringen – du kannst auch einfach zuhören oder anderen Tipps geben!

Description EN: Whose future is being designed here? The libertarian fantasies of tech elites—from Elon Musk to Peter Thiel—promise technological solutions to society’s problems, bypassing democratic control and social responsibility. But behind the promise of progress lies a dystopian reality: growing concentration of wealth, anti-democratic power politics, and a deeply rooted vision of traditional masculinity. Web Preview Text EN: This year’s Symposium Perspectives on Political Education, held as part of the Ars Electronica Festival, addresses topics such as tolerance, democratic rights and social responsibility.
Description EN:
This year’s Symposium Perspectives on Political Education, held as part of the Ars Electronica Festival, addresses topics such as tolerance, democratic rights and social responsibility.

Across many areas of society, we are witnessing regressive developments. Hard-won progress and rights are increasingly being called into question. At the same time, extreme and in some cases anti-democratic ideologies are gaining influence. More and more often, groups of people are being pushed to the margins of society based on factors such as sexual orientation, origin or gender. Media and communication platforms play a central role in this process: the more attention exclusionary narratives receive, the more they circulate in public discourse and thus move into the mainstream.

The foundations for open and peaceful coexistence are laid in childhood and adolescence. Schools, as spaces where young people spend a significant part of their time and learn how people interact with one another, play a particularly important role. When acceptance, tolerance and democratic values are challenged, schools become places where children and young people can learn to question critically and stand up for what matters to them.

The symposium addresses, among other things, the following questions:
How can we respond to extremist views that seek to restrict the rights of others?
How can educators within the school system encourage young people to think independently and foster, within a constructive framework, a readiness for civil disobedience?


We warmly invite you to join us for engaging discussions and inspiring talks. The first 120 registered participants will also be invited to take part in a thematic guided tour of the Ars Electronica Festival.

Moderator: Elke Hackl

Description DE:
Das Symposium Perspektiven Politischer Bildung setzt sich dieses Jahr im Rahmen des Ars Electronica Festival mit Themen wie Toleranz, demokratischen Rechten und gesellschaftlicher Verantwortung auseinander.

In vielen gesellschaftlichen Bereichen lassen sich derzeit rückläufige Entwicklungen beobachten. Erreichte Fortschritte und erkämpfte Rechte werden wieder stärker infrage gestellt. Aktuell gewinnen extreme, teilweise antidemokratische Ideologien an Einfluss. Immer häufiger werden Gruppen von Menschen etwa anhand ihrer sexuellen Orientierung, ihrer Herkunft oder ihres Geschlechts an die Ränder der Gesellschaft gedrängt. Informations- und Kommunikationsmedien kommt dabei eine zentrale Rolle zu: Je mehr Medienaufmerksamkeit ausschließenden Meinungen zuteil wird, desto mehr zirkulieren diese Diskurse in der Öffentlichkeit und damit in der Mitte der Gesellschaft.

Der Grundstein für ein offenes und friedliches Miteinander wird in der Kindheit und Jugend gelegt. Dabei kommt dem Lebensraum Schule, als Ort, an dem junge Menschen einen Großteil ihrer Zeit verbringen und viel darüber lernen, wie Menschen miteinander umgehen, eine besondere Rolle zu. Wenn Akzeptanz, Toleranz und demokratische Grundwerte infrage gestellt werden, ist die Schule der Ort, an dem Kinder und Jugendliche Strategien lernen können, kritisch zu fragen und für Dinge einzustehen, die ihnen wichtig sind.

Im Symposium setzen wir uns unter anderem mit folgenden Fragen auseinander:
Wie kann auf extreme Ansichten reagiert werden, die andere Menschen und deren Rechte einschränken wollen?
Wie können Pädagog*innen im bestehenden Schulsystem den Mut von Schüler*innen zum selbstständigen Denken anregen und sie in einem konstruktiven Rahmen zu zivilem Ungehorsam motivieren?

Wir laden zu lebendigen Diskussionen und interessanten Vorträgen ein. Die ersten 120 angemeldeten Personen erhalten außerdem die Möglichkeit, an einer thematischen Führung durch das Ars Electronica Festival teilzunehmen.

Web Preview Text EN: Starting with sand, this video art work examines both the material and ideological underpinnings of digital technologies. Children playing in a sandbox is explored as a metaphor for Silicon Valley, contemplating progress, waste, responsibility, infantile destruction and the processes that shape our future.
Description EN:
Every Artificial Intelligence begins in a sand box. Starting with sand as the raw material of silicon and microchips, data processing and AI, this video art work examines both the material and ideological underpinnings of digital technologies. Young children construct castles, islands and territories, demarcate borders, negotiate ownership claims and destroy what others have created. Their games mirror the behavioral patterns of Silicon Valley: aspirations of greatness, a low frustration tolerance and the desire for permanent expansion. The oft-cited mantra “move fast and break things” signals not innovation but infantile destruction.
Documentary footage of playing children meets audio fragments drawn from technological environments and digital atmospheres. Between humor and unease, contemplation emerges in relation to issues of progress, waste and responsibility, and the processes that turn play materials into the technologies that form our present time—and the future of the children who play in it.

Jede Künstliche Intelligenz beginnt im Sandkasten. Ausgehend von Sand als Rohstoff für Silizium, Mikrochips, Datenverarbeitung und Künstliche Intelligenz untersucht diese Videoarbeit die materiellen und ideologischen Grundlagen digitaler Technologien. Kinder bauen Burgen, Inseln und Territorien, ziehen Grenzen, verhandeln Besitzansprüche und zerstören, was andere geschaffen haben. Ihre Spiele spiegeln Verhaltensmuster des Silicon Valley wider: den Anspruch auf Größe, eine geringe Frustrationstoleranz und den Drang nach ständigem Wachstum. Das oft zitierte Mantra “Move fast and break things” steht dabei weniger für Innovation als für infantile Zerstörung.
Dokumentarische Aufnahmen spielender Kinder treffen auf Klangfragmente technologischer Umgebungen – das Summen von Maschinen, digitale Klanglandschaften. Zwischen Humor und Unbehagen entsteht eine Reflexion über Fortschritt, Verschwendung und Verantwortung sowie über jene Prozesse, die aus Spielmaterial die Technologien hervorbringen, die uns prägen – und die Zukunft der Kinder, die heute darin spielen.
