Name DE: Wo ist denn der Ton versteckt?
Subtitle EN: Little Piano Builders at the C. Bechstein Centrum Linz
Subtitle DE: Kleine Klavierbauer*innen im C. Bechstein Centrum Linz
Web Preview Text EN: The C. Bechstein Centrum Linz invites children on a journey into the world of pianos and grand pianos, full of opportunities to discover, explore and try things out for themselves.
Description EN:
The C. Bechstein Centrum Linz invites children on a journey into the world of pianos, full of opportunities to discover, explore and try things out for themselves.
What does the sound of a piano string have in common with the beating wings of a bee? And how many elephants would it take to create the right tension for a piano string? Through playful experiments, children learn how a piece of wood becomes a musical instrument, how piano strings are wound and how sound is ultimately created inside a piano.
Together with experienced piano makers, they examine the individual components of a grand piano and discover the fascinating interaction of keys, hammers and strings.
Web Preview Text DE: Das C. Bechstein Centrum Linz lädt ein zu einer Reise in die Welt der Klaviere und Flügel, zum selbst Entdecken und Ausprobieren.
Description DE:
Das C. Bechstein Centrum Linz lädt Kinder zu einer Reise in die Welt der Klaviere und Flügel, zum selbst Entdecken und Ausprobieren.
Was hat der Klang einer Saite mit dem Flügelschlag einer Biene gemeinsam? Und wie viele Elefanten müsste man an einen Draht hängen, um die richtige Spannung für eine Klaviersaite zu bekommen? Spielerisch erfahren die Kinder, wie aus einem Stück Holz ein Instrument wird, wie man eine Klaviersaite wickelt und wie letztlich der Ton ins Klavier kommt.
Zusammen mit erfahrenen Klavierbauer*innen untersuchen die Kinder die Einzelteile eines Flügels und erforschen das faszinierende Zusammenspiel von Tasten, Hämmern und Saiten.

Subtitle EN: A dive into the ground below us
Web Preview Text EN: Guided by science and curiosity, this workshop will provide a sensory exploration of the vast forms of life that exist in soil in order to spark gratitude and compassion. Participants will evolve from being scientists discovering otherly beings to the soiled life itself creating and residing within the Earth’s fragile skin.
Description EN: Is soil alive? Investigating this seemingly simple question, this workshop will enable participants to discover life in the dark ground below. Evolving from scientists who experimentally search for signs of life in soil, participants will embody various forms of soiled life and artistically express their present and immanent reality. Bridging these worlds, the workshop will provide scientific and creative materials so that the complex relevance of soil can be encountered from individual angles.

Name EN: KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN: SHOW ME YOUR FACE
Artists: Johannes Pröll (AT), Mihaela Kavdanska (BG/AT), Dilmana Yordanova (BG/RO), Cornelia Lehner (AT)
Web Preview Text EN: Between genotype and phenotype unfolds a lifelong process of becoming. KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN brings together contemporary genomics, AI and art to open new perspectives on identity, human behavior and violence in particular.
Description EN: KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN explores the interplay between genetics, experience and identity, questioning deterministic views of human behavior, particularly violence. A two-channel video installation using AI, moving images, text and the sonification of genomic data makes the phenotype tangible as a process of becoming between biological potential and lived experience. The discussion features Johannes Pröll, Mika Kavdanska and Dilmana Yordanova with host Cornelia Lehner.
Web Preview Text DE: Zwischen Genotyp und Phänotyp entfaltet sich ein lebenslanger Prozess des Werdens. Der KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN verbindet aktuelle Genomforschung, KI und Kunst und eröffnet neue Perspektiven auf Identität, menschliches Verhalten und insbesondere Gewalt.
Description DE: Der KEPLER SALON EXTRA EXTERN untersucht das Wechselspiel zwischen Genetik, Erfahrung und Identität und hinterfragt deterministische Vorstellungen von menschlichem Verhalten, insbesondere Gewalt. Eine Zweikanal-Videoinstallation mit KI, Bewegtbild, Text und Sonifikation genomischer Daten macht den Phänotyp als Prozess des Werdens zwischen biologischem Potenzial und Erfahrung erfahrbar. Im Gespräch diskutieren Johannes Pröll, Mika Kavdanska und Dilmana Yordanova mit Gastgeberin Cornelia Lehner.

Web Preview Text EN: With JKU medFOCUS, the Faculty of Medicine at Johannes Kepler University Linz invites visitors to experience firsthand current developments in medicine, teaching and research.
Description EN:
The JKU MED Campus is one of the central festival hubs of the Ars Electronica Festival 2026. As a site for modern medical education, research and patient care, it demonstrates that the future does not only begin with technology and digital systems, but also with medical research and clinical practice.

With JKU medFOCUS, the Faculty of Medicine at Johannes Kepler University Linz invites visitors to experience firsthand current developments in medicine, teaching and research. At JKU medSPACE, university clinics present virtual anatomy and offer new perspectives on the heart, brain, abdomen, shoulder and eye. As part of the Best-of 3D program in JKU medSPACE, a live heart surgery broadcast directly from Kepler University Hospital will also be presented, giving visitors the chance to interact live with the surgical team. In addition, exclusive guided tours of laboratories at Kepler University Hospital provide insights into research environments where medical knowledge is created and further developed.

Another program highlight is the presentation of the Clinical Research Institute for Medical Artificial Intelligence, which demonstrates how Artificial Intelligence can contribute to the advancement of medicine. Together with other additional formats, JKU medFOCUS makes it clear that the future of healthcare emerges through the interaction of research, technology and clinical expertise with a clear focus on the human being.
Web Preview Text DE: Mit dem JKU medFOCUS lädt die Medizinische Fakultät der Johannes Kepler Universität Linz Besucher*innen dazu ein, aktuelle Entwicklungen in Medizin, Lehre und Forschung hautnah zu erleben.
Description DE:
Der JKU MED Campus ist einer der zentralen Festival-Hubs des Ars Electronica Festival 2026. Als Ort moderner medizinischer Ausbildung, Forschung und Patient*innenversorgung zeigt der JKU MED Campus, dass die Zukunft nicht nur in Technologie und digitalen Systemen “beginnt”, sondern ebenso in der medizinischen Forschung und klinischen Praxis.

Mit dem JKU medFOCUS lädt die Medizinische Fakultät der Johannes Kepler Universität Linz Besucher*innen dazu ein, aktuelle Entwicklungen in Medizin, Lehre und Forschung hautnah zu erleben. Im JKU medSPACE präsentieren Universitätskliniken virtuelle Anatomie und eröffnen neue Perspektiven auf Herz, Gehirn, Bauchraum, Schulter und Auge. Im Rahmen des Best-of-3D-Programms im JKU medSPACE wird zudem eine Live-Übertragung einer Herzoperation direkt aus dem Kepler Universitätsklinikum gezeigt, bei der die Besucher*innen live mit dem chirurgischen Team interagieren können. Exklusive Führungen durch Labore am Kepler Universitätsklinikum geben außerdem Einblicke in Forschungsumgebungen, in denen medizinisches Wissen entsteht und weiterentwickelt wird.

Ein weiterer Programmhöhepunkt ist die Präsentation des Clinical Research Institute for Medical Artificial Intelligence, das zeigt, wie Künstliche Intelligenz zur Weiterentwicklung der Medizin beitragen kann. Gemeinsam mit weiteren Formaten macht JKU medFOCUS deutlich: Die Zukunft der Gesundheitsversorgung entsteht durch das Zusammenspiel von Forschung, Technologie, klinischer Expertise und einem klaren Fokus auf den Menschen.

Web Preview Text EN: An interactive kinetic installation transforms the visitors’ arm movements into mechanical sequences. Real-time tracking controls servo-driven corkscrews, creating a direct physical response and inviting reflection on repetition and the question of control.
Description EN:
Who is Jumping, Jack? is an interactive kinetic installation that translates visitors’ arm movements into mechanical sequences. Their gestures are captured in real time and transmitted to servo-controlled corkscrews, creating an immediate physical response to their actions. The work explores how actions become embedded within systems of repetition, imitation and control. As human gestures are translated into mechanical movements, the boundary between actor and reflection, action and program, begins to dissolve. 

What initially appears to be a playful interaction actually points to the invisible mechanisms that shape behavior, assign roles and define the limits of agency. In this light, the installation can also be read in relation to the growing use of algorithmic governance and military automation. It evokes technologies in which decisions are delegated, processes become automated and responsibility is increasingly detached from those who initiate an action. The work reveals how agency is both distributed across technological systems and simultaneously obscured, prompting questions about who acts, who decides and who ultimately bears responsibility.

Die Gesten werden in Echtzeit erfasst und an servogesteuerte Korkenzieher übertragen, die unmittelbar auf die Bewegungen reagieren. Die Arbeit untersucht, wie Handlungen in Systeme der Wiederholung, Nachahmung und Kontrolle eingebunden sind.
Description DE:
Who is Jumping, Jack? ist eine interaktive kinetische Installation, die die Armbewegungen der Besucher*innen in mechanische Abläufe übersetzt. Die Gesten werden in Echtzeit erfasst und an servogesteuerte Korkenzieher übertragen, die unmittelbar auf die Bewegungen reagieren. Die Arbeit untersucht, wie Handlungen in Systeme der Wiederholung, Nachahmung und Kontrolle eingebunden sind. Durch die Übersetzung menschlicher Gesten in mechanische Bewegungen verschwimmt die Grenze zwischen Akteur und Spiegelbild, zwischen Handlung und Programm.  

Was zunächst als spielerische Interaktion erscheint, verweist auf die unsichtbaren Mechanismen, die Verhalten formen, Rollen zuweisen und Handlungsräume bestimmen. Vor diesem Hintergrund lässt sich die Installation auch im Zusammenhang mit den zunehmenden Formen algorithmischer Steuerung und militärischer Automatisierung lesen. Sie verweist auf Technologien, bei denen Entscheidungen delegiert, Prozesse automatisiert und Verantwortung zunehmend entkoppelt werden. Die Arbeit macht erfahrbar, wie Handlungsmacht in technologischen Systemen verteilt und zugleich verschleiert wird.

Description EN: Alisa Martynova’s residency at the Ars Electronica Futurelab in 2026 explores perception, consciousness and the unstable nature of truth through an immersive projection environment developed for Deep Space 8K. Drawing from studies on binocular rivalry, entropy and the default neural network, this work examines how the brain constructs reality from fragmented and ambiguous visual information. Dissonant Stereoscopy places the audience within sensory thresholds where the visual system attempts to disambiguate unstable inputs—seeing emerges from the interplay of memory, past experience and interpretation.
Web Preview Text DE: Alisa Martynovas Residency im Ars Electronica Futurelab im Jahr 2026 untersucht Wahrnehmung, Bewusstsein und die Unbeständigkeit der Wahrheit anhand einer immersiven Projektionsumgebung, die für Deep Space 8K entwickelt wurde.
Description DE: Alisa Martynovas Residency im Ars Electronica Futurelab im Jahr 2026 untersucht Wahrnehmung, Bewusstsein und die Unbeständigkeit der Wahrheit anhand einer immersiven Projektionsumgebung, die für Deep Space 8K entwickelt wurde. Ausgehend von Studien zur binokularen Rivalität, zur Entropie und zum Standard-Neuralnetzwerk untersucht das Werk, wie das Gehirn aus fragmentierten und mehrdeutigen visuellen Informationen Realität konstruiert. Durch dissonante Stereoskopie wird das Publikum in sensorische Schwellenbereiche versetzt, in denen das visuelle System versucht, unbeständige Reize zu entschlüsseln – das Sehen entsteht aus dem Zusammenspiel von Erinnerung, vergangenen Erfahrungen und Interpretation.

Subtitle DE: Immersives Hörspiel aus Turnton2047
Web Preview Text EN: A typically relaxed atmosphere fills the Medusa Bar, a popular hangout at Turnton’s harbor, on a hot September evening in 2047, until news suddenly begins to spread...
Description EN:
Since 2017, Time’s Up has been researching, developing and building Turnton2047, bringing it to life through immersive environments. At its heart is a transformed economy that prioritizes the wellbeing of people and the planet while challenging existing concentrations of wealth and power. It also explores the potential of marine regeneration to restore damaged ecosystems.
Developed in collaboration with Theater Phönix, this immersive audio experience invites audiences into the everyday lives of Turnton2047’s inhabitants. Across seven listening stations, visitors take on the role of guests at the Medusa Bar, following the story through a series of episodic scenes. With each change of seat, they are drawn deeper into this possible future, where environmental challenges coexist with a society committed to creating a good life for everyone.
Web Preview Text DE: Es herrscht diese üblich gelöste Stimmung an einem heißen Abend im September 2047 in der Medusa Bar, dem beliebten Treffpunkt im Hafen von Turnton, als plötzlich Neuigkeiten die Runde machen …
Description DE:
Seit 2017 forscht, entwickelt und baut Time’s Up an Turnton2047 und macht es in Form von immersiven Umgebungen zugänglich. Im Zentrum dieser erfahrbaren Zukunft stehen einerseits eine transformierte Wirtschaft, die das Wohlergehen der Menschen und des Planeten in den Vordergrund rückt und damit aktuell vorherrschende Macht- und Vermögenskonzentrationen konterkariert, und andererseits die Potentiale mariner Regeneration, die geeignet sind, beschädigte Meeres-Ökosysteme wiederherzustellen. 
Mit dem Theater Phönix wurde nun ein neues Hörspielformat entwickelt. An sieben abwechselnden Stationen schlüpfen die Besucher*innen in die Rolle der Gäst*innen der Medusabar und verfolgen jeweils in einem Ausschnitt von etwa acht Minuten die Ereignisse. Mit jedem Sitzplatzwechsel taucht das Publikum tiefer in die Erzählung von Turnton2047 ein. Die Kulisse der Bar und die ebenfalls aufliegende Wochenzeitung Turnton Gazette bieten weitere Möglichkeiten, um sich in dieser möglichen Zukunft zu orientieren.

Web Preview Text EN: The Expanded – Conference on Animation and Interactive Art explores the expanding boundaries of animation across artistic, technological and scientific disciplines. Description EN:
The https://expanded-conf.org/ explores the expanding boundaries of animation across artistic, technological and scientific disciplines. Since 2024, Expanded has been organized as an international peer-reviewed conference featuring a call for scientific and artistic papers and the publication of conference proceedings. 
Alongside the established Research Papers and Art Papers tracks, two new tracks have been introduced for the 2026 edition: the Doctoral Consortium, providing an international forum for doctoral researchers to discuss and refine their work, and the Expanded Play Gallery, combining a peer-reviewed short paper with an exhibition presented at Atelierhaus Salzamt. This format strengthens the connection between academic publication and artistic presentation while fostering dialogue between researchers, artists and festival audiences. 
The academic program is complemented by a summer school at the University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria, Hagenberg Campus and a series of curated panels that bring together internationally recognized artists, researchers and practitioners.

Description EN: The exhibition Negotiating the Real – The Desire to Believe asks which systems of belief and worldviews underpin our social order—and, in turn, shape our understanding of what it means to be human. Christl Baur, Head of the Ars Electronica Festival and Program Director, takes you on a tour along the FESTIVAL WALK. Together, you explore the thematical threads of the exhibition across its different venues in the heart of Linz.
Web Preview Text DE: Die Ausstellung Negotiating the Real – The Desire to Believe geht der Frage nach, welche Glaubenssysteme und Weltanschauungen unserer gesellschaftlichen Ordnung zugrunde liegen – und damit wiederum unser Verständnis davon prägen, was es bedeutet, Mensch zu sein.
Description DE:
Die Ausstellung Negotiating the Real – The Desire to Believe geht der Frage nach, welche Glaubenssysteme und Weltanschauungen unserer gesellschaftlichen Ordnung zugrunde liegen – und damit wiederum unser Verständnis davon prägen, was es bedeutet, Mensch zu sein.
Begleite Christl Baur, Leiterin des Ars Electronica Festivals und Programmdirektorin, auf einem Rundgang entlang des FESTIVAL WALK. Gemeinsam erkunden wir die thematischen Aspekte der Ausstellung an ihren verschiedenen Veranstaltungsorten im Herzen von Linz.

Name EN: Spotlight Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real (DE/Austrian Sign Language)
Name DE: Spotlight Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Negotiating the Real (DE/Gebärdensprache)
Web Preview Text EN: How do we negotiate reality? How does community form, both among us humans and with other living beings? What systems of belief shape the conflicts we face in this process and what role does technology play?
Description EN: How do we negotiate reality? How does community form, both among us humans and with other living beings? What systems of belief shape the conflicts we face in this process and what role does technology play? This guided tour takes you on a journey along the FESTIVAL WALK through the heart of Linz visiting a school, a museum, a hospital and several churches, connecting infrastructures of our daily life with artistic projects.
Web Preview Text DE: Wie verhandeln wir Wirklichkeit? Wie entsteht Gemeinschaft – unter uns Menschen und mit anderen Lebewesen? Welche Glaubenssysteme prägen die Konflikte, mit denen wir in diesem Aushandlungsprozess konfrontiert sind? Und welche Rolle spielt dabei die Technologie?
Description DE: Wie verhandeln wir Wirklichkeit? Wie entsteht Gemeinschaft – unter uns Menschen und mit anderen Lebewesen? Welche Glaubenssysteme prägen die Konflikte, mit denen wir in diesem Aushandlungsprozess konfrontiert sind? Und welche Rolle spielt dabei die Technologie? Diese Tour führt dich entlang des FESTIVAL WALK in der Linzer Innenstadt. Wir besuchen unterschiedlichste Orte – darunter eine Schule, ein Museum, ein Krankenhaus sowie Kirchen – und erkunden dabei, wie die Infrastruktur unseres Alltags mit künstlerischen Projekten verbunden ist.

Artists: Deep Space Community (INT),  Ars Electronica Solutions (AT)
Web Preview Text EN: Members of the global Deep Space Community share insights into their current projects and show how ideas become immersive experiences—from interactive applications and stereoscopic 3D experiences to entirely new formats.
Description EN:
Deep Space is an open platform, and its possibilities grow through the people who create for it. This session brings together members of the global Deep Space Community to present what they are currently developing—from interactive applications and stereoscopic 3D experiences to video productions and entirely new formats.
The projects span science communication, art and cultural heritage, medicine and biology and the future of education. Each offers a different perspective on what immersive space can do and who it can reach. Beyond the finished results, participants share the processes behind them: how an initial idea becomes an immersive story, how creative and technical decisions shape the experience and how concepts are developed, tested and implemented. A practical look at what becomes possible when a community builds, experiments and learns together.
Web Preview Text DE: Mitglieder der globalen Deep Space Community geben Einblicke in aktuelle Projekte und zeigen, wie aus Ideen immersive Erlebnisse entstehen – von interaktiven Anwendungen und stereoskopischen 3D-Erfahrungen bis hin zu völlig neuen Formaten.
Description DE:
Deep Space ist eine offene Plattform, deren Möglichkeiten mit den Menschen wachsen, die für sie neue Inhalte und Anwendungen entwickeln. Diese Session bringt Mitglieder der globalen Deep Space Community zusammen, die präsentieren, woran sie aktuell arbeiten – von interaktiven Anwendungen und stereoskopischen 3D-Erlebnissen über Videoproduktionen bis hin zu völlig neuen Formaten.
Die Projekte reichen von Wissenschaftskommunikation über Kunst und kulturelles Erbe bis hin zu Medizin, Biologie und der Zukunft der Bildung. Jedes Projekt eröffnet eine andere Perspektive darauf, was ein immersiver Raum leisten kann und welche Zielgruppen er erreichen kann. Über die fertigen Ergebnisse hinaus geben die Teilnehmer*innen Einblicke in die Prozesse dahinter: wie aus einer ersten Idee eine immersive Geschichte entsteht, wie kreative und technische Entscheidungen das Erlebnis prägen und wie Konzepte entwickelt, getestet und umgesetzt werden. Ein praxisnaher Einblick in die Möglichkeiten, die entstehen, wenn eine Community gemeinsam entwickelt, experimentiert und voneinander lernt.

Subtitle DE: Neue digitale Ansätze für Linz und das Ars Electronica Festival
Web Preview Text EN: On September 11 and 12, 2026, young talents will team up for a two-day AI hackathon at the Ars Electronica Festival, developing creative digital projects with festival data and open data from the City of Linz—all with the goal of experiencing Linz and the festival in exciting new ways.
Description EN:
On September 11 and 12, 2026, students and young talents aged 14 and up will develop digital projects using festival data and open data from the City of Linz at the AI Hackathon.

We are looking for approaches that open up new perspectives on the city and the festival—from smart guides and interactive maps to storytelling tools, artistic projects or completely new ideas. No coding experience is required. AI tools and experienced mentors will support participants in testing out their ideas, developing them further and turning them into concrete projects. Individuals and teams are both welcome to take part. At the end, teams will present their projects in short pitches.

An expert jury will select the winning projects, which will be honored at the Award Ceremony on Sunday, September 13, 2026. The best teams can look forward to prizes, and the winning project will receive support for further development and implementation.
Web Preview Text DE: Am 11. und 12. September 2026 entwickeln junge Talente beim zweitägigen KI-Hackathon im Rahmen des Ars Electronica Festivals kreative digitale Projekte mit Festivaldaten und offenen Daten der Stadt Linz – mit dem Ziel, Linz und das Festival neu erlebbar zu machen.
Description DE:
Am 11. und 12. September 2026 entwickeln Schüler*innen, Studierende und junge Talente ab 14 Jahren beim KI-Hackathon digitale Projekte mit Festivaldaten und Open Data der Stadt Linz. Gesucht sind Ansätze, die neue Perspektiven auf die Stadt und das Festival eröffnen — vom smarten Guide über interaktive Karten und Storytelling-Tools bis hin zu künstlerischen Projekten oder ganz neuen Ideen.

Coding-Erfahrung ist keine Voraussetzung. KI-Tools und erfahrene Mentor*innen unterstützen die Teilnehmenden dabei, ihre Ideen auszuprobieren, weiterzuentwickeln und in konkrete Projekte zu übersetzen. Teilnehmen können Einzelpersonen oder Teams. Zum Abschluss haben die Teams die Möglichkeit ihre Projekte in kurzen Pitches zu präsentieren. 

Ein Community-Voting wählt die Gewinnerprojekte aus, die bei der Award Ceremony am Samstag, 12. September 2026, direkt im Anschluss an den Hackathon in der Grand Garage, gekürt werden. Auf die besten Teams warten Sachpreise, und das Siegerprojekt wird bei der Weiterentwicklung und Umsetzung unterstützt.

Description EN: Protect Our Planet and Climate—a Science Experience by Ars Electronica Solutions and the European Space Agency. Over the course of 30 minutes, we will cover a variety of topics from our home planet to planetary defence: Earth observation and climate data reveal our planet’s current state, ESA satellites deliver the facts and the Hera mission provides the platform for an important conversation about how we defend ourselves against asteroids. Artists: Hakuhodo Inc. (JP), Hakuhodo Inc. Sei-katsu-sha insight R&D Institute (JP), Ars Electronica Futurelab (AT)
Web Preview Text EN: Hello Futures Manifesto is an interactive installation that turns personal visions of the future into vivid posters—a collective manifesto, making futures tangible, shareable and open to negotiation. The work explores how generative AI can support open dialogue and civic participation.
Description EN:
Hello Futures Manifesto is an interactive installation that turns personal visions of the future into vivid posters. Each poster becomes part of a collective manifesto, making futures tangible, shareable and open to negotiation. As third iteration of Citizen Manifesto by Ars Electronica Futurelab and Hakuhodo Inc., the work explores how generative AI can support open dialogue, civic participation and collective creativity. 
As a satellite installation of the Open Futurelab, it connects to the questions of negotiating humanity in Futurelab’s new exhibition Hello Worlds!. Participants discuss what kind of humanity we want to become, and what responsibilities arise as AI increasingly influences society. The conversations are recorded, transcribed, summarized and transformed into posters with generative AI. 
The work invites dialogue, showing that the future is not a fixed prediction, but a shared process shaped through encounter, collaboration and negotiation.
Web Preview Text DE: Hello Futures Manifesto ist eine interaktive Installation, die persönliche Zukunftsvisionen in lebendige Plakate verwandelt – ein kollektives Manifest, das Zukünfte greifbar, teilbar und verhandelbar macht. Die Arbeit untersucht, wie generative KI offenen Dialog und Teilhabe unterstützen kann.
Description DE:
Hello Futures Manifesto ist eine interaktive Installation, die persönliche Zukunftsvisionen in lebendige Poster verwandelt. Jedes Poster wird Teil eines kollektiven Manifests, das Zukünfte greifbar, teilbar und verhandelbar macht. Als dritte Iteration des Citizen Manifesto von Ars Electronica Futurelab und Hakuhodo Inc. untersucht die Arbeit, wie generative KI offenen Dialog, Teilhabe und kollektive Kreativität unterstützen kann.
Vom Hauptplatz Linz aus verknüpft das Hello Futures Manifesto das Herz der Stadt mit dem Open Futurelab und der neuen Futurelab-Ausstellung Hello Worlds!. Die Teilnehmenden diskutieren, welche Art von Menschheit wir anstreben und welche Verantwortung sich durch den zunehmenden Einfluss von KI auf die Gesellschaft ergibt. Die Gespräche werden transkribiert, zusammengefasst und mithilfe generativer KI in Plakate verwandelt. 
Das Werk lädt zum Dialog ein und zeigt, dass die Zukunft keine feste Vorhersage ist, sondern ein gemeinsamer Prozess.

Web Preview Text EN: The Flood the Zone with Courage program presents a series of interventions, each lasting no more than seven minutes. Through diverse artistic approaches, these interventions reimagine protest, exploring the many forms it can take and inviting audiences into concentrated moments of action.
Description EN: The Flood the Zone with Courage program presents a series of interventions, each lasting no more than seven minutes. Through diverse artistic approaches, these interventions reimagine protest, exploring the many forms it can take and inviting audiences into concentrated moments of action that continuously shift in both form and intensity. This year’s program explores many of the challenges that shape our everyday lives. Some interventions respond to the climate crisis and explore how technological and social developments shape the way we perceive the world. Others explore the relationship between the body and the social gaze, while several focus on practices of collectiveness and the ways we come together in public space. Taking place entirely outdoors in Linz’s Main Square, the festival transforms one of the city’s central public spaces into a platform for civic imagination, exchange and collective courage.
Web Preview Text DE: Das Programm Flood the Zone with Courage präsentiert eine Reihe von Interventionen, die jeweils nicht länger als sieben Minuten dauern. Mit vielfältigen künstlerischen Zugängen denken sie Protest neu und laden das Publikum zu konzentrierten Momenten des Handelns ein.
Description DE: Das Programm Flood the Zone with Courage präsentiert eine Reihe von Interventionen, die jeweils nicht länger als sieben Minuten dauern. Mit vielfältigen künstlerischen Zugängen denken sie Protest neu und laden das Publikum zu konzentrierten Momenten des Handelns ein, die sich in Form und Intensität ständig verändern. Das diesjährige Programm beleuchtet zentrale Herausforderungen, die unseren Alltag prägen. Manche Interventionen reagieren auf die Klimakrise und untersuchen, wie technologische und gesellschaftliche Entwicklungen unsere Wahrnehmung der Welt prägen. Andere widmen sich dem Verhältnis von Körper und gesellschaftlichem Blick, während mehrere Arbeiten Praktiken des Kollektiven und Formen des Zusammenkommens im öffentlichen Raum ins Zentrum stellen. Das Programm findet zur Gänze im Freien am Linzer Hauptplatz statt und verwandelt einen zentralen öffentlichen Raum der Stadt in eine Plattform für zivilgesellschaftliche Vorstellungskraft, Austausch und kollektiven Mut.

Name EN: Glitch & Leak: Overflowing Bodies in Public Space at Main Square
Artists: FIFTITU% Vernetzungsstelle für Frauen* in Kunst und Kultur in OÖ (AT)
Web Preview Text EN: Glitch & Leak is an invitation to open up a space together: a space of disruption, permeability, collective imagination and transformation. It uses disruption and leakage to collectively imagine how public space could be transformed.
Description EN:
Glitch & Leak is an invitation to open up a space together: a space of disruption, permeability, collective imagination and transformation. The glitch is not an error in the system, but a strategy of resistance—a way of interrupting established patterns and creating openings for other possibilities.
These patterns are also embedded in public space. Public space is never neutral. It is shaped by social, political and economic power relations, which determine who can access it, how it can be used and whose presence is welcomed or excluded. Glitch & Leak uses disruption and leakage as ways to make these structures visible, to unsettle them and to collectively imagine how public space could be transformed.
Web Preview Text DE: Glitch & Leak ist eine Einladung, gemeinsam einen Raum zu öffnen: einen Raum der Störung, der Durchlässigkeit, der kollektiven Imagination und der Transformation.
Description DE:
Glitch & Leak ist eine Einladung, gemeinsam einen Raum zu öffnen: einen Raum der Störung, der Durchlässigkeit, der kollektiven Imagination und der Transformation. Der Glitch ist kein Fehler im System, sondern eine Strategie des Widerstands – er unterbricht etablierte Muster und schafft Öffnungen für anderes.
Diese Muster sind auch dem öffentlichen Raum eingeschrieben. Öffentlicher Raum ist nie neutral. Er wird von gesellschaftlichen, politischen und ökonomischen Machtverhältnissen geformt, die bestimmen, wer Zugang hat, wie er genutzt werden kann und wessen Anwesenheit willkommen ist und wessen ausgeschlossen wird. Glitch & Leak arbeitet mit Störung und Durchsickern, um diese Strukturen sichtbar zu machen, sie zu irritieren und gemeinsam zu entwerfen, wie öffentlicher Raum verändert werden könnte.

Name EN: Listen To Each Oida: Dalia Ahmed
Web Preview Text EN: FM4, the Austrian public broadcaster ORF’s radio station for young audiences, connects social discourse with pop culture. Music at the close of each of the two festival days carries the themes discussed throughout the day—democracy, courage and the culture of conflict.
Description EN:
FM4, the Austrian public broadcaster ORF’s radio station for young audiences, connects social discourse with pop culture. Music at the close of each of the two festival days carries the themes discussed throughout the day—democracy, courage, the culture of conflict—into a pop-cultural format: music has historically been a central medium of protest, and here it is both reflected upon and celebrated. The main square thus remains an open space of encounter into the evening, where social dialogue and shared experience come together.

Dalia Ahmed is a DJ, radio host and music editor at Radio FM4, where she presents Dalia’s Late Night Lemonade every Saturday night. A show dedicated to house, techno and many different global club sounds.
Web Preview Text DE: FM4, das junge Radio des ORF, verbindet gesellschaftlichen Diskurs mit Popkultur. Musik zum Abschluss der beiden Veranstaltungstage überführt die zuvor diskutierten Themen – Demokratie, Mut, Konfliktkultur – in ein popkulturelles Format.
Description DE:
FM4, das junge Radio des ORF, verbindet gesellschaftlichen Diskurs mit Popkultur. Musik zum Abschluss der beiden Veranstaltungstage überführt die zuvor diskutierten Themen – Demokratie, Mut, Konfliktkultur – in ein popkulturelles Format: Musik ist historisch ein zentrales Medium des Protests und wird hier zugleich reflektiert und gefeiert. Der Hauptplatz bleibt so bis in den Abend ein offener Ort der Begegnung, an dem gesellschaftlicher Dialog und gemeinsames Erleben verbunden werden.

Dalia Ahmed ist DJ, Radio Moderatorin und Musikjournalistin bei Radio FM4, wo sie jede Samstag Nacht Techno, House und unterschiedliche globale Club Sounds in Dalia’s Late Night Lemonade präsentiert.

Artists: Sofie Burgos-Thorsen (DK), Andreas Refsgaard (DK), Anna Minta (DE), Bernd Ziegler (DE)
Web Preview Text EN: Wicked Mirror confronts visitors with an AI-generated version of themselves that argues the opposite position. Together with the artists, researchers of the Catholic Private University Linz discuss how AI transforms identity, empathy and democratic dialogue—and what it means to negotiate with ourselves in the age of Artificial Intelligence.
Description EN: Wicked Mirror transforms public debate into an encounter with one’s AI-generated double. A photorealistic clone adopts the visitor’s face, voice and arguments—only to challenge them. In conversation with the artists, researchers of the Catholic Private University Linz explore how AI reshapes identity, empathy and democratic dialogue. From the perspectives of art history and theology, they ask how aesthetic experience can foster reflection, disagreement and new ways of negotiating what it means to be human in an increasingly AI-mediated world.

Name EN: Robertina Šebjanič – Journal from the TARA expedition vessel: Echoes of the Abyss
Artists: Robertina Šebjanič (SI), Ilaria Hoppe (DE), Martin Koci (CZ)
Web Preview Text EN: Echoes of the Abyss explores the hidden legacy of chemical weapons dumped in the ocean. Based on the artist’s Baltic Sea research, the talk examines how artistic practice reveals ecological threats and creates new perspectives on the links between science, history and environmental destruction.
Description EN: Echoes of the Abyss addresses the overlooked issue of chemical weapons dumped on the ocean floor. These remnants of past conflicts threaten biodiversity, alter water chemistry and act as environmental time bombs. Based on research conducted during the artist’s expedition with the Tara Ocean Foundation in the Baltic Sea, the talk hosted by researchers from the Catholic Private University Linz explores the intersection of artistic research, marine science, history and ecological destruction.
Web Preview Text DE: Echoes of the Abyss erkundet die verborgenen Altlasten von im Meer versenkten chemischen Waffen. Ausgehend von Forschungen in der Ostsee beleuchtet der Vortrag, wie künstlerische Praxis ökologische Bedrohungen sichtbar macht und neue Perspektiven auf die Verbindungen zwischen Wissenschaft, Geschichte und Umweltzerstörung eröffnet.
Description DE: Echoes of the Abyss widmet sich dem oft übersehenen Problem chemischer Waffen auf dem Meeresgrund. Diese Überreste vergangener Konflikte bedrohen die Biodiversität, verändern die Wasserchemie und wirken wie ökologische Zeitbomben. Ausgehend von einer Ostsee-Expedition mit der Tara Ocean Foundation untersucht der von Forscher*innen der Katholischen Privat-Universität Linz organisierte Vortrag das Zusammenspiel von künstlerischer Forschung, Meereswissenschaft, Geschichte und ökologischer Zerstörung.

Name EN: Expert Tour FESTIVAL WALK: Elisabeth Falkensteiner (EN)
Web Preview Text EN: The FESTIVAL WALK exhibition tour takes visitors to eight different locations around OK Platz in Linz, guided by co-curator Elisabeth Falkensteiner.
Description EN: Join co-curator of the FESTIVAL WALK Elisabeth Falkensteiner for a guided tour. Subtitle DE: Dualistisches Denken erweitern
Web Preview Text EN: How can we design new technologies that transcend towards pluralistic intention, agency and outcome within a broader biological perspective? Yamaha Motor and Ars Electronica Futurelab explore the future of relationships between humans and machines as living systems.
Description EN:
How can biological plurality challenge and expand dualistic thinking? 
Yamaha Motor and Ars Electronica Futurelab explore the future of relationships between humans and machines as living systems. We present early outcomes of our collaboration since April 2026.
In conventional machine thinking, we think of switching as a dualistic concept, on and off, 0 and 1, useful and useless, natural and artificial. Yet living systems and nature do not operate solely within fixed boundaries. There is more in the in-between. How can we design new technologies that transcend towards pluralistic intention, agency and outcome within a broader biological perspective?  
Art, like nature, holds contradiction, imperfection, partial states, and open questions as productive conditions rather than problems to solve. The project promotes public discourse on how technologies are designed and engages with the ethical concerns around current technological innovation.
Web Preview Text DE: Wie können wir neue Technologien entwickeln, die in einer breiten biologischen Perspektive zu pluralistischer Intention, Handlungsfähigkeit und Ergebnissen führen? Description DE: Wie kann biologische Pluralität dualistisches Denken hinterfragen und erweitern? Yamaha Motor und Ars Electronica Futurelab erforschen die Zukunft der Beziehungen zwischen Mensch und Maschine als lebende Systeme. Wir präsentieren erste Ergebnisse unserer seit April 2026 bestehenden Zusammenarbeit. Im konventionellen maschinellen Denken betrachten wir das Schalten als dualistisches Konzept, an und aus, 0 und 1. Doch lebende Systeme und Natur funktionieren nicht nur innerhalb fester Grenzen. Wie können wir neue Technologien entwerfen, die im Rahmen einer umfassenderen biologischen Perspektive zu pluralistischen Absichten, Handlungsmöglichkeiten und Ergebnissen führen? Die Kunst betrachtet – wie die Natur – Widersprüche, Unvollkommenheit, Teilzustände und offene Fragen als produktive Bedingungen statt als Probleme. Das Projekt fördert den öffentlichen Diskurs darüber, wie Technologien gestaltet werden, und setzt sich mit den ethischen Bedenken auseinander, die mit aktuellen technologischen Innovationen einhergehen.

Web Preview Text EN: The Academic Session: Research Papers presents six contributions selected through the Expanded Conference Open Call.
Description EN:
The Academic Session: Research Papers presents six contributions selected through the Expanded Conference Open Call. Following a rigorous peer-review process, the Research Papers highlight artistic research, experimental methodologies and critical perspectives on expanded animation and interactive art. Each speaker will give a 15-minute presentation of their work.

16:30-16:45
XR Meets the Performing Arts: LED Wall Laboratories at the Intersection of Theatre and Virtual Production

This paper presents an interdisciplinary curriculum framework—the LED Wall Lab (LWL)—designed to integrate Extended Reality (XR) technologies into performing arts education through structured collaboration between a school of performing arts and a partner film school. We argue that this integration produces artistically and pedagogically distinct outcomes that neither discipline achieves alone, provided that the performer’s body remains the central dramaturgical force around which digital media is organized. Over three iterations of the workshop (2023–2026), interdisciplinary student teams composed of acting, directing, dramaturgy and media production students developed more than 15 performances employing LED walls as interactive scenographic environments. The paper discusses a notable case study in inclusive performance involving a non-sighted performer. The findings suggest that XR technologie —particularly when embedded in real-time, improvisational workflows characteristic of the performing arts—offer a productive site for rethinking the relationship between embodied performance and digital scenography. Ilja Mirsky (DE)

16:45-17:00
The Extractive Image-World: Artistic Counter-Practices in Gaussian Splatting, NeRFs, and Volumetric Machine Vision.

This paper examines probabilistic spatial images as an extractive media formation and asks how artists and critical practitioners make that formation visible. It focuses on navigable image-worlds produced through Gaussian splats, neural radiance fields, point clouds and related volumetric machine-vision techniques. The paper develops a media-archaeological reading through Jussi Parikka’s operational images, Brooke Belisle’s depth effects, and scholarship on media ecology, digital materiality and environmental violence. It surveys artistic counter-practices by John Gerrard, Ars Electronica Futurelab, ScanLAB Projects, Forensic Architecture and Morehshin Allahyari that expose the mechanics and environmental conditions of volumetric capture. These practices challenge the fantasy of neutral “reality capture” by revealing scanner agency, evidentiary uncertainty, cultural extraction and infrastructural costs. The paper argues that probabilistic spatial images are extractive image-worlds, dependent on energy, minerals, data centres, water, hardware and waste. Tom Milnes (UK)

17:00-17:15
Generative Artificial Intelligence for Non-Representational Art: LoRA-Based Style Learning on FLUX

This paper investigates whether generative AI can learn and reproduce the stylistic identity of a single non-representational abstract artist. The FLUX model was adapted using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and trained on a curated corpus of 127 abstract artworks with an LLM-assisted, artist-grounded annotation pipeline. The model was deployed in a public exhibition, where visitors generated artworks interactively and participated in a perceptual study comparing AI-generated images with human-made originals. The system was evaluated through quantitative style-similarity metrics, public perception and qualitative artist assessment. The LoRA-adapted model outperformed non-finetuned baselines on perceptual style-similarity measures, while annotation ablation confirmed that artist-grounded captions improved the precision and coverage of the learned style distribution. Audience discrimination did not significantly exceed chance level, while the artist identified differences in material process and surface quality. The findings suggest that generative AI can capture visual style while remaining limited in reproducing the material and process-oriented conditions of artistic production. Jan Tietz (DE), Niklas Beuter (DE), Abdulaziz Alhamadani (US)

17:15 - 17:30
Feel.Back.Loop: Affective Co-Adaptation between Humans and Embodied Intelligent Systems through Reinforcement Learning

Feel.Back.Loop is a robotic tail that learns from human emotion. Drawing on the animal tail as a metaphor for non-verbal communication, the work uses affective computing and reinforcement learning to read facial expressions in real time and uses detected affect as a reward signal to continuously evolve its movement behavior, developing through interaction a movement language that was never explicitly authored. This talk presents the conceptual framework, technical architecture and interaction dynamics of the installation, drawing on observations from its presentation at Ars Electronica Festival 2025 and a structured user study. The subjects of focus are the system's exploration-exploitation balance, its role in shaping the character of the human-machine relationship, and the kinds of affective bonds that emerge when participants encounter an autonomous system that moves like a living organism without being one. The work is situated within broader questions about empathy, agency and what it means to form a bond with an intelligent system that adapts through encounter. Ghazal Hosseini (IR/AT)

17:30-17:45
Empowering Marginalized Narratives through Pixel Art. A Case Study of The Video Game of My Life and the Metzineres Association

The Video Game of My Life is a project merging video games, digital art and social activism. It was selected for the sixth edition of the Simfonies de Ciutat (City Symphonies) program, that stems from a collaboration between the association of women in media (Dones Visuals) and the CCCB (Barcelona Contemporary Culture Center). This 10–15-minute piece utilizes a 1980s arcade aesthetic to visualize the dissident experiences of “womxn,” specifically those facing homelessness and addiction in Barcelona’s Raval neighborhood. In a landscape strained by gentrification and tourism, the project grants agency to individuals often rendered invisible by society. Rooted in Barcelona province, The Video Game of My Life hit the program’s criteria for novelty and visually challenging narratives by introducing underrepresented imageries. By translating lived survival into a creative medium, the project confronts the harsh realities of drug use and urban displacement through an artistic lens focused on social justice. Maria Pagès (ES), Nea Ehrlich (ES), Ruben Tous (ES) and Lasse Loepfe (ES)

17:45-18:00
From Screen to Space: Rethinking How Interactive Markers Reshape Physical–Digital Interaction in AR Games

Screen-centric interaction remains a persistent challenge in mobile Augmented Reality (AR) games, where prolonged on-screen engagement often limits tangible interaction and spatial forms of play. This talk investigates interactive markers as a design mechanism for interrupting continuous screen use by reallocating the locus of engagement from on-screen interaction to tangible, spatial construction. Through an exploratory qualitative study with 12 participants, we examined how players interact with physical markers during AR gameplay. The findings show that interactive markers shift gameplay between physical construction and brief scanning, encouraging off-screen interaction and revealing diverse digital literacy and sequential workflows. These findings contribute design insights for mobile AR games by demonstrating how interactive markers can structure spatial and tangible play while regulating screen-centric interaction. Vinaya Tawde (CZ)

Web Preview Text EN: Mario von Rickenbach, Simon Christen and Sputniko! explore the intersections of animation, technology and society. From interactive games and Pixar’s character animation to speculative design and women’s health, they talk about creative processes, industry experiences and how artistic practices can evolve into meaningful social innovation.
Description EN:
10:00 - 10:30  16 Years of Interactive Animation
Mario von Rickenbach will give insights into different aspects of his work, including his collaborations at Playables and his latest game Pocket Boss. For 16 years, he has been exploring the field of video games through the lens of interactive animation. He will share insights about the design and development process and the unpredictable reality of releasing his projects on commercial video game distribution channels.

10:30 - 11:00 Pixar Alchemy - Animating authentic characters
Simon Christen will share his journey and experiences at Pixar, offering a behind-the-scenes look at the creativity and culture that shape the studio, along with a glimpse into life on the Pixar campus. He will also walk through his process of bringing scenes to life as a character animator, from first ideas to final performance. He will share stories from productions like Ratatouille, Coco and Elio, along with lessons learned from balancing craft, technology and storytelling. A candid look at what it is really like to animate at Pixar.

11:00 - 11:30 From the Menstruation Machine to Cradle - Japan’s Largest Workplace Women's Health Platform
Sputniko! will trace her journey from design as inquiry to social implementation, exploring how her practice has addressed the invisibility of menstruation and other bodily experiences. She will discuss works including Menstruation Machine (2010), a wearable device making menstrual pain experienceable by anyone, and Menstrualverse (2022), which explored menstrual blood in virtual worlds and was subsequently censored. She will also reflect on founding Cradle in 2020, a corporate platform addressing menstruation, menopause, and fertility, now adopted by more than 90 major Japanese companies and reaching nearly one million employees. The talk considers how speculative design can move from critical inquiry toward tangible social change.

Artists: Ryat Yezbick (US), Veneta Androva (BG), Andrew Herzog (US)
Web Preview Text EN: Andrew Herzog, Golden Nica winner, and Honorary Mention recipients Ryat Yezbick and Veneta Androva share insights into their artistic practices, offering a glimpse beyond the works recognized in the New Animation Art category of Prix Ars Electronica 2026.
Description EN:
11:30 - 12:00 God was my first encounter with surveillance technologies
Ryat Yezbick discusses their interdisciplinary practice spanning experimental documentary, performance, archival methods and emerging technologies. Trained in cultural anthropology and studio art, Yezbick explores how technologies shape perception, memory and social life. Their work examines surveillance as both technological infrastructure and a system of belief that influences collective memory and the politics of witnessing. Through selected artworks, Yezbick will reflect on images as sites of evidence, uncertainty and resistance, asking how we determine what is true and what remains beyond visibility.

12:00 - 12:30 Speculative Evidence: Construction as Documentary Practice
Veneta Androva reflects on an artistic practice that uses construction as a documentary method for investigating realities that resist direct observation. She approaches animation, game engines and digital environments as research tools for examining political, technological and social infrastructures. Combining archival research, found materials, digital assets and speculative narration, her work constructs documentary experiences that engage with realities beyond direct observation. Construction becomes both an aesthetic and epistemological strategy for producing speculative evidence of increasingly mediated and algorithmic realities.

12:30 - 13:00 Human Nature
Andrew Herzog talks about his medium-agnostic practice, which examines the constructed boundaries between humanity and the natural world, utilizing nature as subject, setting, material and collaborator. His work considers the systems, technologies and narratives through which humans understand, organize and often assert their place in the world. His experiences as a father and caregiver have brought greater focus to the ways masculinity shapes these assertions. These inquiries extend to questions of lineage, inheritance,and responsibility, as he explores the Anthropocene as both a condition of ecological transformation and a reflection of the human impulse to separate, categorize and control.

Web Preview Text EN: ASIFA Austria Forum: Current Perspectives brings together artists 2girls1comp, Claudia Larcher and Hisko Hulsing to discuss contemporary animation practices, exploring game hacking, ecological mourning, generative AI, political storytelling and new approaches to image-making.
Description EN:
14:30 - 15:00 The Game Was Rigged From the Start
2girls1comp shares an insight into their practice in the form of a lecture performance. While navigating the world of Grand Theft Auto V, one of the best selling video games in history, they will showcase how they hack, change and reclaim the software of popular AAA computer games.

15:00 - 15:30 No applause, no life, no pain.
Claudia Larcher presents two of her films, both on view in her solo exhibition No applause, no life, no pain. at the Francisco Carolinum Linz: The End and Extinction Story. Both works connect narratives of ecological mourning with questions about the future of cinema and image production in the age of generative AI. Extinction Story departs from the inherited bird egg collection of the artist's grandfather, addressing species extinction, loss and the materiality of the photographic archive, thereby turning it into a reflection on disappearance and the conditions of future image-making. The End continues this inquiry and condenses it into a posthumanist vanitas, in which images, bodies and environments appear as fragile constellations.

15:30 - 16:00 Danse Macabre – a warning against fascism
Hisko Hulsing presents Danse Macabre, a short animated film about the rise of fascism and the absurdity of war, based on the Allegro from Shostakovich's 10th Symphony. Hulsing began the project in 2014, following Russia's invasion of Crimea and the rise of increasingly dangerous populism worldwide. He will discuss the film's historical and political roots, as well as its production, which combines oil paintings, 3D animation in Blender and Houdini, AI-assisted style transfers using ComfyUI, and 2D animation in TVPaint.
