Web Preview Text EN: The Academic Session #1 Art Track: Archive presents five contributions from the Expanded Conference Open Call that explore how digital and immersive technologies can engage with archives, cultural heritage, memory and histories in transformation.
Description EN:
The Academic Session #1 Art Track: Archive presents five contributions from the Expanded Conference Open Call that explore how digital and immersive technologies can engage with archives, cultural heritage, memory and histories in transformation.

11:30 - 11:45
Lineage Canvas: Productive Friction in Born-Digital Heritage

What does it mean to generate something with cultural meaning when the source has its own history, restrictions and conditions for use? Lineage Canvas is a browser-based generative artwork that does not train a model on Indigenous textile patterns. Instead, it uses explicit construction grammars, acoustic context and governance conditions drawn from Taiwanese Atayal, Rukai and Paiwan textile knowledge. Visitors must recognize, negotiate and commit to a lineage before any artifact can be generated. Each output inherits visible relations from its sources, keeping origin, transformation and restriction legible. Refusal is part of the work: incomplete or restricted lineage can delay, constrain or stop generation, making silence and interruption part of the artwork. The talk introduces Productive Friction as a framework for born-digital heritage, where consent, attribution and care are embedded in the interaction rather than left to policy. It situates the work against the frictionless paradigm of contemporary generative tools.

Shih-Wen Huang (TW)
11:45-12:00
Interrupted Chronologies: Pseudo-Code Histories on Ceramic Vessels

Viewing history as an ongoing process of interruption, this installation moves away from finished narratives. Python-like code replaces natural language to frame civilization as executable logic rather than a linear story. Cultural transcoding occurs as symbols rearrange themselves across screens, ceramic vessels and computational structures. Friction between code and audience interference reshapes these myths. Words or noise from viewers act as disruptions, forcing the system to keep running under unstable conditions rather than following commands. Placing prehistoric totems and internet emojis alongside pseudo-code on ceramics creates a model of history that is both chaotic and deliberate. Exploring error and "babble" as generative tools, the project uses the "Ship of Fools" metaphor to look at machine creativity. Interruption serves as a core method, turning historical failures into states that can be physically felt and examined. Xinyi Zhang (CN)

12:00- 12:15
Root-Seeking · Xun Gen: A Practice-Based Inquiry into XR Environments for Diasporic Cultural Reconnection

This presentation introduces a practice-based PhD project investigating how XR environments can support cultural reconnection for people living within diasporic communities. Through the development of the Root-Seeking · Xun Gen project, the research explores how immersive spatial design, cultural heritage, memory and interactive storytelling can create meaningful experiences of identity and belonging. The presentation outlines the project’s methodology, creative development and audience research, including insights gathered through focus-group activities. It also discusses the practical and conceptual challenges of translating culturally significant places and narratives into immersive experiences while maintaining space for personal interpretation and emotional engagement. Daichen Wang (CN/AU)

12:15 - 12:30
The Dunwich Rose: ReXR as a sustainable methodology for virtual heritage development using obsolete extended reality technologies

The village of Dunwich in Suffolk was once a thriving Anglo-Saxon capital, but much of the original medieval city has been lost to the North Sea owing to coastal erosion. Virtual heritage offers a way to tell the lost stories of Dunwich. However, the XR space used in virtual heritage is becoming mired in unsustainable practices. We must question, then, how creative technologists can develop XR experiences of heritage that is at risk from the effects of climate change, when the very tools and technologies they are using are disappearing more quickly than the environments they are trying to protect.

This research confronts the need to decarbonise immersive practice while addressing crises of climate and social justice by interrogating the tension between XR and environmental crisis. Byproposing a new novel methodological approach to the sustainable development of virtual heritage, ReXR (Recycled Extended Reality) utilises lost technologies to tell lost stories. Emily Godden (GB)

12:30 - 12:45
Anywhere Door: Tethered Hallucination as a Medium for Remembering Shanghai's Vanishing Longtang Alleys.

Anywhere Door proposes AI hallucination and human remembering as structurally parallel operations: both assemble accounts of the past from fragments, filling gaps with plausible material in the absence of the original. The work develops this proposition through Shanghai's vanishing longtang alleys, residential neighborhoods once home to seventy percent of the city's population, now replaced by heritage districts, themed commercial spaces and demolition sites. The installation grounds its AI generation in a 500,000-word nonfiction corpus spanning the 1840s to the 2020s, compiled from seven historical sources. Through a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline, selected objects query this corpus to produce first-person narratives, voiced from inside a steel door frame and rendered as a room glimpsed through a glass peephole. Visitors lean toward the threshold to listen and bend to the peephole to see. The paper calls this a tethered hallucination: fiction that departs from documented reality through a traceable route. Xinran Wu (US)

Artists: Marcus Round (UK), Adam Cole (UK), Mick Grierson (UK), Tomás Laurenzo (US), Ting-Chun Liu (DE), Leon‑Etienne Kühr (DE), Nozomu Kubota (JP)
Web Preview Text EN: The Academic Session #2 Art Track: Authorship presents five contributions from the Expanded Conference Open Call that explore authorship, agency and creative control in expanded animation and interactive art.
Description EN:
The Academic Session #2 Art Track: Authorship presents five contributions from the Expanded Conference Open Call that explore authorship, agency and creative control in expanded animation and interactive art.

14:30–14:45
sent(i)ence: A Performance-Game on Tarot-Steered Language Models and the Ambiguous First Person
When ChatGPT says “I”, what does it mean? sent(i)ence stages this question as an immersive performance-game in which two participants and a large language model collaboratively construct a personal affirmation. The work treats AI-generated language as a contested site of authorship: a sentence may feel intimate and personal even when no single participant can fully claim it as their own. I will discuss how this question developed through my broader artistic practice around games, language and agency, and focus on the work’s technical core: a tarot-inspired system that steers the model using curated interpretability features rather than conventional prompting. By bringing tarot, mechanistic interpretability and participatory performance together, sent(i)ence asks what happens to the human “I” when our thoughts are increasingly articulated through systems that have learned to speak in the first person. Marcus Round (UK), Patrick Hartono (VN)

14:45–15:00
Vertigo Vertigo: Reconstructing a Cinematic Ideal through its Predictive AI Double
Vertigo Vertigo is a scene-for-scene AI reconstruction of Alfred Hitchcock's Vertigo from only 2.78% of the film's original frames. The project algorithmically extracts these keyframes and uses an AI model to fill in the gaps. The resulting film overlaps with the original at its anchor points but constantly diverges, hallucinates, and re-merges in between. This oscillation creates an unstable overlay between the original and its predictive shadow, fueling a persistent doubt in the viewer's perception of what is "real" — a 21st-century vertigo. Hitchcock's Vertigo is fundamentally a film about the obsessive attempt to reconstruct an artificial ideal. Vertigo Vertigo applies that same logic to the material of the film itself, asking what normative cinematic language is embedded in generative systems. In doing so, it argues that generative media is not a paradigm shift from classic Hollywood cinema but an acceleration of its logic of desire and false authenticity. Adam Cole (US/UK)

15:00–15:15
Speculative Pasts
Tomás Laurenzo will present Speculative Pasts, an ongoing research and artistic programme that uses generative artificial intelligence to construct images and videos of histories that did not, could not, or cannot fully appear in the archive. The project is organised around a set of related works — Montevideo, 1983, Abandoned Fictions, Abandoned Future, Hommage Numérique, and La MASA — that approach the past not as a stable object to be recovered, but as a contested field of affect, ideology, omission and technical mediation. Laurenzo argues that AI-generated media can operate as a critical apparatus for the production of speculative memory: not the falsification of history nor the simulation of documentary evidence, but the construction of plausible images that make visible the instability through which memory, city and political imagination are produced. Situated within practice-based research, media art and urban memory studies, the project treats generative systems as instruments of estrangement whose errors, excesses, recognisable biases and capacity for historical pastiche are material conditions through which the politics of representation can be examined. Tomás Laurenzo (UY/US)

15:15–15:30
Will the future of internet be purple?
Will the future of the internet be purple? Steering Through the Inner Residue is a video installation that treats generative AI as a cybernetic system, feeding the output of diffusion models recursively back as input. Inspired by Alvin Lucier's I Am Sitting in a Room (1969), where repeated rerecording reveals resonant frequencies of a room, we apply the same feedback logic to diffusion models, removing text prompts so the system can only respond to its own output. Across six open weight models, this loop settles into a small set of recurring images: patterns, faces, cultural symbols, fragments of advertising. The talk presents the resulting installation, an array of visual panels arranged as an unfolded box, and discusses what these recurring images reveal about the aesthetic tendencies hidden inside generative systems, and what they might suggest about a future internet increasingly built from its own residue. Ting-Chun Liu (TW/DE), Leon-Etienne Kühr (DE)

15:30–15:45
Production of Absence: Reading Stable Diffusion's NSFW Filter through Code and Typology.
This paper introduces production of absence as a critical concept for analyzing AI image generation systems. Through a study of Stable Diffusion's NSFW filter, I show that the filter can systematically remove hand sketches containing anatomical variations—polydactyly, oligodactyly and atypical finger arrangements—rather than the sexual or violent content it ostensibly targets. The paper makes three contributions: a methodology that treats the source code of generation pipelines as a critical primary source; empirical analysis of approximately 10,000 NSFW-flagged images including manual observation of a 316-image subset, suggesting that this exclusion is not incidental but structurally patterned; and a reading of the installation The Invisible Hand of AI as a forensic reconstruction of what the filter has produced as absent. NSFW filters, I argue, are not safety devices but apparatuses that invisibly govern the composition of the visual field. Nozomu Kubota (JP)

Artists: Weibin Duan (CN), Chen Weibo (CN), Magda Hamilton (US), Takafumi Morita (JP), Takayuki Todo (JP), Pei-Ying Lin (TW), Hsianghua Chang (TW), Tzumu Yang (TW), Yiwen Huang (TW), Bingchen Kao (TW), Tsunhung Tsai (TW)
Web Preview Text EN: The Academic Session #3 Art Track: Control presents five Art Papers from the Expanded Conference Open Call that examine how control is negotiated between humans, technologies, materials and environments in expanded animation and interactive art.
Description EN:
The Academic Session #3 Art Track: Control presents five Art Papers from the Expanded Conference Open Call that examine how control is negotiated between humans, technologies, materials and environments in expanded animation and interactive art.

10:00–10:15
Siphon and Overflow A Curatorial Methodology for Art–Technology Dialogue: A Practice-Based Reflection from the China (Hangzhou) Art and Technology Biennale, Symbiotic Cosmos (2025)
This presentation proposes “siphon and overflow” as a curatorial methodology for art-and-technology biennales, examined through the inaugural China (Hangzhou) Art and Technology Biennale, Symbiotic Cosmos (2025). Moving beyond spectacle-driven and showcase-oriented models, the methodology defines siphoning as editorial concentration: creating a disciplined field where heterogeneous practices, discourses, and technological imaginaries encounter one another. Overflow refers to the controlled extension of this field into pedagogical, institutional and translational contexts. Their methodological force emerges through a cyclical tension between concentration and diffusion. The presentation situates this approach within curatorial studies, biennale discourse and cosmotechnics, while grounding it in Liangzhu cosmology, Hangzhou’s historical and digital cultures and the China Academy of Art’s century-long engagement with art and science. Its operation is demonstrated through four thematic sections and selected anchoring works, followed by a reflection on tensions encountered in practice. Weibin Duan (CN), Chen Weibo (CN)

10:15–10:30
Solaris: Designing for Unknowability in Interactive Systems
What does it take to build something that genuinely resists being understood—not broken, not random, but governed by logic the viewer cannot reach? This talk presents Solaris, a real-time WebGL simulation of Stanisław Lem's sentient ocean, built around that question. The work argues that unknowability cannot be authored at the surface: aesthetic strangeness wears off, behavioral mystery collapses under interpretation. Instead, it must be constructed at the level of logic—in physics models, response grammars and communication structures. Three technical decisions are examined as a single argument: a viscoelastic physics model with memory and intent, a gravitational labor visualization and a mood-governed response system whose parameters shift on a schedule the viewer cannot observe. A fourth subsystem fails, and the failure is instructive. The talk proposes four design resources for building systems that sustain the experience of encountering something whose interior stays closed. Magda Hamilton (US)

10:30–10:45
MorphFlux: A Kinetic Installation of a Ferrofluid-Based Physical Display Beyond Human Control Through Human–Material Co-Creation
This art paper presents MorphFlux, a kinetic installation of a ferrofluid-based physical display in which the forms and flows of liquid continuously transform through their mutual interaction. By controlling an array of electromagnets, the ferrofluid forms circular protrusions and ripple-like waves whose interference produces dynamic structures across the liquid surface. While humans guide the liquid, its behavior cannot be fully determined by such control alone, but instead emerges from the interaction among human, material and environment. This relationship is framed as human–material co-creation, in which the material is positioned not as a passive medium but as an active agent that co-produces behavior. Through these behaviors, MorphFlux offers a way to reconsider the relationship between humans and materials from a more-than-human perspective. Takafumi Morita (JP)

10:45–11:00
Dynamics of a Dog on a Leash
In this presentation, I trace how my installation Dynamics of a Dog on a Leash developed from its initial conception around 2010 to its realization in 2025. I reflect on how the project changed through fifteen years of technological, social and artistic shifts, and on how making the work transformed its original premise. Presenting the installation as practice-based research, I examine how animacy and empathic stress emerged through the material and performative relations among a quadruped robot, chain, floor surface, posture-control system, concealed operator and audience. Rather than being scripted or anthropomorphically designed, the robot’s animal-like behavior arose through minimal control, physical constraint, entanglement, balance correction, sound and motor overheating and shutdown. I then consider how these dynamics made viewers perceive intention, vulnerability and suffering in a machine without a face or eyes, and how the work shifted from representing danger to staging ethical discomfort through direct encounter. Takayuki Todo (JP)

11:00–11:15
Role Shift: A VR Trolley Problem on Identity Framing, Forced Embodiment and Moral Discomfort
Role Shift is a virtual reality artwork that reinterprets the Trolley Problem as an embodied, moral encounter. Rather than presenting moral choice as a disembodied trade-off, the work asks the audience to make three successive switch-lever decisions about a runaway train, each followed by a forced viewpoint switch onto the tracks where they experience the consequence. Information about the people on the tracks is disclosed progressively, culminating in a moral reversal before the final decision. The piece combines a haptic vibration vest and high-contrast halftone visuals to attach somatic markers to each decision. Where most VR perspective-taking works invite empathic identification with a victim, Role Shift lets the audience act as the one who decides, then forces them to occupy the position of the harmed. This paper situates the work, articulates its three intertwined design strategies and reflects on what we learned from showing it to fourteen audience members. Pei-Ying Lin (TW), Hsianghua Chang (TW), Tzumu Yang (TW), Yiwen Huang (TW), Bingchen Kao (TW), Tsunhung Tsai (TW)

Artists: Danqi Yao (HK), Anita Mun Yee Lam (HK), Andrew Stokes (HK), Keon Ju Maverick Lee (CA), Philippe Pasquier (CA), Albert Barqué-Duran (ES), Ada Llauradó-Crespo (ES), Shahma Abdulla (SG), Erika Mondria (AT), Alain Renaud (CH)
Web Preview Text EN: The Academic Session #4 Art Track: Embodiment presents five contributions from the Expanded Conference Open Call that explore embodied interaction, perception and the relationship between human bodies and emerging technologies in expanded animation and interactive art.
Description EN:
The Academic Session #4 Art Track: Embodiment presents five contributions from the Expanded Conference Open Call that explore embodied interaction, perception and the relationship between human bodies and emerging technologies in expanded animation and interactive art.

11:30–11:45
Wolf and Tahr: Designing Mixed Reality Dance Performances for Expanded Theatre
This presentation introduces Wolf and Tahr, a mixed reality dance performance developed as a practice-based research project through cross-disciplinary collaboration. It shares the concept, design and implementation process of the work, including our design approaches to key challenges in MR dance performance, and explores the possibilities of MR for expanded theatre, functioning as one section of the performance rather than its sole or dominant format. Danqi Yao (HK), Anita Lam (HK), Andy Stokes (HK)

11:45–12:00
Revival: Metacreation, Co-Creation, and Digital Afterlife with Musical Agents
Revival explores how artificial intelligence, improvisation and historical musical traces can be brought into relation within a live audiovisual performance. Created by the artist collective K-Phi-A, the work unfolds through structured improvisation among human performers, musical agents and generative visual systems. Drawing on curated small datasets, including fragments associated with deceased composers and the collective's own materials, Revival reactivates historical traces through agents that transform and recombine these materials without reproducing them directly. In doing so, the project challenges fixed notions of authorship, liveness and creative control, framing expanded performance as a site of distributed agency through avant-garde percussion sounds, live electroacoustic music, live electronics and interactive audiovisual production. As an artwork and case study, Revival demonstrates how human and artificial agents can co-produce emergent audiovisual form, reanimating historical materials as active forces within present performance. Keon Ju Maverick Lee (KR/CA/QC) & Philippe Pasquier (FR/CA)

12:00–12:15
SYNAPTICON: Creative Alignment at the Brain–AI Model Interface
SYNAPTICON is an artistic-research project combining human-computer interaction, brain-computer interfaces, AI language models and multimodal audiovisual performance. The project proposes creative alignment as the negotiated relationship among performer intention, neural signals, AI model priors, audiovisual mappings and audience interpretation. Rather than treating decoded neural activity as transparent access to inner speech, it functions as a creative index shaping transitions, narratives and perceptual dynamics in real time. The project introduces four layers of creative alignment—signal, semantic, narrative and social—to examine how neural activity becomes technically processable, aesthetically structured and culturally legible. It argues that uncertainty is not simply a technical limitation but a condition shaping co-agency, co-authorship and interpretability, while raising questions of cognitive liberty, mental privacy and responsible brain–AI interface design. Albert Barqué-Duran (ES), Ada Llauradó-Crespo (ES)

12:15–12:30
OUROBOROS_v:init - The Anti-Game: Diagnosing the Achievement Subject through Real-Time EEG
OUROBOROS_v:init is a brain-computer interface installation that inverts the reward gradient of the interactive systems it draws from. Beta-band activity, the established neurological correlate of focused, goal-directed cognition, is mapped to an inverse function of visual stability: as the participant intensifies effort, the rendered environment fragments. Stabilisation requires the suspension of the very reflex the participant has been culturally trained to amplify. In preliminary sessions with fourteen participants, every one responded to the discovery that effort was producing collapse by intensifying effort further. Prior briefing did not interrupt the response. The reflex ran faster than the cognitive recognition of it. This talk presents the installation as a practice-based study of Han's achievement subject and Fisher's privatisation of stress, rendered legible in real-time neural data. It proposes a category of designed environment, diagnostic rather than optimising, that turns the measurement instrument on the person supplying the data. Shahma Abdulla (BH/SG)

12:30–12:45
KIMA: Resonance - Humming in Harmony and Resonance for Creative Health Outcomes
Research points to a sustained effect of humming on mental health and wellbeing. Research across public health, participatory arts and creative health foregrounds the wellbeing effects of humming on diverse populations including infants and young mothers, elderly and groups with mild cognitive impairment and the general public. The art science project KIMA: Resonance by the art collective Analema Group builds on this research. KIMA: Resonance provides an interface for humming, visualizing vocal harmonies between two singers and the effect of humming on the human mind. Measuring harmonic intervals between two interactants alongside its effect on brainwave of a third person, the artwork provides a visual and sonic representation of humming and its effect on the audio-visual cortex. Participatory art has shown to affect human stress levels, and with it its effect on health. This art paper describes the cultural context, genesis of the work and its exhibition at Ars Electronica Festival. Erika Mondria (AT), Alain Renaud (CH)

Artists: Caroline Vogel (AT), Juice Shuting Cui (UK), Peijing Mou (US), Ella Raidel (AT/SG), Benjamin Seide (DE/SG), Clarissa Ribeiro (BR), Margarita Köhl (AT), David Altweger (AT)
Web Preview Text EN: The Academic Session #5 Art Track: More-than-Human presents five Art Papers from the Expanded Conference Open Call that explore multispecies relations and more-than-human perspectives through emerging technologies and artistic practices.
Description EN:
The Academic Session #5 Art Track: More-than-Human presents five Art Papers from the Expanded Conference Open Call that explore multispecies relations and more-than-human perspectives through emerging technologies and artistic practices.

16:30–16:45
Falling Silent: Relational Listening, Mourning, and Multispecies Attunement To Coral Reefs Through Speculative Instrument Co-Making
This presentation shares a participatory workshop on listening to and re-mapping coral reef soundscapes through co-creative, speculative instrument-making, developed in collaboration with the Horniman Museum and Gardens, London. Drawing on marine bioacoustic research showing that coral larvae and juvenile fish orient toward the complex sounds of healthy reefs to locate places to settle, the workshop invites participants to dwell with the gradual loss of these acoustic environments. The session explores listening as a relational practice in the face of ecological loss, and negotiates acts of collective instrument-making as a form of situated, tacit knowledge production that foregrounds embodied, relational modes of engagement with more-than-human worlds. Caroline Vogel (DE/AT), Juice Shuting Cui (CN/UK)

16:45–17:00
Trout Telephone: A Telematic System for More-than-Human Communication Across Fragmented Habitats
Human infrastructure profoundly reshapes nonhuman lives. This talk introduces Trout Telephone, a telematic art installation that presents a communication system for trout across habitats that have been fragmented by dam constructions. For millennia, trout have inhabited the Arroyo Seco watershed in the Los Angeles basin, migrating between a river surrounded by forest and the sea—an ancestral route now interrupted by human interventions and concrete infrastructures. Responding to this ecological injustice to a nonhuman species, the work places two actuated trout-tail sculptures at the divided sites—one upstream in the forest, one in a coastal lagoon. The project links them through a real-time network, creating a call-and-response system across the distant extremes of trout populations. Developed as an on-site installation, experimental documentation and an indoor gallery version, this project contributes a more-than-human model of ecological care and communication, where technological connections are reoriented towards nonhuman perception. Peijing Mou (US)

17:00–17:15
No Path: Immersive Ecologies and the Worlding of a Vanishing Forest
This paper examines No Path, a 360° virtual reality installation engaging with the vanishing secondary forest of Dover Forest West in Singapore as both site and subject of artistic research. Integrating point cloud environments, spatial sound, cinematic VR, ecological data, oral histories and speculative narration, the work creates an embodied mode of sensing rather than observing the forest. Situated within post-cinema, immersive media and environmental humanities, the paper argues that VR can foster ecological attention rather than mere simulation. LiDAR scanning and 3D Gaussian Splatting reconfigure the forest as a “living dataset,” while exposing tensions between technological extraction and preservation. Borrowed from video-game logic, the title denotes inaccessible terrain where navigation fails, becoming a metaphor for the limits of human knowledge and control. Through sensory reorientation and ecological encounter, No Path proposes that immersive media can contribute to sustainability discourse through affective, embodied engagement, recalibrating human perception in the Anthropocene. Ella Raidel (AT/SG), Benjamin Seide (DE/SG)

17:15–17:30
Carbon, Code, Mourning, and Care: Performative Technoetics as a Way of Inhabiting a Burning World
This presentation introduces Ecovotive Chimeras, an interactive expanded animation installation that combines generative AI, augmented reality (AR) and digital fabrication to explore ecological grief and multispecies loss. The accompanying paper examines the conceptual and methodological development of the installation, integrating online image searches, satellite-based wildfire visualizations, environmental datasets and AI-assisted morphogenesis into a reproducible artistic workflow. Beginning with a search phrase extracted from a 2024 New York Times article on the Pantanal fires, the project developed a standardized methodology for locating images of carbonized wildlife from wildfire-affected ecosystems worldwide. Selected images served as prompts in Krea AI to generate morphogenetic animations of unstable interspecies transformations. Frames extracted from these animations informed the production of fifteen 3D-printed chimeric sculptures reanimated through AR, creating a recursive dialogue between moving image, physical artifact and embodied interaction. The paper argues that expanded animation can translate ecological trauma across biological, digital and material realities, fostering new forms of ecological perception, mourning and care. Clarissa Ribeiro (BR)

17:30–17:45
Doubleblind. Sensibilities of Extinction Inducing commemorative practices of countermapping and distributed archiving in an extended reality (XR) environment
Biodiversity is under threat, with accelerating species extinction marking what many theorists describe as the sixth mass extinction. This art-based research project investigates mapping, collecting and archiving as practices shaped by both a desire to preserve what is disappearing and histories of colonial ordering, extraction and control. Drawing on Achille Mbembe’s concept of necropolitics, extinction is approached not only as a biological crisis but also as a cultural and epistemic crisis of representation, memory and imagination. In response, the project develops a speculative “living archive”: an XR-based, processual environment of hybrid creatures and counter-maps that continually updates, recontextualizes and questions its holdings. Through critical cartography and collective, partly speculative archiving, participants co-produce living counter-memorials to interspecies necropolitics. The XR environment reimagines mapping and archiving as shared, more-than-human practices, fostering speculative literacy for engaging with loss, uncertainty, responsibility, care and alternative futures through playful and exploratory participation. Margarita Köhl (AT), David Altweger (AT)

Subtitle EN: The resonance of the encounter in space
Subtitle DE: Die Resonanz der Begegnung im Raum
Web Preview Text EN: What if architecture became an active participant in our interactions? Exploring physical materiality in the context of architecture and the encounters of people in it.
Description EN:
In September 2027, the longstanding collaboration between Ars Electronica Futurelab and SAP, Europe’s largest software manufacturer, reaches another milestone: the lab will create a media artwork composed of three interconnected pieces centered around encounters between people in the atrium of SAP’s remodeled headquarters in Walldorf, Germany.

One of three installations is See You!, an impressive 150-square-meter wall covered in a novel material consisting of flip dots and glass. Futurelab’s anonymous laser tracking system pharus provides the basis for the artistic interpretation of encounters. As people move, meet and pass by, the digital-analog surface not only reflects the encounters, it becomes part of them. The material explores a future in which architecture behaves like a living system, constantly reacting and reflecting its inner ongoings.
Web Preview Text DE: Was wäre, wenn Architektur zu einem aktiven Teil unserer Interaktionen würde?Encounters erforscht physische Materialität im Kontext von Architektur und den Begegnungen der Menschen, die sie beleben.
Description DE:
Im September 2027 erreicht die langjährige Zusammenarbeit zwischen dem Ars Electronica Futurelab und SAP, Europas größtem Softwarehersteller, einen weiteren Meilenstein: Das Lab schafft ein Medienkunstwerk, das aus drei miteinander verbundenen Teilen besteht und sich den Begegnungen der Menschen im Atrium der umgebauten SAP-Zentrale in Walldorf widmet.

Eine der drei Installationen ist See You!, eine eindrucksvolle, 150 Quadratmeter große Wandfläche in einem neuartigen Material aus Flip-Dots und Glas. Das anonyme Lasertracking-System pharus des Futurelab bildet die Grundlage für die künstlerische Interpretation dieser Begegnungen. Wenn sich Menschen bewegen, begegnen und aneinander vorbeigehen, spiegelt die digital-analoge Oberfläche diese Begegnungen nicht nur wider, sondern wird Teil davon. Das Material lotet eine Zukunft aus, in der sich Architektur wie ein lebendiges System verhält, das ständig reagiert und seine inneren Vorgänge widerspiegelt.

Subtitle EN: Data, Art and Science as Local Resources
Subtitle DE: Daten, Kunst und Wissenschaft als lokale Ressourcen
Web Preview Text EN: How can we use data to shape the future of local communities and its revitalization? As part of the Data, Art & Science Project, initiatives and tools are becoming part of the social infrastructure in local communities.
Description EN:
How can we use data to shape local communities’ futures, facing various challenges? Data Art & Science (DAS) is a collaborative project between Ars Electronica Futurelab and Toyota Coniq. This new interdisciplinary field incorporates artistic perspectives on future transformations based on data science. The project has been working for several years to revitalise in Shiga, Japan.
The highlight this year is that the initiatives and tools for the region emerging from DAS are becoming part of the social infrastructure in the area. In Shiga, focused on the “Water-centric” concept, the project has moved from the experimental phase to the implementation in local education, industry and administration. DAS prototypes such as the experimental rice farming are being rolled out as products and services; in addition, textbook and educational programs to learn about the DAS approach are also being developed. Visitors are invited to explore how future visions become a foundation of local communities.
Web Preview Text DE: Wie können wir Daten nutzen, um die Zukunft lokaler Communitys und deren Wiederbelebung mitzugestalten? Im Rahmen des Data, Art & Science Project werden Initiativen und Instrumente zu einem festen Bestandteil der sozialen Infrastruktur von Gemeinschaften.
Description DE: Wie können wir Daten nutzen, um die Zukunft lokaler Communitys angesichts vielfältiger Herausforderungen mitzugestalten? Data Art & Science (DAS) ist ein Gemeinschaftsprojekt von Ars Electronica Futurelab und Toyota Coniq. Dieses neue interdisziplinäre Feld verbindet künstlerische Perspektiven auf zukünftige Veränderungen mit datenwissenschaftlichen Ansätzen. Das Projekt arbeitet seit mehreren Jahren an der Wiederbelebung der Region Shiga in Japan. Das Highlight in diesem Jahr ist, dass die aus DAS hervorgehenden Initiativen und Instrumente für die Region zunehmend Teil der sozialen Infrastruktur vor Ort werden. In Shiga, wo der Schwerpunkt auf einem “wasserzentrierten“ Konzept liegt, ist das Projekt von der experimentellen Phase zur Umsetzung in den Bereichen Bildung, Industrie und Verwaltung übergegangen – mit Produkten, Dienstleistungen und Bildungsprogrammen. Besucher*innen sind eingeladen, zu entdecken, wie Zukunftsvisionen zur Grundlage lokaler Gemeinschaften werden.

Web Preview Text EN: This year, Futurelab Night takes on a new form: instead of a fixed stage programme, visitors are invited to freely explore pop-up interventions, performances, demos and conversations across Open Futurelab, Hello Worlds! and Deep Space 8K—and experience how futures begin today.
Description EN: At this year’s Futurelab Night, we celebrate not only the opening of our new exhibition Hello Worlds! but also 30 years of Ars Electronica Futurelab. The long-standing tradition of Futurelab Night as a festival highlight takes on a new form: exploring uncharted territories by transforming multiple floors of the Ars Electronica Center into a shared stage for encounters, exchange and discovery. Through pop-up interventions, performances, demos and conversations, visitors are invited to move through a dynamic landscape of ideas, experiences and unexpected connections. The future does not simply arrive; it takes shape through encounters, dialogue and continuous negotiation. Futurelab Night offers a vibrant setting for exactly these encounters: not a presentation of what the Futurelab does, but an invitation to experience how futures start taking shape today.
Web Preview Text DE: Die Futurelab Night lädt dieses Jahr zum freien Entdecken ein: Pop-up-Interventionen, Performances, Vorführungen und Gespräche im Open Futurelab, bei Hello Worlds! und im Deep Space 8K machen erfahrbar, wie Zukunft schon heute beginnt.
Description DE: Bei der diesjährigen Futurelab Night feiern wir nicht nur die Eröffnung der neuen Ausstellung Hello Worlds!, sondern auch das 30-jährige Jubiläum des Ars Electronica Futurelab. Die langjährige Tradition der Futurelab Night als Festival-Highlight entfaltet sich in einer neue Form: Mehrere Etagen des Ars Electronica Center werden in eine gemeinsame Bühne für Begegnungen, Austausch und Entdeckungen verwandelt. Durch Pop-up-Interventionen, Performances, erlebnisbasierte Einblicke hinter die Kulissen und Gespräche sind die Besucher*innen eingeladen, sich durch eine dynamische Landschaft aus Ideen, Erfahrungen und unerwarteten Verbindungen zu bewegen. Die Zukunft passiert nicht einfach so; sie nimmt durch Begegnungen, Austausch und ständiges Verhandeln Gestalt an. Die Futurelab Night bietet einen lebendigen Rahmen für genau diese Begegnungen: keine Präsentation dessen, was das Futurelab tut, sondern eine Einladung zu erleben, wie Zukunftsszenarien bereits heute greifbar werden.

Subtitle DE: Youth Exchange Project
Web Preview Text EN: On the last day of the festival, the final presentation of the Youth Exchange Project will take place.
Description EN:
On the last day of the festival, the final presentation of the Youth Exchange Project will take place.

For the Youth Exchange Project, young people from different countries come together in Linz for a cultural and artistic exchange in the context of the Ars Electronica Festival. A multifaceted project takes shape during the festival that brings together creatives and socially engaged individuals between 16 and 20 years old.

This year, the group is developing a film in close collaboration with https://ars.electronica.art/negotiatinghumanity/en/view/film-city-38f38ddb450c807c8442f7a76532c68f/ and other projects of the Ars Electronica Festival, focusing on themes of identity, assigned roles and the breaking of stereotypes. From writing the script and developing storyboards to production, filming, editing and post-production, all participants contribute their skills and interests collectively to create a short film during the festival. The final result will be presented on Sunday at 16:30 in Lecture Hall 1 at the MED Campus.
Web Preview Text DE: Am letzten Festivaltag findet die Abschlusspräsentation des Youth Exchange Projects statt.
Description DE:
Am letzten Festivaltag findet die Abschlusspräsentation des Youth Exchange Projects statt.

Für das Jugendbegegnungsprojekt kommen junge Menschen aus verschiedenen Ländern in Linz für einen kulturellen und künstlerischen Austausch im Rahmen des Ars Electronica Festival zusammen. Durch das Zusammentreffen von Kreativen und gesellschaftlich Engagierten im Alter von 16 bis 20 Jahren entsteht jedes Jahr während der Festivaltage ein vielfältiges Projekt.

In diesem Jahr gestaltet die Gruppe in enger Zusammenarbeit mit der https://ars.electronica.art/negotiatinghumanity/de/view/film-city-38f38ddb450c807c8442f7a76532c68f/ und anderen Projekten des Ars Electronica Festival einen Film zu den Themen Identität, Rollenzuschreibungen und das Brechen mit Stereotypen. Vom Schreiben des Drehbuchs und Skizzieren des Storyboards über die gestalterische und technische Umsetzung bis hin zu Schnitt und Nachbearbeitung bringen alle Teilnehmenden ihre Fertigkeiten und Interessen ein. So entsteht an den Festivaltagen gemeinsam ein Kurzfilm. 

Das Ergebnis wird am Festivalsonntag um 16:30 im Hörsaal 1 am MED Campus präsentiert.

Web Preview Text EN: Visitors are invited to experience current developments in medicine, teaching and research first-hand at JKU medSPACE, where JKU university clinics and institutes present virtual anatomy and offer new perspectives in 3D operations on the heart, brain, abdomen, shoulder and eye.
Description EN: At JKU medSPACE, visitors are invited to experience current developments in medicine, teaching and research first-hand. JKU university clinics and institutes present virtual anatomy and demonstrate how 3D operations open up new perspectives on the heart, brain, abdomen, shoulder and eye. The program shows how digital technologies can expand our understanding of the human body, medical education and research. A special highlight on September 12: the live broadcast of a heart surgery into JKU medSPACE. While the operation takes place in the operating room at Kepler University Hospital, visitors follow the procedure live on a large-scale projection and can ask the surgical team questions in real time.
Web Preview Text DE: Besucher*innen sind eingeladen, Entwicklungen in Medizin, Lehre und Forschung im JKU medSPACE aus nächster Nähe zu erleben. Dort präsentieren Universitätskliniken und Institute der JKU virtuelle Anatomie und eröffnen neue Perspektiven durch 3D-Operationen an Herz, Gehirn, Bauch, Schulter und Auge.
Description DE: Im JKU medSPACE sind Besucher*innen eingeladen, aktuelle Entwicklungen in Medizin, Lehre und Forschung aus nächster Nähe zu erleben. Universitätskliniken und Institute der JKU präsentieren virtuelle Anatomie und zeigen, wie 3D-Operationen neue Einblicke in Herz, Gehirn, Bauchraum, Schulter und Auge eröffnen. So wird sichtbar, wie digitale Technologien das Verständnis des menschlichen Körpers, die Ausbildung künftiger Ärzt*innen und medizinische Forschung erweitern. Ein besonderes Highlight am 12. September: die Live-Übertragung einer Herzoperation in den JKU medSPACE. Während der Eingriff im Operationssaal des Kepler Universitätsklinikums läuft, verfolgen die Besucher*innen das Geschehen live auf einer Großprojektion und können dem chirurgischen Team dabei in Echtzeit Fragen stellen.
Additional Info EN: Content Note: Depicts blood and medical interventions. | Please note: Admission is free, but capacity is limited. Seating tickets for this event are available on SAT 12.9. from 9:30 AM at the INFODESK of the JKU MED Campus (Administration Building, ADM).

Name EN: Who Heals Tomorrow? AI, Medicine and the Future of Decision-Making
Name DE: Wer heilt morgen? KI, Medizin und die Zukunft der Entscheidung
Artists: Experts from the fields of medicine, AI research, law and patient advocacy
Web Preview Text EN: In a fishbowl format, experts from the fields of medicine, AI research and law will discuss the opportunities and risks of AI in healthcare with patient representatives and a live audience—exploring ways in which innovation, responsibility and safety can all be brought together through smart data governance.
Description EN: Will AI replace doctors in the future? Who is liable when incorrect decisions are made? And what does health data without borders actually mean? In a fishbowl format, experts from the fields of medicine, AI research and law will discuss the opportunities, risks and societal consequences of AI in healthcare together with patient representatives and a live audience. The discussion will outline the enormous possibilities of AI use in medicine, but also address questions of responsibility, patient safety, data protection and trust—prerequisites for innovation, medical expertise and smart data governance to be able to work together for the benefit of people. Join us for this discussion about the medicine of tomorrow.
Web Preview Text DE: Im Fishbowl-Format diskutieren Expert*innen aus Medizin, KI-Forschung und Rechtswissenschaft gemeinsam mit Patient*innenvertretungen und dem Publikum über Chancen und Risiken von KI in der Medizin – und darüber, wie Innovation, Verantwortung und Sicherheit durch kluge Data Governance zusammenwirken.
Description DE: Ersetzt KI künftig Ärztinnen und Ärzte? Wer haftet bei Fehlentscheidungen? Und was bedeuten Gesundheitsdaten ohne Grenzen? Im Fishbowl-Format diskutieren Expert*innen aus Medizin, KI-Forschung und Rechtswissenschaften gemeinsam mit Patient*innenvertretungen und dem Publikum über Chancen, Risiken und gesellschaftliche Folgen von KI im Gesundheitswesen. Es geht um die gewaltigen Möglichkeiten des Einsatzes von KI in der Medizin, aber auch um Fragen zu Verantwortung, Patientensicherheit, Datenschutz und Vertrauen – Voraussetzungen dafür, dass Innovation, medizinische Expertise und kluge Data Governance zum Nutzen der Menschen zusammenwirken. Diskutiere mit – über die Medizin von morgen.
Credits long: Experts from medicine, AI research, law, and patient advocacy

Web Preview Text EN: Flow in circle is a performance by sound artist Zata Zhdkv for water, audio feedback and body. It explores the unknown submerged territory—physically, acoustically and metaphorically—and asks the question: can we understand the foreign world?
Description EN: Flow in circle is a performance for water, feedback and body. While exploring the unknown space in both physical, acoustical and metaphorical way, it asks the question: can we understand the foreign world? How can we interact with it and establish communication in unusual conditions? The piece stages an encounter between human perception and an acoustic environment that remains partially inaccessible.
Web Preview Text DE: Flow in circle ist eine Performance der Klangkünstlerin Zata Zhdkv für Wasser, Audiofeedback und Körper. Sie erkundet unbekanntes, untergetauchtes Terrain – physisch, akustisch und metaphorisch – und stellt die Frage: Können wir die fremde Welt verstehen?
Description DE: Flow in circle ist eine Performance für Wasser, Audiofeedback und Körper. Während sie den unbekannten Raum physisch, akustisch und metaphorisch erkundet, fragt sie: Können wir die fremde Welt verstehen? Wie können wir mit ihr interagieren und unter ungewohnten Bedingungen in Kommunikation treten? Das Stück inszeniert eine Begegnung zwischen menschlicher Wahrnehmung und einer akustischen Umgebung, die teilweise unzugänglich bleibt.

Web Preview Text EN: Wu Cheng-Ru is a Taiwan-based new media artist specializing in audiovisual performance. Through sound experimentation, real-time visuals and digital signal integration, his work explores human relationships and cognitive gaps by manipulating the friction and distortions within signal transmission.
Description EN: Thiann is the Taiwanese word for “listening.” This live AV performance explores local identity by collecting mundane, yet unique Taiwanese acoustics—such as rural vendor broadcasts and vehicular speed-limit alerts. Through experimental remixing and electronic deformation, the artist deconstructs these everyday social cues and collective sonic memories into an immersive noise-driven soundscape.
Web Preview Text DE: Wu Cheng-Ru ist ein in Taiwan lebender Medienkünstler mit Schwerpunkt auf audiovisueller Performance. Durch Klangexperimente, Echtzeit-Visualisierungen und digitale Signal-Integration erforscht seine Arbeit menschliche Beziehungen und kognitive Lücken, indem sie die Reibung und Verzerrungen innerhalb der Signalübertragung manipuliert.
Description DE: Thiann ist das taiwanesische Wort für “Zuhören”. Die Live-AV-Performance untersucht lokale Identität anhand alltäglicher, unverwechselbar taiwanesischer Klänge – etwa Lautsprecherdurchsagen ländlicher Händler*innen oder akustischen Geschwindigkeitswarnungen in Fahrzeugen. Durch experimentelles Remixing und elektronische Verfremdung dekonstruiert der Künstler diese alltäglichen sozialen Signale und kollektiven klanglichen Erinnerungen zu einer immersiven, von Noise geprägten Klanglandschaft.

Web Preview Text EN: WHEREISCHAPPIE (Liu Tung-Yu) is an audiovisual artist and project manager. His work treats code and self-built interfaces as performative materials and usually reflects observations of subcultural community alongside a sense of childlike playfulness.
Description EN:
Gao Huang is an interactive audiovisual performance that uses motion capture and image recognition to transform the performer’s movements into real-time sound and visuals. Drawing on the “Gao Huang” acupoint as a metaphor for accumulated bodily
tension, the work makes visible and audible the hidden friction, imbalance and persistent aches shaped by contemporary patterns of labor and stillness.
Web Preview Text DE: WHEREISCHAPPIE (Liu Tung-Yu) ist audiovisueller Künstler und Projektmanager. In seiner Arbeit behandelt er Code und selbstgebaute Interfaces als performative Materialien. Dabei reflektiert er oftmals Beobachtungen subkultureller Communitys verbunden mit einem Gespür für kindliche Verspieltheit.
Description DE: Gao Huang ist eine interaktive audiovisuelle Performance, die Motion Capture und Bilderkennung nutzt, um in Echtzeit die Bewegungen der*des Performer*in in Klang und Visualisierungen zu übersetzen. Der Akupunkturpunkt “Gao Huang” dient dabei als Metapher für angestaute körperliche Spannung. Die Arbeit macht verborgene Reibung, Ungleichgewicht und anhaltende Beschwerden sichtbar und hörbar, die durch gegenwärtige Formen von Arbeit und Bewegungslosigkeit geprägt sind.

Web Preview Text EN: Subkutan explores the physicality of sound and its relation to space and the body. Played exclusively on subwoofers, it transcends auditory thresholds and amplifies corporeal sensations. Trembling and floating, soothing and arousing, this performance subtly gets into your ears and under your skin.
Description EN: Subkutan explores the physicality of sound, space and the body. Performed exclusively on subwoofers, it works with sub-bass frequencies that are felt as much as heard, amplifying bodily sensation and pushing beyond auditory thresholds. Trembling, floating, soothing and arousing, this performance slips under the skin to create an immersive experience. By engaging environmental resonances and reflections, it sets bodies in motion and synchronizes audiences within an altered spatial reality.
Web Preview Text DE: Subkutan erforscht die physische Dimension von Klang und sein Verhältnis zu Raum und Körper. Ausschließlich über Subwoofer wiedergegeben, überschreitet die Performance auditive Grenzen und verstärkt körperliche Empfindungen. Zitternd und sanft schwebend, beruhigend und mitreißend dringt sie subtil ins Ohr und unter die Haut.
Description DE: Subkutan erforscht die physische Dimension von Klang, Raum und Körper. Über Subwoofer wiedergegeben, arbeitet die Performance mit Subbassfrequenzen, die ebenso spürbar wie hörbar sind. Sie verstärkt körperliche Empfindungen und überschreitet auditive Grenzen. Zitternd, schwebend, beruhigend und mitreißend dringt sie unter die Haut und schafft ein immersives Erlebnis. Raumresonanzen und -reflexionen setzen Körper in Bewegung und synchronisieren das Publikum in einer veränderten Realität.

Web Preview Text EN: Linz-based artist 1=1 (aka DJ Döner) invites their DJ mother, NEVSS from Cyprus for a DJ set on the experimental edge of dance music.
Description EN:
Brought together in Cyprus during the COVID pandemic, 1=1 and NEVSS blend dance music with experimental elements and ambient textures. Their shared background is rooted in underground culture and shaped by experiences across European cities.
For this special DJ set, NEVSS is traveling from Cyprus to reunite with Linz-based 1=1.
Web Preview Text DE: Der*die in Linz lebende Künstler*in 1=1 (aka DJ Döner) lädt seine*ihre DJ-Mutter, NEVSS aus Zypern zu einem DJ-Set an den experimentellen Rändern der Dance Music ein.
Description DE: Während der COVID-Pandemie auf Zypern zusammengebracht, verbinden 1=1 und NEVSS Dance Music mit experimentellen Elementen und Ambient-Texturen. Ihr gemeinsamer Hintergrund ist in der Underground-Kultur verwurzelt und von Erfahrungen in verschiedenen europäischen Städten geprägt. Für dieses besondere DJ-Set reist NEVSS aus Zypern an, um gemeinsam mit dem*der in Linz lebenden Künstler*in 1=1 aufzulegen.

Web Preview Text EN: This audiovisual performance explores how artificial sound can reshape the act of listening. AI-generated birdsong, granular synthesis, sine waves, noise and real-time visuals form a mediated field where natural and synthetic textures blur and listening becomes unstable, uncertain and transformed.
Description EN: The project explores how artificial sound reshapes listening in a world saturated with human-made and mediated sound. Through a live audiovisual performance, AI-generated birdsong is processed through granular synthesis, while sine waves and noise create tension between natural and synthetic textures. Real-time visuals respond to sound, forming an unstable field where listening becomes uncertain and transformed.
Web Preview Text DE: Diese audiovisuelle Performance untersucht, wie künstlicher Klang das Hören neu formen kann. KI-generierter Vogelgesang, Granularsynthese, Sinuswellen, Rauschen und Echtzeitvisualisierungen bilden ein vermitteltes Feld, in dem natürliche und synthetische Klangtexturen ineinanderfließen und das Hören instabil, ungewiss und transformiert wird.
Description DE: Das Projekt untersucht, wie künstlicher Klang das Hören in einer Welt neu formt, die von menschengemachten und medial vermittelten Klängen durchdrungen ist. In einer AV-Live-Performance wird KI-generierter Vogelgesang mittels Granularsynthese verarbeitet, während Sinuswellen und Rauschen ein Spannungsfeld zwischen natürlichen und synthetischen Klangtexturen erzeugen. Echtzeitvisualisierungen reagieren auf den Klang und bilden ein instabiles Feld, in dem das Hören ungewiss und transformiert wird.

Web Preview Text EN: de-attractor is an audiovisual performance exploring the decomposition of order. It begins with a spherical point cloud that fractures as sound shifts into unstable oscillations. Particles break free from their axes, dispersing into irregular textures to document a chaotic dissipation.
Description EN: de-attractor is a generative audiovisual performance visualizing the decomposition of geometric order. Through TouchDesigner, the audience observes a spherical point cloud fracturing into erratic particles. Sonically, pre-arranged audio collides with unpredictable, live modular synthesizer patching. This shifting auditory landscape parallels the visual distortion, enveloping the viewer in a chaotic dissipation that probes the fragile boundary between structural stability and collapse.
Web Preview Text DE: de-attractor ist eine audiovisuelle Performance, die den Zerfall von Ordnung erkundet. Ausgangspunkt ist eine kugelförmige Punktwolke, die aufbricht, während der Klang in instabile Oszillationen übergeht. Partikel lösen sich von ihren Achsen und zerstreuen sich zu unregelmäßigen Texturen, die eine chaotische Dissipation dokumentieren.
Description DE: de-attractor ist eine generative audiovisuelle Performance, die den Zerfall geometrischer Ordnung visualisiert. Über TouchDesigner beobachtet das Publikum eine kugelförmige Punktwolke, die in erratische Partikel zerbricht. Klanglich kollidiert vorarrangiertes Audio mit unvorhersehbarem Live-Patching modularer Synthesizer. Die Klanglandschaft spiegelt die visuelle Verzerrung und hüllt das Publikum in eine chaotische Dissipation, die die fragile Grenze zwischen Stabilität und Kollaps auslotet.

Web Preview Text EN: Electrosensitivity is a multichannel sound performance for an array of resonant circuits and a custom-made plasma-controlled postdigital synthesizer that explores imperceptible manifestations of electrical phenomena in our everyday lives.
Description EN: Electrosensitivity sound performance uses custom high-frequency resonant generators and the author's hand-controllable plasma-discharge instruments to explore the gap between electricity's crucial role in our bodies and our inability to sense electric and magnetic fields. This gap allows us to use the electromagnetic processes as the core of modern technology, which is rapidly changing our environments and their human and non-human inhabitants, in ways that remain to be revealed.
Web Preview Text DE: Electrosensitivity ist eine Mehrkanal-Soundperformance für ein Ensemble aus Schwingkreisen und einen eigens entwickelten, plasmagesteuerten postdigitalen Synthesizer. Die Performance erkundet die nicht wahrnehmbaren Erscheinungsformen elektrischer Phänomene in unserem Alltag.
Description DE: Electrosensitivity nutzt eigens entwickelte Hochfrequenz-Resonanzgeneratoren und handgesteuerte Plasmaentladungsinstrumente. Die Soundperformance untersucht die Kluft zwischen der Bedeutung von Elektrizität für unsere Körper und unserer Unfähigkeit, elektrische und magnetische Felder wahrzunehmen. Diese Kluft erlaubt uns, elektromagnetische Prozesse als Grundlage moderner Technologien zu nutzen, die unsere Umwelt und ihre menschlichen wie nichtmenschlichen Bewohner*innen unabsehbar verändern.

To submerge opens up new modes of attention and multi-sensory listening that change our relation with the surrounding.

Web Preview Text EN: A live performance combining biological material and synthesis. Enclosed mold is used as a living resistor to generate sound, interacting with MIDI-controlled electronics in a performative sonic system.
Description EN: A live performance combining biological material and sound synthesis. What counts as “dirty” or “pure” when biological matter becomes an active sonic agent? The project uses mold as a living resistor, translating bio-activity into sound through interaction with electronic circuits. The audience experiences a performative sonic system in real time, exploring how biological systems can reveal marginalized conditions of existence.
Web Preview Text DE: Eine Live-Performance, die biologisches Material und Synthese verbindet. Eingeschlossener Schimmel dient als lebender Widerstand zur Klangerzeugung und interagiert in einem performativen Klangsystem mit MIDI-gesteuerter Elektronik.
Description DE: Eine Live-Performance, die biologisches Material und Klangsynthese verbindet. Was gilt als “schmutzig” oder “rein”, wenn biologische Materie selbst aktiv Klang erzeugt? Das Projekt nutzt Schimmelpilz als lebenden Widerstand und übersetzt seine Bio-Aktivität im Zusammenspiel mit elektronischen Schaltkreisen in Klang. Das Publikum erlebt dieses performative Klangsystem in Echtzeit und erkundet, wie biologische Systeme marginalisierte Existenzbedingungen sichtbar machen können.

Web Preview Text EN: FACE SHIFT is a raw, improvisational live performance by I-ID and Mascha Illich, blending analogue synthesis, live DJing, noise and fractured rhythms. An immersive journey through tension, movement and transformation, where every performance unfolds uniquely in real time.
Description EN: FACE SHIFT is a live performance and collaborative DJ set emerging from qujOchÖ’s ongoing project Rhizomaniacs. The performance is developed as a duo by I-ID and Mascha Illich. Moving through live mixing, analogue synthesis, broken rhythms, noise and spontaneous sonic interventions, FACE SHIFT is shaped by real-time sensation and the connection between mind and body. It explores how sound affects perception, emotion and movement, shifting between intensity, tension and release.
Web Preview Text DE: FACE SHIFT ist eine rohe, improvisierte Live-Performance von I-ID und Mascha Illich, die analoge Synthese, Live-DJing, Noise und gebrochene Rhythmen verbindet. Eine immersive Reise durch Spannung, Bewegung und Transformation, die sich bei jeder Aufführung in Echtzeit neu und einzigartig entfaltet.
Description DE: FACE SHIFT ist eine Live-Performance und ein kollaboratives DJ-Set von I-ID und Mascha Illich, entstanden aus dem Projekt Rhizomaniacs von qujOchÖ. Durch Live-Mixing, analoge Synthese, gebrochene Rhythmen, Noise und spontane klangliche Interventionen wird FACE SHIFT zu einem Echtzeiterlebnis, geprägt von der Verbindung von Geist und Körper. Die Performance untersucht, wie Klang Wahrnehmung, Emotionen und Bewegung beeinflusst, und bewegt sich dabei zwischen Intensität, Spannung und Entladung.

Web Preview Text EN: Parasomnia is inspired by the delirious states that emerge during light sleep. What seems real begins to dissolve and what seems imagined acquires physical weight. Gestures, timing and subtle theatrical actions are interwoven, reinforcing the ambiguity between authenticity and simulation.
Description EN: Parasomnia is a performance for self-built instruments and electronics exploring the delirious states of light sleep, where perception becomes unstable and the boundary between reality and imagination dissolves. It invites the audience to immerse themselves in a shifting sonic environment where authenticity, memory and dreams become increasingly difficult to distinguish.
Web Preview Text DE: Parasomnia ist von den delirierenden Zuständen inspiriert, die im leichten Schlaf entstehen. Was real erscheint, beginnt sich aufzulösen, und was imaginiert scheint, gewinnt an körperlichem Gewicht. Gesten, Timing und subtile theatrale Handlungen verweben sich und verstärken die Mehrdeutigkeit zwischen Authentizität und Simulation.
Description DE: Parasomnia ist eine Performance für selbst gebaute Instrumente und Elektronik, die delirierende Zustände des leichten Schlafs erkundet, in denen die Wahrnehmung instabil wird und die Grenze zwischen Realität und Imagination verschwimmt. Sie lädt das Publikum ein, in eine sich wandelnde Klangumgebung einzutauchen, in der Authentizität, Erinnerung und Träume zunehmend schwer voneinander zu unterscheiden sind.

Web Preview Text EN: Meshes bring their electroacoustic practice to Sound Campus—an investigation into tactile sound, real-time processing and the dissolving boundary between acoustic and digital.
Description EN: Meshes present a new work for percussion and electronics that examines the boundaries between the physical and the computational. Kolmbauer approaches the drum set through unconventional implement and extended techniques. Sounds are captured-submitted to real-time electronic processing, rendering the intimate audible and the incidental compositional. Jociūtė works with synthesizers and electronics as analog control interfaces and effects to receive, transform and redirect this material.
Web Preview Text DE: Meshes bringen ihre elektroakustische Praxis zum Sound Campus – eine Untersuchung über taktilen Klang, Echtzeitverarbeitung und die sich auflösende Grenze zwischen Akustischem und Digitalem.
Description DE: Meshes präsentieren ein neues Werk für Percussion und Elektronik, das die Grenzen zwischen dem Physischen und dem Digitalen auslotet. Kolmbauer nähert sich dem Schlagzeug mit unkonventionellen Hilfsmitteln und erweiterten Spieltechniken. Klänge werden aufgenommen und in Echtzeit elektronisch verarbeitet, wodurch das Intime hörbar und das Beiläufige kompositorisch wird. Jociūtė nutzt Synthesizer und Elektronik als analoge Steuerungsschnittstellen und Effekte, um dieses Material zu empfangen, zu transformieren und weiterzuleiten.

Web Preview Text EN: An experimental electroacoustic folk duo that offers a perspective on the mystical links between ourselves and nature. Blending acoustic instruments with electronic textures, their music uses traditional folk forms as living material, which is transformed into something timeless and oneiric.
Description EN: This project presents an experimental electroacoustic folk performance set within its own mythological world. Through music, poetic imagery and ritual-like compositional forms, it invites the audience into a garden where both beauty and darkness reside. The project aims to create a space for contemplation, memory and imagination, exploring mythology as a living language for the present moment.
Web Preview Text DE: Ein experimentelles elektroakustisches Folk-Duo, das eine Perspektive auf die mystischen Verbindungen zwischen uns und der Natur eröffnet. Es verwebt akustische Instrumente mit elektronischen Texturen und nutzt traditionelle Folk-Formen als lebendiges Material, das in etwas Zeitloses und Traumartiges verwandelt wird.
Description DE: Das Projekt präsentiert eine experimentelle elektroakustische Folk-Performance, die in einer eigenen mythologischen Welt angesiedelt ist. Durch Musik, poetische Bildsprache und ritualähnliche Kompositionsformen lädt es das Publikum in einen Garten ein, in dem Schönheit und Dunkelheit gleichermaßen zu Hause sind. Das Projekt möchte einen Raum für Kontemplation, Erinnerung und Imagination schaffen und dabei Mythologie als lebendige Sprache für den gegenwärtigen Moment erkunden.

Web Preview Text EN: Meditative Chaos is a live performance exploring the threshold between deep listening and sonic turbulence. Through feedback, resonance and transformation, an immersive environment is created where contemplation and instability coexist, revealing hidden rhythms and layers.
Description EN: Meditative Chaos is a live sonic journey through states of attention, resonance and transformation. Drawing on practices of deep listening, feedback systems and electronic sound synthesis, DEEP THROAT constructs an immersive environment where fragile balances emerge between contemplation and disruption. The performance invites audiences to navigate this soundscape, revealing chaos not as disorder but as a space of heightened perception and collective listening.
Web Preview Text DE: Meditative Chaos ist eine Live-Performance, die die Schwelle zwischen vertieftem Zuhören und klanglicher Turbulenz erkundet. Durch Feedback, Resonanz und Transformation entsteht eine immersive Umgebung, in der Kontemplation und Instabilität nebeneinander bestehen und verborgene Rhythmen und Schichten hervortreten.
Description DE: Meditative Chaos ist eine Live-Klangreise durch Zustände von Aufmerksamkeit, Resonanz und Transformation. Mit vertieftem Zuhören, Feedbacksystemen und elektronischer Klangsynthese schafft DEEP THROAT eine immersive Umgebung, in der fragile Gleichgewichte zwischen Kontemplation und Disruption entstehen. Die Performance lädt das Publikum ein, diese Klanglandschaft zu erkunden und Chaos nicht als Unordnung, sondern als Raum gesteigerter Wahrnehmung und des gemeinsamen Zuhörens zu erfahren.

Name EN: On Forecasting Monsters by Kairos TV
Web Preview Text EN: Sound performance On Forecasting Monsters by Kairos TV takes the format of a weather channel’s program, in which extreme weather phenomena are embodied by the figure of the monster.
Description EN: Kairos TV is a collaborative project initiated by Marie-Andrée Pellerin and Stanisław Welbel, using the format of a weather channel for artistic and critical purposes. The performance presents a fictional daily weather program in which extreme weather phenomena are embodied by the figure of the monster. The visual content, built from found footage video is complemented by live sound performance created by the duo, with synthesizers and samples.
Web Preview Text DE: Die Soundperformance On Forecasting Monsters by Kairos TV ist wie eine Sendung eines Wetterkanals gestaltet, in der extreme Wetterphänomene durch die Figur des Monsters verkörpert werden.
Description DE: Kairos TV ist ein von Marie-Andrée Pellerin und Stanisław Welbel initiiertes kollaboratives Projekt, das das Format eines Wetterkanals für künstlerische und kritische Zwecke nutzt. Die Performance präsentiert eine fiktive tägliche Wettersendung, in der extreme Wetterphänomene durch die Figur des Monsters verkörpert werden. Die visuellen Inhalte aus Found-Footage-Material werden durch eine Live-Soundperformance ergänzt, die das Duo mit Synthesizern und Samples gestaltet.

Name EN: Feeling Virtual: An Archive of Touch
Web Preview Text EN: Challenging our “Look, Don't Touch” culture, this installation draws on disabled ways of knowing. Experience materials from the Salzburg Festival Archive through a tactile XR artwork, an accompanying video and a workbook inviting you into the crip practice of tactile descriptions.
Description EN:
Feeling Virtual: An Archive of Touch challenges the cultural convention of “look, don’t touch” and proposes an alternative approach to knowledge and perception. Drawing on materials from the archive of the Salzburg Festival, this installation makes the archive accessible through touch and, from the perspective of Disability Studies, develops a mode of seeing beyond the visual. Through a tactile XR application, an accompanying video and a workbook, the work invites visitors to experience archival materials through vibration, sound, images and tactile descriptions. 

The installation draws on disabled ways of knowing that recognize the body, touch and multisensory experience as autonomous forms of knowledge. It reveals how cultural institutions reproduce normative assumptions about bodies and perception. By establishing touch, vibration and multisensory experience as equally valid modes of knowing, the work challenges visually dominant epistemologies and opens up more inclusive ways of engaging with culture and memory.
Web Preview Text DE: Feeling Virtual: An Archive of Touch hinterfragt unsere kulturelle “Look, Don’t Touch”-Praxis und eröffnet einen anderen Zugang zu Wissen und Wahrnehmung. Die Installation macht Materialien aus dem Archiv der Salzburger Festspiele über Berührung erfahrbar.
Description DE:
Feeling Virtual: An Archive of Touch hinterfragt unsere kulturelle “Look, Don’t Touch”-Praxis und eröffnet einen anderen Zugang zu Wissen und Wahrnehmung. Die Installation macht Materialien aus dem Archiv der Salzburger Festspiele über Berührung erfahrbar und entwickelt aus der Perspektive von Disability Studies eine Form des Sehens jenseits des Visuellen. Mithilfe einer taktilen XR-Anwendung, eines begleitenden Videos und eines Workbooks lädt die Arbeit dazu ein, Archive durch Vibrationen, Klänge, Bilder und taktile Beschreibungen neu zu erfahren. Die Arbeit greift auf behinderte Formen des Wissens zurück, die den Körper, Berührung und multisensorische Erfahrung als eigenständige Erkenntnisformen verstehen.  
 
Die Installation macht sichtbar, wie kulturelle Institutionen bestimmte Körper- und Wahrnehmungsnormen reproduzieren. Sie etabliert Berührung, Vibration und multisensorische Erfahrung als gleichwertige Erkenntnisformen. Damit fordert sie visuell geprägte Wissensordnungen heraus und eröffnet inklusivere Zugänge zu Kultur und Erinnerung.

Web Preview Text EN: We attune to the earth’s body alongside our own, exploring how ecological grief and planetary suffering are felt in our nervous systems and affect our sense of belonging. As the world heats up and changes permanently, where does that solastalgia land in you? Join us in a practice of listening and inter-being.
Description EN: In this workshop, we attune to the earth’s body alongside our own, exploring how environmental loss, ecological grief and planetary suffering are felt in our nervous systems and in our bodies, and how they affect our sense of belonging. Drawing on the concept of inter-being, we expand the notion of pain beyond the individual. When forests burn, species vanish and the world heats up. Where does that solastalgia land in you? Please join us in a practice of listening, dissolving and recognizing ourselves in the wound of the world.
Web Preview Text DE: Wir stimmen uns auf den Körper der Erde ein, so wie auf unseren eigenen, und erkunden, wie sich ökologische Trauer und planetares Leiden in unserem Nervensystem und unserem Zugehörigkeitsgefühl niederschlagen. Wo hinterlässt die Solastalgie ihre Spuren in dir?
Description DE: In diesem Workshop stimmen wir uns auf den Körper der Erde ein, so wie auf unseren eigenen, und erkunden, wie sich Umweltverlust, ökologische Trauer und planetares Leiden in unserem Nervensystem, unseren Körpern und unserem Zugehörigkeitsgefühl niederschlagen. Ausgehend vom Konzept des Zusammen-Seins (inter-being) erweitern wir Schmerz über das Individuum hinaus. Wenn Wälder brennen, Arten verschwinden und sich die Erde erwärmt – wo setzt sich diese Solastalgie in dir fest? Wir laden dich ein zu einer Praxis des Zuhörens, des Loslassens und des Erkennens unserer selbst in der Wunde der Welt.
Additional Info EN: The event will take place in the MED Campus in the P.A.I.N. (Personal And Interconnected with Nature) installation, part of the LBG-OIS Center.
Additional Info DE: Diese Veranstaltung findet im MED Campus im Bereich der Installation P.A.I.N. (Personal And Interconnected with Nature) statt (Teil des LBG-OIS Center).

Web Preview Text EN: The Live Cinema Lab invites participants to become part of a filmmaking process. Within an open installation, they experience different departments of filmmaking and their interplay firsthand through experimenting, exploring and collaboratively developing a scene.
Description EN: The Live Cinema Lab is a participatory film installation that invites participants to actively immerse themselves in the world of filmmaking. The focus is not on the final result, but on the creative process itself: How does a scene emerge? How do decisions, encounters and perspectives shape a story? Participants step into a role and develop a short film scene together with a professional acting partner on site. They experience a glimpse of everyday life on a film set, from preparation and acting to directing, camera, sound and costume. The scene is explored, reflected on and transformed. The Live Cinema Lab creates an open space for encounter, experimentation and learning, making the processes, decisions and collaborations behind filmmaking directly tangible.
Web Preview Text DE: Das Live Cinema Lab lädt Teilnehmer*innen ein, selbst Teil eines Filmprozesses zu werden. In einer offenen Installation erleben sie unmittelbar die unterschiedlichen Gewerke des Filmemachens und ihr Zusammenspiel – durch Ausprobieren, Experimentieren und das gemeinsame Entwickeln einer Szene.
Description DE:
Das Live Cinema Lab ist eine partizipative Film-Installation, die Teilnehmer*innen einlädt, aktiv in die Welt des Filmemachens einzutauchen. Im Mittelpunkt steht nicht das fertige Ergebnis, sondern der gemeinsame Prozess: Wie entsteht eine Szene? Wie verändern Entscheidungen, Begegnungen und Perspektiven eine Geschichte?
Die Teilnehmer*innen schlüpfen in eine Rolle und entwickeln gemeinsam mit einer Schauspielpartnerin beziehungsweise einem Schauspielpartner vor Ort eine kurze Filmszene. Dabei erleben sie einen Ausschnitt aus dem Alltag eines Filmsets – von der Vorbereitung über Schauspiel und Regie bis hin zu Kamera, Ton und Kostüm. Die Szene wird ausprobiert, reflektiert und verändert. Das Live Cinema Lab schafft einen offenen Raum für Begegnung, Experiment und Lernen. Es öffnet den Blick auf die Prozesse, Entscheidungen und Begegnungen, die Film entstehen lassen, und macht sie für Teilnehmer*innen unmittelbar erfahrbar.

Web Preview Text EN: PULS is an audiovisual installation of eight light-speaker units. It creates an immersive environment where time, space, rhythm and movement feel unstable. Rapid flashes and multidirectional sound produce fleeting, distorted impressions of the surrounding architecture.
Description EN: PULS explores the boundaries and peculiarities of our perception through the use of sensory extremes. Flashing light, total darkness and brief audiovisual impulses repeating at rates between rhythm and tone will manipulate our sense of time and space. The installation will overwhelm us, create illusions, force us to change perspectives or even bring us to different state of consciousness.
Web Preview Text DE: PULS ist eine audiovisuelle Installation aus acht Licht-Lautsprecher-Einheiten. Sie schafft eine immersive Umgebung, in der Zeit, Raum, Rhythmus und Bewegung instabil erscheinen. Schnelle Lichtblitze und Klang aus mehreren Richtungen erzeugen flüchtige, verzerrte Eindrücke der umgebenden Architektur.
Description DE: PULS erkundet die Grenzen und Eigenheiten unserer Wahrnehmung durch den Einsatz sensorischer Extreme. Aufblitzendes Licht, völlige Dunkelheit und kurze audiovisuelle Impulse, die sich in Frequenzen zwischen Rhythmus und Ton wiederholen, manipulieren unser Zeit- und Raumempfinden. Die Installation überwältigt uns, erzeugt Illusionen, zwingt uns, die Perspektive zu wechseln oder versetzt uns sogar in einen veränderten Bewusstseinszustand.

Web Preview Text EN: Join us at the Creative Coding Open House, a friendly community space hosted by members of the vvvv, Processing, p5.js, Clinic for Open Source Arts (COSA) and other creative coding communities where you can start and extend your journey as a creative coder!
Description EN:
Join us at the Creative Coding Open House, a friendly community space within the Ars Electronica Festival. It is hosted by members of the vvvv, Processing, p5.js, Clinic for Open Source Arts (COSA) and other creative coding communities.

Think of it as a cosy living room where artists, designers, educators, students, researchers and anyone curious about code-based creative practices can drop in, share their work, learn from others or simply spend some time with likeminded folks exploring the creative possibilities of code.
One of the things we would like to explore is how different creative coding communities can learn from one another. Our goal is to make space for conversations that might not happen otherwise.
We will have some scheduled activities, but we are also leaving plenty of room for participation. If you would like to propose an activity, join us at: https://matrix.to/#/#ccoh-matrix.org.

We will be open 13:00-18:00 during the festival and have a different focus each day:

WED 9.9. – Creative Coding Open House – Stop by to find out what Creative coding is and how you can get started.

THU 10.9. – Creative Coding Buffet – Come and try different tools and find something new!

FRI 11.9. – Contributing to Open Source – Learn how to get engaged as a community member and support your favorite tools, new and old!

SAT 12.9. – Discover vvvv – learn to code with nodes!

SUN 13.9. – Processing Community Day – learn and build with Processing, p5.js and more!
